nba.shot_profile.label: Shot location/profile (rim/mid/3), zone defense allowed
nba.shot_profile.mechanism: A team's or player's distribution of attempts by zone and the opponent's zone defense determine expected efficiency and the mix of points, rebounds and threes.
nba.shot_profile.rationale: Expected points per shot depends on shot zone, and defenses concede zones in a stable way (drop teams give mid-range, switching gives threes). For props it sets 3PA and rim-attack volume; for totals it sets efficiency. Subtle: opponent adjustment requires matching offense zone frequency with defense zone frequency allowed (not simply averaging).
nba.shot_profile.measurement: Zone frequencies and FG% by zone for offense and defense (restricted area, paint, mid, corner 3, above-break 3); expected points per attempt using matchup-weighted frequencies; shrink FG% by zone to league mean.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) shotchartdetail, leaguedashteamshotlocations
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.three_volume.label: 3PA rate, catch-and-shoot share, 3P% shrinkage and opponent 3PA allowed
nba.three_volume.mechanism: Threes made equal attempts times make probability; attempts are driven by role, minutes and opponent scheme, and make% must be shrunk heavily.
nba.three_volume.rationale: A player's 3PA per minute is much more stable than 3P%; make% over a season reverts toward career and shot-quality-based expectation. Opponent 3PA allowed and pace/spacing change attempt volume. Subtle: attempts are overdispersed (game-to-game volume varies), so a binomial with fixed attempts understates variance.
nba.three_volume.measurement: 3PA per 36 minutes with exponential weights (half-life 20 games) shrunk to the player's prior-season rate with k=20 games; catch-and-shoot share from tracking splits when available; attempt count model = negative binomial with mean = 3PA/36 x projected minutes/36 x opponent index (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 / league mean, 20-game half-life) and dispersion estimated on 3 seasons. 3P% is not computed here; use nba.three_make_by_openness_prior. Output expected 3PA, sd and P(3PA >= k). As-of: games before tip.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerptshot / shotchartdetail
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

sources.name: nba_api / stats.nba.com (leaguegamelog, boxscoretraditionalv2, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashptdefend)

nba.player_shooting_regression.label: Player shooting luck vs expectation (3P%, FG%, FT%)
nba.player_shooting_regression.mechanism: Hot or cold stretches in 3P%/FG%/FT% mostly regress to a player's shot-quality-adjusted talent, so recent form overstates the next game's expected efficiency.
nba.player_shooting_regression.rationale: Markets and naive models overweight recent hot shooting; true talent is better estimated by priors from career, volume and shot openness. FT% stabilizes faster than 3P%. Subtle: real changes (mechanics, injury recovery, role) exist, so shrinkage weight should depend on sample size and change signals.
nba.player_shooting_regression.measurement: Beta-binomial shrinkage with prior mean = career/role expectation and prior strength set empirically per stat (3P ~ 300-500 att, FT ~ 100-150 att); compare recent vs shrunk estimate; include shot-quality (openness) adjustment.
free_sources: PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)
raw_data: shotchartdetail shot-level rows (zone, action type, result)

sources.name: nba_api / stats.nba.com (leaguegamelog, boxscoretraditionalv2, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashptdefend)

nba.steal_block_rates.label: Steals/blocks per minute, opponent turnover and rim-attempt rates
nba.steal_block_rates.mechanism: Steals and blocks are low-count events driven by per-minute skill, minutes, and the opponent's turnover and rim-attempt propensities.
nba.steal_block_rates.rationale: Per-minute rates are fairly stable for steals/blocks, and opponent turnover rate (esp. live-ball turnovers) and rim attempts per possession modulate them. Their low-count Poisson nature means strike lines at 0.5 and 1.5 are dominated by dispersion modeling. Subtle: official-scorer credit (esp. blocks and steals) varies by arena.
nba.steal_block_rates.measurement: Per-36 steals/blocks (EWMA, shrink with Gamma-Poisson prior), opponent TOV% and live-ball TOV per 100, opponent rim FGA per 100, matchup-adjusted; minutes distribution to produce count distribution.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashplayerstats, hustlestats

nba.turnover_pressure.label: Turnover propensity and opponent pressure (turnovers per touch, deflections)
nba.turnover_pressure.mechanism: Turnovers scale with ball-handling load and are raised by opponent pressure, deflections and steal rates.
nba.turnover_pressure.rationale: Turnover props depend on usage/ball handling as well as opponent live-ball pressure; high-assist creators also turn the ball over more. Subtle: turnover counts correlate with assists and minutes, so independent modeling misprices combos and conditional stats; scorer judgments (bad pass vs lost ball) are noisy.
nba.turnover_pressure.measurement: TOV per 100 touches/possessions used, bad-pass vs lost-ball split; opponent forced TOV% and deflections per 100; ball-handler pressure ratio; negative binomial with minutes.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) hustlestats, leaguedashptstats

nba.ft_attempts.label: Free-throw attempt rate and FT% (for FT-made props), opponent foul-rate allowed
nba.ft_attempts.mechanism: Free throws made equal attempts (drives, post play, foul-drawing, and late-game fouling) times FT%.
nba.ft_attempts.rationale: FTA/FGA is a stable per-player trait; FT% has a high true-talent component but moderate sampling noise. Late-game intentional fouls raise attempts for the leading team's ball handlers and make FT props sensitive to game script. Subtle: FT made props at 0.5/1.5/2.5 depend heavily on minutes and referees; overdispersed.
nba.ft_attempts.measurement: FTA per 36 and per FGA (EWMA), FT% shrunk with Beta prior; opponent FTA allowed per 100 relative to league; crew foul index; game script factor for last-2-minute fouling.

nba.foul_rates.label: Personal fouls per minute, foul-out and foul-trouble minute loss
nba.foul_rates.mechanism: Players with high foul rates face early-foul benching and foul-outs that cut minutes and counting stats, especially bigs against foul-drawing offenses.
nba.foul_rates.rationale: Foul trouble truncates minutes non-linearly and produces left-tail outcomes in over/under props; it is predictable in terms of baseline (PF per 36) and opponent (drawn fouls, big-vs-big matchups) but not realized. Subtle: coaches differ in how early they bench players with 2 fouls in the first half; crew effect interacts.
nba.foul_rates.measurement: PF per 36, P(2 fouls in Q1/first half) and P(foul-out) from game logs; minutes lost distribution in foul-trouble games; opponent drawn-foul rate; crew foul index; coach rule for early fouls.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay

nba.scorer_bias.label: Official scorer/arena stat-credit bias (assists, steals, blocks, rebounds)
nba.scorer_bias.mechanism: Statistics like assists, blocks and steals are subjective official-scorer judgments, and arena-level tendencies (home scorer) can shift counts systematically.
nba.scorer_bias.rationale: If home arenas credit more assists/blocks/steals to the home team, prop outcomes depend on venue and the scorer culture; the effect can be measured as arena-level residual in stat/min controlling for team and opponent. It is a hypothesis, probably small, and needs panel data over multiple seasons. Subtle: team-composition confounds (a team always plays at its own arena), so use opponent-team residuals at the same venue.
nba.scorer_bias.measurement: Per team-game (3 seasons, regular season), compute AST, STL, BLK per 100 possessions for each side. Fit a mixed model y = team_off + opp_def + venue + home x venue + error, with team_off and opp_def random intercepts (shrunk) and venue random effect identified by visiting teams' deviation from their own road average at that arena; report the venue effect in per-100 units with a posterior sd, shrinking to zero with a prior sd estimated by cross-validation (leave-one-season-out). Output a venue adjustment only if its out-of-sample reduction in stat-count error is positive; otherwise zero. As-of: games before tip; arenas that changed in the window are split.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) team game logs by arena
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)
raw_data: player-game assists, steals, blocks, rebounds with minutes

sources.name: nba_api / stats.nba.com (leaguegamelog, boxscoretraditionalv2, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashptdefend)

nba.tip_first_shot.label: Tip-off winner tendencies and first-shot/first-basket usage
nba.tip_first_shot.mechanism: The tip winner and opening play design determine who takes the first shot, and with starters fixed, first-shot share dominates first-basket probability.
nba.tip_first_shot.rationale: First-basket markets depend on tip winner probability (center vertical, ~50/50 with small edges), team's opening set plays (who the first shot is designed for), and shooter conversion on the first attempt. Subtle: very low base rates mean even small modeling errors matter; opening play patterns change after injuries/new starters.
nba.tip_first_shot.measurement: From play-by-play: first possession shot-taker distribution by starter lineup, jump-ball winner rates by center matchup, opening-play type (ATO), first FGA/first FGM share per player; EWMA with lineup conditioning.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.first_basket_share.label: First-basket history by team and player (first FGM share, first possession usage)
nba.first_basket_share.mechanism: The share of games where a player scores the team's first basket reflects set-play design and usage on the opening possessions.
nba.first_basket_share.rationale: Opening possessions differ from average possessions (set plays for specific scorers, centers off tip). Rates are small and sample-limited; they must be shrunk to usage-based priors. Also depends on which team scores first, linking to tip and defense. Subtle: starter changes reshape the distribution.
nba.first_basket_share.measurement: Per player: P(first team basket) and P(first game basket) from last 1-2 seasons, shrunk toward usage-share prior; condition on lineup identity; combine with P(team scores first) and P(tip).
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial) playbyplay
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.q_scoring.label: Historical scoring by quarter/half, first-quarter pace and starter minutes
nba.q_scoring.mechanism: Period totals/margins depend on starter minutes in that period, pace and efficiency conditional on lineup, and game state in later periods.
nba.q_scoring.rationale: Q1 is dominated by starters (lineups known pregame), Q2 mixes benches and Q4 is state-dependent (garbage time, close-game fouls). First-half share of game total differs by team (slow starters, halftime adjustments). Subtle: period totals have higher relative variance than game totals and key lattice effects.
nba.q_scoring.measurement: Per team: points scored/allowed by quarter and half, adjusted for opponent and lineup; first-half share of game points; variance by period; calibrate to period lines vs actual.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboard by period (boxscoretraditional by period)
cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)

nba.bench_scoring.label: Bench scoring share and rotation depth by team
nba.bench_scoring.mechanism: Bench points depend on how many players the coach plays, the quality of reserves and the starters' minutes load.
nba.bench_scoring.rationale: Bench points markets/tie-ins depend on injuries to starters (promotes bench players into starter role and reduces the 'bench' denominator), blowout minutes, and rotation depth. Subtle: definition of bench is 'did not start', so lineup changes alter the market outcome mechanically.
nba.bench_scoring.measurement: Team bench points per game by opponent/spread bucket, rotation depth (players over 10 minutes), starters' minute shares; adjust for who starts tonight.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamdashboardbygeneralsplits (starters vs bench)

nba.stat_dist.label: Per-stat count distributions (overdispersion, correlation)
nba.stat_dist.mechanism: Player stat counts are overdispersed relative to Poisson because minutes, role and game state vary; the correct distribution shape determines tail probabilities across rungs.
nba.stat_dist.rationale: Over/under probabilities at a line require the whole distribution: minutes mixture, negative binomial or zero-inflated forms, and ceiling/floor effects (blowout minutes). Stat correlations within a game (pts, ast, tov) matter for combos. Subtle: fitting only a mean from a line and a normal sd mis-prices tails at 25+, 30+ rungs.
nba.stat_dist.measurement: Fit count models (NB, mixtures over minutes scenarios) per player-stat with covariates; check dispersion, rung calibration; estimate correlation matrix of stats given minutes.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game logs
hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.combo_covariance.label: Covariance between stat components in combos (PRA, PR, PA, RA)
nba.combo_covariance.mechanism: Combined-stat markets sum correlated components: minutes create positive covariance, while role tradeoffs and game scripts can create negative covariance.
nba.combo_covariance.rationale: Variance of PRA is not the sum of component variances; positive correlation via minutes widens the tails, while negative correlation (usage vs assist focus) narrows them. Market makers often price combos from component lines, leaving mismatches. Subtle: covariance depends on role (center vs guard) and game script.
nba.combo_covariance.measurement: Estimate within-game covariance matrix (pts, reb, ast) per player conditional on minutes; simulate joint outcomes; compare implied combo distribution with sum of marginal rungs.
free_sources: hoopR / sportsdataverse (free R/Python pull of ESPN and NBA data)

nba.milestone_rates.label: Double-double/triple-double base rates and threshold proximity
nba.milestone_rates.mechanism: DD/TD are binary conjunctions of several count thresholds, so their probability depends on the joint distribution and proximity of each component to 10.
nba.milestone_rates.rationale: A player whose average assists are 7 and rebounds 11 has a double-double probability that is a product-like function of both stats' distribution; triple doubles are rare and depend on minutes and teammate shot-making. Subtle: coaches and scripts (blowouts) cut the tail; stat-padding behavior in last minutes is plausible but small.
nba.milestone_rates.measurement: Joint simulation from stat distributions per player, calibrated against historical DD/TD rates by minute bucket and third-stat distribution; compute P(any 2 of 3 >= 10).
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) game logs/DD-TD logs

nba.tracking.label: Tracking data (speed, defender distance, rim protection)
nba.tracking.mechanism: Tracking-derived measures (shot defender distance, rim deterrence, speed, drives) describe shot quality and defensive impact beyond box scores.
nba.tracking.rationale: Contested-vs-open breakdowns separate shooting skill from shot quality and expose rim-protection differences that box scores miss. Public access is partial and endpoints are rate-limited; many fine-grained tracking fields are only available as aggregates. Subtle: tracking-based tags change definitions over seasons, so historical comparability needs checking.
nba.tracking.measurement: Aggregate: shots by defender distance and zone, rim-defense DFG% at the rim, drives per game, speed/distance, hustle stats; use as shrunk, opponent-adjusted covariates into shot-quality and rebound models.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) leaguedashptstats, leaguedashptdefend, leaguehustlestatsplayer
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.onoff.label: On/off and lineup combination efficiency
nba.onoff.mechanism: Lineup- and player-level on/off efficiency estimates the effect of specific absences/combos on team ratings, usually after shrinkage.
nba.onoff.rationale: On/off is the raw material for availability-adjusted ratings and lineup adjustments but is noisy and confounded by teammates and opponent quality; combinations of 5-man units have tiny samples. Subtle: use regularized estimates (RAPM) and only trust combos with large minutes.
nba.onoff.measurement: On/off net rating with opponent adjustments and shrinkage; lineup-level net ratings with minutes threshold; with/without splits for key teammates.
free_sources: nba_api / stats.nba.com (free, undocumented, rate-limited) teamplayeronoffdetails, teamdashlineups
PBPStats.com (free tier: on/off, lineup, possession-level splits)

nba.standings_sim.label: Season/playoff simulation, tiebreakers, play-in
nba.standings_sim.mechanism: A Monte Carlo of the remaining schedule using team ratings, injuries and tiebreakers produces probabilities for seeds, playoffs, play-in, divisions and conference outcomes.
nba.standings_sim.rationale: Season futures are determined by the full distribution of outcomes including tiebreaker rules (head-to-head, division record, conference record), the play-in tournament and the Cup effect on the schedule; simple win-total extrapolation misses boundary effects near seed lines. Subtle: rating uncertainty must be sampled across sims, not fixed, otherwise tails are overconfident.
nba.standings_sim.measurement: Single shared regular-season path simulation for every season-level archetype: 20,000 seasons of the remaining schedule, game by game in date order, from team ratings with posterior uncertainty (common within a season draw), home advantage, rest and injury scenarios; store each path's game-level results so season_futures_team (win totals, records, seeds, divisions via nba.tiebreak_ledger, play-in) and season_stat_markets (streaks via nba.team_win_streak_hazard and nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model, last unbeaten) read the same draws; output seed pmf and series inputs to nba.title_path. As-of: nightly after final scores.

nba.award_stats.label: Award-candidate production, voting narrative
nba.award_stats.mechanism: Award outcomes depend on production, team success, availability and media narrative; the voting process itself (ballot structure) shapes outcomes.
nba.award_stats.rationale: Historical voters favor high-volume scoring or advanced metrics depending on award, team seed and games played; modeling voting shares requires features like PER/BPM/win shares, team record, games played, narrative and rank in ballots. Subtle: the 65-game eligibility minimum and late-season injuries heavily alter finalists.
nba.award_stats.measurement: Per candidate: per-game stats, BPM/VORP/win shares, team win%, games played, minutes; historical vote-share regression by award; narrative proxies (odds, media consensus).
free_sources: Basketball-Reference (free; polite scraping, rate-limited) award voting history and advanced stats

nba.games_played_eligibility.label: Award/ranking eligibility rules (65-game minimum, minutes/stat thresholds)
nba.games_played_eligibility.mechanism: Eligibility thresholds convert missed games into a hard cutoff that determines whether a player can win or make an All-NBA team.
nba.games_played_eligibility.rationale: A candidate on pace to miss the games threshold has a lower probability of award or selection regardless of production; teams may manage minutes to preserve eligibility or fail. Rules have specific exceptions (partial games, appeals) and changes between seasons, which must be read from official rules text.
nba.games_played_eligibility.measurement: Per award, encode the season's governing rule from the league criteria: 65-game minimum (20+ minutes in 63, 15-20 minutes allowed in two) for MVP, DPOY, Most Improved, All-NBA and All-Defensive (verified 2025-26, no change reported for 2026-27); none for ROY, Sixth Man, All-Rookie; flag Clutch as unconfirmed. Track counting games and games remaining vs the threshold via nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger, add the Extraordinary Circumstances challenge branch from nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model, and flag candidates within 5 games of the line.
free_sources: NBA official award eligibility rules (nba.com/official, free)

nba.voting_narrative.label: Media narrative, voter composition and ballot dynamics
nba.voting_narrative.mechanism: Voting for awards and selections reflects narrative (momentum, team success, positional balance) and ballot structure, not only statistics.
nba.voting_narrative.rationale: Narrative signals can be partly measured from betting market prices, media rankings, and award-tracker ladders; position constraints in All-NBA balloting (guard/forward/center) affect selection. Subtle: narrative-based features have small samples and are prone to overfit.
nba.voting_narrative.measurement: Ladder-ranking data (media award trackers), position-balloting rules, historical gaps between production rank and voting rank; use ordinal logit by award.
free_sources: ESPN/other media award trackers (free articles; no API)

nba.title_path.label: Playoff bracket path, matchup and home-court structure
nba.title_path.mechanism: Series winner and title probabilities depend on the bracket path (seed, opponent strength, home-court) and matchup-specific adjustments.
nba.title_path.rationale: Title odds are the product of series-win probabilities along a path that depends on which seed you are, who you face and the rest/injury states. A given team's path difficulty can differ substantially even for equal rating. Subtle: series outcomes are correlated through injuries to key players across rounds.
nba.title_path.measurement: Shared playoff bracket simulation for the bracket-level consumers attached to it (season_futures_team, series_and_cup, player_milestones for KXNBAPLAYOFF3D, the playoff single-game points archetype, awards_draft and parlay_combo): 50,000 draws; seeds from nba.standings_sim paths, play-in from nba.play_in_path_model, each series simulated game by game with the per-series kernel of nba.series_length_distribution (p_g from playoff ratings, 2-2-1-1-1 home court, injury state, series dependence); store per-path series lengths, venues and advancement so these consumers read the same draws. Single-series contracts whose matchup is already set (series cumulative points, per-series length markets) use the kernel directly; it equals title_path's conditional for that series. Output P(reach round r), P(title), opponents and games played per team. As-of: nightly.

sources.name: cdn.nba.com liveData and static schedule JSON
Derived from own-model ratings and simulation

nba.series_model.label: Best-of-seven series model (home-court, game-to-game correlation, adjustments)
nba.series_model.mechanism: Series win and game-count probabilities derive from per-game win probabilities with home pattern; correlated injuries and adjustments change the distribution.
nba.series_model.rationale: A simple independent binomial overstates sweeps vs actual; playoff rotations shorten, pace slows, and stars play more minutes, shifting the effective team rating. Series props (sweep, exact games, player series totals) need game-level scoring simulations. Subtle: in-series injuries and coaching adjustments create positive correlation between games.
nba.series_model.measurement: Per-game win p from playoff-adjusted ratings with home advantage; sample game-to-game correlation parameter; adapt rating after injuries; compute pmf of series length and winner.

sources.name: nba_api / stats.nba.com (leaguegamelog, boxscoretraditionalv2, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashptdefend)

nba.playoff_rotation.label: Playoff rotation tightening and minutes inflation
nba.playoff_rotation.mechanism: Playoff games feature shorter rotations and higher starter minutes, changing player props and team-level ratings relative to the regular season.
nba.playoff_rotation.rationale: Stars play several more minutes per game and bench depth matters less; regular-season minutes baselines understate playoff volume for starters and overstate bench contributions. Subtle: the effect varies by round and by series pace/blowout probability.
nba.playoff_rotation.measurement: For each player-season with >=20 regular-season games and a playoff series, compute the ratio r = playoff minutes per game / regular-season minutes per game (regular season through the last 20 games to avoid rest-game noise), pooled by role bucket (top-3 minutes, other starters, rotation, bench) and round, 2010-present, with shrinkage of player r to the bucket mean at k=8 playoff games. Team rotation depth = number of players averaging >=12 minutes in the series, versus regular season. Output for each player: expected playoff minutes = projected regular-season minutes x r_bucket,round with sd, conditioned on series pace and blowout probability from own-model margin. As-of: games before tip; regular-season baseline fixed at season end.
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData JSON (boxscore, playbyplay, odds; free, unofficial)
raw_data: player-game minutes regular season and playoffs, starter flag

sources.name: nba_api / stats.nba.com (leaguegamelog, boxscoretraditionalv2, playbyplayv3, shotchartdetail, leaguedashptdefend)

nba.cup_format.label: NBA Cup group/knockout structure and tiebreakers
nba.cup_format.mechanism: Cup outcomes depend on group-stage point-differential tiebreakers, wildcard rules and single-elimination knockout games hosted by the higher seed through the semifinal, with a neutral-site final (2026-27: Hinkle Fieldhouse).
nba.cup_format.rationale: Group-stage point differential makes blowout margins matter in Cup games, and group games count in the regular-season standings while the final does not; rest decisions and star availability vary relative to regular-season games. In 2026-27 the quarterfinals and semifinals are home games for the higher seed and only the final is neutral, so seeding carries home court. Rules change by season and must be re-read from official documentation.
nba.cup_format.measurement: 2026-27 format (verified NBA.com/ESPN): six groups of five, group winners plus one wild card per conference (best non-winner, wild-card ties start at point differential) seeded 1-4 per conference; quarterfinals 1v4 and 2v3 hosted by the higher seed; semifinals at the higher seed's arena (Dec 8-9); final neutral at Hinkle Fieldhouse, Indianapolis (Dec 11). Enumerate remaining group games with margin simulation and the group tiebreak order (nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state), then knockout games with home court for the higher seed through the semifinal and none in the final; Cup final excluded from regular-season stats.

sources.name: NBA.com Emirates NBA Cup rules and standings
sources.note: tiebreak order is versioned by season

nba.sos_remaining.label: Remaining schedule strength and rest structure
nba.sos_remaining.mechanism: The strength, location and rest pattern of remaining opponents modulate expected wins, seeds and playoff probability.
nba.sos_remaining.rationale: Equal-rating teams with different remaining schedules have different expected finishes; back-to-back and road-heavy stretches affect both rating and injury risk. Subtle: strength must be measured with current availability-adjusted ratings, not preseason.
nba.sos_remaining.measurement: Sum expected win probabilities for remaining games with home, rest, and opponent availability-adjusted ratings; difference vs baseline schedule.

nba.injury_risk_season.label: Season-level availability risk (games missed expectations, injury history)
nba.injury_risk_season.mechanism: Expected games missed by key players changes season win totals, seed, awards and futures via lost minutes.
nba.injury_risk_season.rationale: Players with long injury histories, age and heavy minutes miss more games; season markets (wins, stat leaders, awards) are exposed. Subtle: injury events are rare/high-impact and fat-tailed; the model needs a mixture with a small probability of season-ending absence.
nba.injury_risk_season.measurement: Hazard model: games missed per season by age, position, prior injury, minutes; simulate availability; propagate through minutes to team rating and player stat totals.
free_sources: Spotrac / RealGM / Pro Sports Transactions (free tiers: contracts, cap, transactions) (injury/transactions history)
NBA official injury report PDF (official.nba.com, free; updates through the day before and day of game)

nba.season_stat_pace.label: Season-to-date pace and per-game stat trajectory for leaders
nba.season_stat_pace.mechanism: Season stat leader and streak markets depend on current totals, per-game rates, minutes and games remaining, with variance from injuries.
nba.season_stat_pace.rationale: A leader market is a race between players' cumulative totals; the gap and rate difference with remaining games define probability, with injury/rest scenarios central. Subtle: per-game average leaderboards have minimum games rules that interact with load management.
nba.season_stat_pace.measurement: Current totals + projected per-game rates x expected games (availability distribution) for each candidate; simulate race; check rule definitions (per-game vs total, minimum games).

nba.draft_board.label: Draft order, lottery odds and consensus prospect ranking
nba.draft_board.mechanism: Draft markets depend on lottery outcomes (odds table), team needs and consensus big boards/mock drafts.
nba.draft_board.rationale: Pick position and consensus ranking jointly drive who is selected; lottery odds are fixed by the standings and rules; mock draft consensus moves in the final days with workouts and team intel. Subtle: draft-night trades change order, and the market may lead the public mocks.
nba.draft_board.measurement: Lottery odds from standings and rules, consensus rank aggregated across public big boards/mocks, rank volatility near draft, trade-rumor flags.
free_sources: Public mock-draft aggregators (e.g. Tankathon, free web)

nba.transaction_flow.label: Transaction-flow signals (rumors, cap/apron constraints, trade rules)
nba.transaction_flow.mechanism: Trades, signings and waivers are constrained by cap rules, apron limits, roster spots and timelines; rumors from reliable reporters move probability.
nba.transaction_flow.rationale: Whether a player is traded or signed depends on contract status, salary-matching constraints, roster counts, deadline dates and team context; an event market's probability is the product of rule feasibility and reporting. Subtle: reporter reliability and wording (talks vs agreed) differ greatly, and rule details come from the CBA.
nba.transaction_flow.measurement: Compile cap sheet, apron and roster constraints, trade deadline dates, reported-talks timeline; base rates of rumored deals completing by reporter and wording.

nba.org_stability.label: Coach/front-office stability (record vs expectation, tenure, ownership)

nba.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rates for NBA off-court events
nba.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Franchise, rule and personnel events occur at historical frequencies tied to the calendar.
nba.offfield_base_rate.rationale: These contracts cannot be modelled from game data; the honest prior is the frequency of the event class by calendar window, updated by dated reporting. Subtle: markets often over-price dramatic events relative to base rates.
nba.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Count events of the class per season and calendar window from news archives and league announcements; shrink with an empirical-Bayes prior; record the announcement timestamp.

nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.label: Qualifying-games ledger (65 games with 20+ minutes) and slack
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.mechanism: The award eligibility count is a deterministic ledger that only the league's definition of a qualifying game updates; slack to the line plus injury hazard gives the probability of staying eligible.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.rationale: The existing eligibility input restates the rule but not the arithmetic; a player at 50 qualifying games with 20 left has a very different conditional risk from one at 62 with a nagging injury, and games of 15-20 minutes count only in a small allowance.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.measurement: Per player: counting games = games with minutes >= 20, plus up to 2 games with 15-20 minutes (verified 2025-26 rule: 20+ minutes in at least 63 of the 65 games, 15+ in the other two); slack = games_remaining - (65 - counting); P(ledger) = P(missed or sub-threshold games among remaining <= slack) under a Poisson-binomial with per-game miss probability = player-season availability rate shrunk with k=20 games toward the position prior, updated nightly after the 6pm ET injury report; P(eligible) = P(ledger) + (1 - P(ledger)) x P(appeal granted) from nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model. As-of: last completed game. Governed awards (verified): MVP, DPOY, Most Improved, All-NBA, All-Defensive; ROY, Sixth Man and All-Rookie exempt; not applied to monthly awards, Coach/Executive of the Year, All-Star or draft markets; Clutch POY coverage unconfirmed (flag).

nba.award_role_filters.label: Award-specific candidate filters (bench-start ratio, rookie status, clutch minimum)
nba.award_role_filters.mechanism: Each award has a definitional filter (Sixth Man must come off the bench in more games than he starts, ROY needs rookie status, Clutch POY needs clutch minutes/games, MIP needs improvement versus prior year) that decides who is in the candidate set.
nba.award_role_filters.rationale: A single input called award_stats treats all awards alike, but the candidate set is built by the filter first; a starter promoted mid-season loses Sixth Man eligibility, and a rookie who played overseas may or may not be a rookie.
nba.award_role_filters.measurement: Per award and as-of date compute boolean eligibility from the league definition stored per season: Sixth Man = games_off_bench > games_started (Sixth Man is exempt from the 65-game rule, verified 2025-26); ROY = first-year player on the league rookie list (exempt); Clutch POY = clutch minutes (last 5 minutes, margin within 5) >= the published minimum for that season (read from rules text, else 25th percentile of the prior season). Candidates then ranked by the stat the award names: clutch net points per 100 clutch possessions, BPM delta vs prior season (MIP, min 500 minutes both seasons), DWS per 36 (DPOY), each shrunk to season value with prior weight 10 games. nba.expectation_overperformance.label: Wins minus preseason expectation (own, non-market)
nba.expectation_overperformance.mechanism: Coach, Executive, MIP and team-driven awards reward results above what the roster implied before the season, so voters compare wins to a preseason baseline.
nba.expectation_overperformance.rationale: Total wins alone ranks the best teams first, but Coach of the Year goes to the largest positive surprise; the baseline must be an own rating-based preseason projection and not a sportsbook win total to avoid a market-derived input.
nba.expectation_overperformance.measurement: exp_wins_pre = 82 * pythagorean win% with exponent 14 applied to the own preseason points scored/allowed per game, where the preseason net rating is the minutes-weighted sum over the projected rotation of player impact (weight 0.6 last-season, 0.4 career, then regressed 30% to the league mean). On the as-of date, projected wins = wins_to_date + (82 - GP) * win% from the current own rating (nba.ratings, not the preseason value). surprise = (wins_to_date - exp_wins_pre*GP/82) / 6 expressed in wins; units = standard deviations; as-of = last completed game.

nba.allnba_points_ladder.label: All-NBA points ladder and cut-line margins (positionless)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.mechanism: All-NBA teams are three five-player cut lines on a single points ranking (5/3/1 for first/second/third team); a candidate's probabilities across team markets are nested.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.rationale: Candidates with similar profiles split votes and a margin of a few points moves a player between teams; ballots are positionless since 2023-24, so the old guard/forward/center constraints no longer bind and should not be modelled.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.measurement: Per candidate on as-of date compute score_i = 0.5*z(BPM, minutes-weighted, min 1,500 min) + 0.3*z(team win% projected to season end) + 0.2*z(points per game), restricted to players meeting the 65-game/20-minute eligibility ledger (nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger). Simulate 100 ballots: each voter perturbs score_i by Gaussian noise with sd fitted so simulated vote-share dispersion matches 2023-25 published ballots (all-time seasons used only for the ballot-size prior), ranks the top 15, assigns 5/3/1 points to the three 5-man teams and ranks by total points. Output P(rank<=5), P(rank<=10), P(rank<=15) with sums of 5, 10, 15, nightly.

nba.prospect_board_dispersion.label: Prospect consensus rank and cross-board dispersion
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.mechanism: Selection at slot N is a categorical outcome over the top prospects; disagreement across public boards and team-specific mocks signals entropy and information arrival.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.rationale: A single consensus rank hides that the second pick is nearly deterministic in some drafts and a coin flip among four prospects in others; measuring dispersion is the correct uncertainty input.
nba.prospect_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect: mean and sd of rank across at least 6 boards (ESPN, The Athletic, Tankathon, NBADraft.net, Bleacher Report, Yahoo) with weights proportional to each source's historical rank-error; convert to P(selected at slot k) by a Plackett-Luce model fit on 2015-2025 drafts; update after each workout/medical report with 48h half-life.

nba.monthly_window_schedule.label: Games-in-window and schedule for monthly awards
nba.monthly_window_schedule.mechanism: Monthly player/rookie/coach/defender awards depend on games played inside the window, with fewer games for a candidate lowering his total counting stats and chance of an extreme month.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.rationale: Players on teams with 12 games in the window versus 16 have different expected volume; the conference split of winners and ties matters for pro-rata payout.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.measurement: Per candidate (conference): expected points per game over the window = 10-game shrunk per-game mean (prior weight 10 games toward season mean) times games in window from the schedule; team wins expected from own ratings. Score_i = 0.5*z(PPG) + 0.3*z(team win% in window, expected) + 0.2*z(TS% or BPM), z computed over the conference candidate pool (top 30 by minutes). P(win) = softmax(Score_i / T) with temperature T and the three weights fitted by conditional logit on 10 seasons of monthly Player-of-the-Month winners; as-of date = day before window close.

nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.label: All-Star starter composite (fan 50% / player 25% / media 25%), positionless top five per conference
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.mechanism: Starters are the five best weighted-average ranks per conference without regard to position (2026 rules): each candidate's rank in the fan, current-player and media votes is combined 50/25/25 and the fan vote breaks composite ties.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.rationale: KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR are not decided by the ballot of about 100 media voters in stage s4: the fan vote carries half the weight, is public in early-return snapshots during the voting window, and depends on market size and social following, while the player and media votes follow production. Since 2026 the five starters per conference are chosen without regard to position, so displacement is conference-wide and then by the 16 US / 8 international minimum, not between guard and frontcourt slots.
nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite.measurement: For each candidate and conference compute composite = 0.50 x fan_rank + 0.25 x player_rank + 0.25 x media_rank over all positions (verified for 2026: positionless, fan vote breaks ties, as with Wembanyama over Edwards in the West); fan_rank at close = last published early-return rank plus a random-walk adjustment scaled by the share of voting window remaining (step variance from past return snapshots), prior from last year's final fan rank, market size and social following; player and media ranks from the production rank in nba.award_stats with beta noise from past ballot-vs-stat rank gaps; starters = five lowest composites per conference; 10,000 draws, P(starter) per candidate. Use the 2027 rules when announced; until then the 2026 rules apply.

nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.label: All-Star reserve selection by coaches (7 per conference, positionless) and Commissioner replacements
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.mechanism: After starters are fixed, each conference's head coaches vote seven reserves without regard to position (not their own players), the Commissioner names injury replacements and, under the USA-vs-World format, adds players to meet the 16 US / 8 international minimum.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.rationale: KXNBAALLSTARS and KXNBAALLSTAR settle on the full roster, so reserve probability matters as much as starter probability; coaches value team record and recent play more than fan appeal, and an injured selectee is replaced by a commissioner choice that is hard to forecast.
nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.measurement: For each non-starter candidate: coach-vote score = z-score of production rank (nba.award_stats) plus team win% rank, calibrated by logistic regression on 10 seasons of reserve selections with conference strata only (positionless since 2026; earlier seasons had position slots, so fit with a pre/post-2026 indicator); P(reserve) = P(rank among the 7 conference reserve slots after starters are removed) via 10,000 draws conditional on the starter simulation; then apply the nationality minimum from nba.allstar_nationality_quota; injury replacement = P(a selectee is injured) x P(Commissioner picks the next-ranked player of the same conference).

nba.voter_signal_proxy.label: Observable voter-signal proxy: public media ladders, prior-win count and repeat-winner penalty
nba.voter_signal_proxy.mechanism: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative and voter-fatigue notion with observables: average rank in published media award ladders and straw polls, the number of consecutive prior wins, and the candidate's first-place share in the previous two seasons.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.rationale: nba.voting_narrative is audited WEAK because it is not measurable as defined, yet narrative and fatigue are the only drivers of the vote beyond production and team success; a proxy built from public ladders and past ballots gives them a measurable form without using any market price.
nba.voter_signal_proxy.measurement: For each candidate and award: mean rank over the last 4 published media ladders (NBA.com ladder, ESPN straw poll; unranked = 6th) with weights 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 newest first; repeat_penalty = number of consecutive prior wins; prior_share = first-place vote share in the last two seasons (0 if not a finalist); fit a conditional-logit ballot model on 2000-2026 winners with these three features plus production rank and seed, shrinking coefficients with a ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out.

nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture weights and component rates
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: Minutes are a mixture of regimes (blowout truncation, normal, foul-limited, OT, restricted) whose weights depend on game state and each regime has different per-minute stat rates.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing nba.minutes is a point projection that hides the multimodality; for a threshold sum, P(S>=25) is driven by the weight of the full-minutes regime, not by the mean minutes.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: From 3+ seasons of play-by-play, classify each player-game into regimes by the minutes and score margin (blowout: |margin|>=18 with 4th-quarter minutes<8; foul-limited: >=4 fouls by Q3; OT; restriction: coach-announced); fit regime weights as a multinomial logit of (own-model spread, rest, opponent pace, bench depth) with ridge shrinkage; each regime's stat-per-minute rates estimated with 15-game half-life and a prior from players of the same role; as-of timestamp = last injury report vintage.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).

nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.label: Lineup-conditional per-100 rates for points, rebounds and assists
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.mechanism: The three components move differently when teammates are on or off court: a creator off court raises the player's usage and assists, a big off court raises rebounds.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.rationale: Season-average per-minute rates blur lineup regimes, and teammate_absence_shift is a single directional signal; separate rates per partner set are needed for a sum that moves in offsetting directions.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.measurement: Per player: per-100-possession PTS, REB, AST computed by on-court partner set (with/without each of the top-3 teammates by minutes), minimum 300 possessions per cell, empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the player's overall rate with k=400 possessions; applied to tonight's expected lineup from the confirmed or projected starters; as-of = latest lineup information.

nba.first_possession_chain_prob.label: Opening-possession race probability (team scores first)
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.mechanism: Probability that team A scores first given tip result and each team's opening-possession conversion rate: pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)).
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.rationale: The existing tip input treats tip win as the driver, but the tip only fixes who starts the race; the conversion rates on both sides decide it and the formula shows why the tip's effect is only a few points. At pA = pB = 0.5 the race formula gives 0.667 for the team holding the ball, so a tip win is worth about 2-3 points of team-first probability, not more.
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.measurement: pA = (games where A's first possession produced a score under the contract rule (made FG only, or any made shot or FT) + 40*0.50) / (games + 40) over the last 2 seasons with 15-game half-life; pB likewise for the first defensive trips, so each team uses its own first-trips rate. P(A wins tip) = 0.5 + beta*(tipA - tipB) where tipX is the starting jumper's tip-win rate shrunk to 0.5 with k=15 tips and beta estimated by regression of the tip winner on tipA - tipB over 5 seasons. P(A first) = P(A wins tip)*pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)) + (1-P(A wins tip))*(1 - pB/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB))). As-of: starters confirmation.

nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.label: First-attempt shot-type mix and make probability
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.mechanism: The opening shot is more likely a rim attempt or a catch-and-shoot three off a set play, and the make rate depends on that type.
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.rationale: The existing shot_profile is season-wide but the opening plays use their own distribution; a player whose first shots are layups has a higher conversion than the same player's season average.

Make probability by type: his own all-attempt make rate for that type shrunk to the league type rate (computed from the same 3 seasons, not hard-coded) with prior weight 50 attempts, times opponent factor = opponent first-6-minutes zone FG% allowed / league (shrunk 20 games). Output P(first FGA is a make of type t) = mix * make probability. As-of: starters confirmation.

nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.label: Non-additive multi-absence cost curve
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.mechanism: The margin cost of losing several rotation players is not the sum of individual costs because the replacement pool deteriorates and rotations compress.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.rationale: The existing catalog sums per-player impact (player_impact, lineup_adj_rating) but missing two starters on a team with a deep bench costs less than two times one, whereas on a thin team it costs more; the curve must be estimated by roster depth.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.measurement: Fit on 5 seasons of team-games: margin residual vs number of missing rotation players (top-8 by minutes) and the sum of their impact values, with spline in missing impact and interaction with depth index (average impact of players 9-12); predictions per scenario branch; shrink spline with ridge; as-of nightly after injury report.

nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.label: Replacement-level minutes absorption
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.mechanism: When a rotation player is out, minutes flow to specific teammates at specific quality; who absorbs them (a starter playing more versus a bench player starting) determines the actual rating loss.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.rationale: Impact-based absence valuations assume replacement at team-average bench quality; a team whose next man up is a two-way player or an out-of-position player loses much more.
nba.replacement_level_minutes_absorption.measurement: From 3 seasons of game-level minutes: for each team and absent role (primary ball handler, wing, rim protector), estimate the share of vacated minutes absorbed by each teammate with ridge regression, then compute expected replaced rating = Σ share_j × impact_j(minutes-adjusted); use 20-game half-life; compare to team default; fallback to position-group priors for new combinations.

nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.label: Roster-overlap weighted team rating
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.mechanism: Past game results are weighted by how similar the active set of that game was to tonight's, so results from games with different rosters count less.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.rationale: Season ratings blend games played with and without stars, and a rating from a healthy-roster sample misleads for a depleted lineup; the overlap weighting makes the baseline condition on the rotation.
nba.roster_overlap_weighted_rating.measurement: Weight w_g = exp(-lambda × (1 - overlap_g)) × recency half-life 40 games, overlap_g = Σ over tonight's top-10 players of min_share_tonight × I(played in game g), lambda fit by out-of-sample game-margin error on 3 seasons; rating = weighted opponent-adjusted net rating shrunk to the preseason prior with k=15 effective games.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.

nba.series_game_conditional_state.label: Playoff-series game-conditional state
nba.series_game_conditional_state.mechanism: In a series, a game's mean margin depends on series score, rest days between games, accumulated injuries and coaching adjustments.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.rationale: Single-game ratings treat games as independent; series markets (home clinch, game 7, comeback) depend on the dependency between games and on elimination-state minutes tightening.
nba.series_game_conditional_state.measurement: Model for game g of a series: margin_residual = actual margin - own-model pre-game expected margin (ratings plus home advantage, as of tipoff, from nba.ratings) regressed on rest days since the last game, elimination-game indicator for the trailing team, injury-status change since game 1 (minutes-weighted impact of newly absent players), previous game's margin (shrunk) and games played, on playoff series 2000-2025 with a series random intercept; estimate the sd of the random intercept by REML (do not assume 2 points) and report its posterior. nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from nba.margin sd model (about 12, scale sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.

nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.label: Coach-level tie-forcing and intentional-foul policy
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.mechanism: How often a team trailing by 2-3 in the last 30 seconds attempts a tying three or a fast two, and how often the leading team fouls up three.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.rationale: Excess tie mass comes from end-of-game choices; teams differ, and the same game state yields a tie more often when the trailing coach shoots for the tie than when he fouls and hopes.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: in games within 3 points with <30 seconds left, share of trailing-team possessions ending in a 3PA, a 2PA or a foul-drawn FT; leading-team foul-up-3 rate; compute per coach over 3 seasons (min 15 events) with shrinkage k=10 events to league mean; produce per-matchup tie-conditional probability = P(close at 30s) × P(tie | close, policies).

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). nba.bench_minutes_distribution.label: Bench minutes distribution (240 + 25k minus starter minutes)

nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.label: Starter/bench designation ledger and rest-driven reclassification
nba.starter_bench_definition_ledger.mechanism: The bench is the set of players not in the official starting five, so a starter absence promotes the next man into the starter group and shifts scoring from bench to starter.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.mechanism: The head-to-head team stat is the difference of two counts with positive correlation through game pace and negative through script effects.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.
nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.measurement: For a team stat X (e.g. 3PM): mean_X = attempts_X x rate_X using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life, rate shrunk with k=150 attempts); each team's count ~ negative binomial with dispersion estimated from 3 seasons of team-games. Correlation rho between the two teams' counts = empirical correlation of residual counts across the same game over 3 seasons, modelled as a linear function of the game's total possessions (pace) and pooled by stat; use a Gaussian copula with this rho to couple the two NB marginals. Compute P(A>B) and P(tie) by summing the joint pmf; apply the blowout correction by increasing the trailing team's 3PA rate by the coefficient estimated from the margin-conditional attempt rate (nba.three_att_script_elasticity). As-of: games before tip.

nba.three_point_variance_load.label: Three-point attempt volume as a variance load
nba.three_point_variance_load.mechanism: The sd of the total depends on how many threes both teams attempt and on the dispersion of free-throw and two-point results.
nba.three_point_variance_load.rationale: The draft says total sd is about 17-19 as a constant; it varies with shot mix, and wide-open three-heavy teams produce a wider total distribution that matters at ladder tails.
nba.three_point_variance_load.measurement: Var(total) = Var(possessions) x ppp^2 + sum over both teams of E[3PA] x 9 x p3(1-p3) + E[2PA] x 4 x p2(1-p2) + E[FTA] x pft(1-pft) x (1 + dispersion), plus the covariance 2 x Cov(possessions, ppp) x E[poss] x ppp, using opponent-adjusted attempts and rates (20-game half-life) as of tipoff; Var(possessions) estimated from 3 seasons of team-game pace residuals. Calibrate a scalar lambda so that predicted variance divided by realised squared residual of total points in the 2 previous seasons equals 1 (rolling), report sd per game and skew from the third moment of the same components. All inputs are team shot counts, not lines. As-of: games before tip.

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.label: Margin decay after starters are pulled (by coach and lead size)
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.mechanism: The final margin equals the margin at the pull time plus a bench-vs-bench drift whose size depends on lead and coach.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.rationale: Blowout probability alone does not tell how much a 20-point lead at 6:00 shrinks; a coach who pulls starters early gives up points.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.measurement: Trigger moment = first time at least 4 of the leading team's 5 starters are on the bench (leading team defined at that moment) with the lead at least 10; record lead L0 then final margin M_F; delta = M_F - L0 (leading team perspective). Bucket L0 in 10-14, 15-19, 20+; per bucket compute mean and sd of delta over 3 seasons by coach with shrinkage to the league bucket mean with prior weight 8 games. Output drift and sd for tonight's coaches; as-of = last completed game.

nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.label: Second-unit net rating gap
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.mechanism: The bench lineups play most late blowout minutes, so the margin drift is the second unit's net rating difference.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.rationale: Starter-based team ratings say nothing about who wins the last six minutes of a blowout; a deep bench preserves a lead.
nba.second_unit_net_rating_gap.measurement: Define a team's top-5 as the five players with the highest minutes per game (ties by nba.player_impact) over the last 40 games, excluding long-term injured. Second-unit lineups = all 5-man lineups with at most one top-5 player on court. Net rating per 100 possessions = pooled points diff/possessions over the last 40 games, opponent-adjusted by the opponents' defensive/offensive ratings faced, shrunk to the team's overall net rating minus 3 points with k=250 possessions. gap = team A second-unit minus team B second-unit; expected margin drift per six-minute bench stretch = gap x game_pace/48 x 6/100. As-of: projected rotation from the confirmed injury list; lineup data from games before tip only.

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.mechanism: If regulation ties, the final margin is the margin of a five-minute period (or more), concentrated in 1-8 points.

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.label: Deal-stage ledger and league approval pipeline

nba.calendar_hazard_profile.label: Calendar hazard profile (deadlines, draft, free agency, board meetings)
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.mechanism: Event hazard varies with landmarks: trade deadline, draft week, free-agency opening, league board meetings, season start.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.rationale: A uniform hazard over the window badly misprices markets with a deadline; most transactions cluster in a few days and the remaining hazard collapses after each landmark.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.measurement: Daily event counts per type (trade, coach change, retirement, signing) from 15 seasons of Pro Sports Transactions, indexed by day offset from each landmark (trade deadline, draft, free-agency opening, lottery). Discrete hazard h_d = events on day d / teams-at-risk on day d, smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of sd 2 days plus landmark dummies for day -1, 0, +1, estimated by Poisson regression. P(event in remaining window) = 1 - product over days of (1 - h_d), conditioned on no event so far; announced meeting dates enter as additional landmark days. As-of = announcement timestamp of the latest transaction.

nba.franchise_valuation_comps.label: Franchise valuation reference class (comparable sale and expansion prices)
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.mechanism: A headline franchise value is drawn from the distribution of recent sale and expansion prices, scaled by market size and revenue growth, so P(value above strike) comes from a predictive distribution over comparables, not a base rate of events.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.rationale: KXNBAFRANCHISECOST resolves on a headline enterprise value above a strike after bundled assets are stripped; the event base rate says only whether a sale happens, whereas the strike probability needs a valuation model built from comparable transactions and the league's expansion-fee reporting.
nba.franchise_valuation_comps.measurement: Collect headline enterprise values of NBA franchise sales and expansion fees 2015-2026 with market, year and reported separable asset adjustments; regress log(value) on the prior-year published franchise valuation, revenue growth and market size; predictive sd from residuals (inflate for expansion franchises, which have no comparables); P(headline > strike) from the predictive distribution, then multiply by P(qualifying sale announced and approved within the window) from the approval pipeline.

nba.game_factor_loadings.label: Game-level latent factor loadings by leg type
nba.game_factor_loadings.mechanism: Legs load on shared factors (pace/total, margin, team shooting luck, availability) with loadings that differ by leg type and player role.
nba.game_factor_loadings.rationale: The draft lists covariance of a single player's stats, but multi-leg dependence spans legs from different mechanisms; a factor model captures it with a manageable parameter count.
nba.game_factor_loadings.measurement: Build leg indicators without any line: team margin above own-model expectation (nba.own_model_team_totals), game total above own-model total, and player stat above the own-model mean at typical thresholds. Transform each indicator to normal scores through its marginal CDF (probability integral transform on own-model predictive distribution) over 6 seasons; fit a 3-factor (total, margin, team luck) Gaussian factor model with loadings per team-side and role cell (starter guard, wing, big) by ridge-penalised maximum likelihood on the latent scale (tetrachoric correlations for binary legs). Report loadings and their sd over 100 bootstrap draws of games; as-of end of previous game.

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.

nba.leg_void_state.label: Leg void-state probabilities and combo payoff rule
nba.leg_void_state.mechanism: The combination's payoff depends on how a void leg (inactive player, protected early exit, postponement) is treated.
nba.leg_void_state.rationale: If one leg can void, the effective probability of Yes given not void differs from the product of the remaining legs, and the void probability itself is correlated with other legs through the injury event.
nba.leg_void_state.measurement: For each leg: P(void) = P(inactive) + P(protected early exit) + P(postponement beyond 48 hours) from the availability model; compute joint outcome probabilities for each void combination; apply the contract's rule (void whole, drop leg, or No) to compute the payoff probability; the rule is an input to be read from rules_primary when a combo series is live.

nba.own_model_team_totals.label: Own-model expected team points and total (market-free shared scoring factor)
nba.own_model_team_totals.mechanism: Expected team points = expected game possessions times availability-adjusted points per possession against the specific opponent, with a residual distribution built from own predictions; gives the shared scoring factor that same-game legs load on.
nba.own_model_team_totals.rationale: The shared pace/total factor must come from an own-model team total because a total implied by sportsbook lines is a market output and cannot serve as an input; this input also supplies the margin-total residual correlation that sportsbook-implied totals cannot.
nba.own_model_team_totals.measurement: possessions = pace composition of the two teams (nba.pace, lineup-aware, last 20 games weighted with half-life 8 games, shrunk to league mean with k=15 games); points per possession = availability-adjusted offence versus opponent defence rating with home adjustment, shrunk with k=20 games; team points = possessions x ppp; residual sd by team from own predictions on 5 seasons (not closing lines); output joint (margin, total) mean and covariance for the simulation.

nba.on_court_assist_share.label: On-court assist share of team assisted field goals
nba.on_court_assist_share.mechanism: The fraction of the team's assisted makes credited to the player while he is on the floor, which is the stable per-opportunity rate.
nba.on_court_assist_share.rationale: Potential assists and usage are indirect; the on-court assist share is the direct outcome rate, decomposed by lineup and whether co-creators are present, and is the cleanest basis for projecting the count from team assisted makes.
nba.on_court_assist_share.measurement: Share = player AST / (team assisted FGM while player on court), computed over last 60 games with half-life 25 games, separately for lineups with and without the top co-creator; shrink to role prior with k=300 on-court team assisted FGM; projected AST = share × expected team assisted FGM in projected minutes; as-of last game.

nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.label: Expected team assisted field goals in the player's minutes
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.mechanism: Team assisted makes depend on possessions, field-goal percentage, shot mix and the style-driven assisted rate.
nba.team_assisted_fgm_expectation.rationale: The draft uses implied team totals (market-derived) as the environment; an own estimate of assisted makes depends on assisted-rate by team and by opponent coverage, which totals do not capture.

nba.co_creator_load.label: Co-creator load (ball-dominant teammates on court)
nba.co_creator_load.mechanism: The presence of another ball-dominant creator divides initiations and assists.
nba.co_creator_load.rationale: Usage alone cannot distinguish a lone primary creator from a two-creator backcourt; assists fall when the second creator is on the floor and rise when he is out.
nba.co_creator_load.measurement: For the player and each teammate compute time of possession and touches per minute over 60 games; co-creator load = sum of the other four players' expected time of possession per minute (from lineup minutes) minus the league-average of the role; regress player's potential assists per minute on load (ridge) with team fixed effects; compute with tonight's expected lineups and scenarios.

nba.return_timeline_hazard.label: Return-from-injury timeline hazard by injury type
nba.return_timeline_hazard.mechanism: The probability a player has returned by a date follows a recovery time-to-event distribution with setbacks, not a point estimate.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.rationale: Reported timelines are lower bounds with setbacks; a return-by-date market is a CDF at a date, and the shape depends on the injury (ankle sprain versus stress fracture versus surgery).
nba.return_timeline_hazard.measurement: For each injury event 2015-present define t = days from the first public report date to first game appearance (right-censored at season end). Fit a Weibull survival model per injury category (ankle, knee, hamstring, back, foot/fracture, surgery, illness) with parameters shrunk to the pooled category with k=8 events, plus covariates: stated timeline (log days), team disclosure ratio (team's median actual/stated duration over its prior 10 events, shrunk to 1 with k=5) and age. P(return by T) = 1 - exp(-(t_T/scale)^shape) where t_T = days from the report date to T conditional on survival to the as-of day (use the conditional survival). Update at each new report; as-of timestamp = latest report vintage before the decision.

nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.label: Rare-make accrual rate (attempts per game x make probability x exposure)
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.mechanism: P(at least one make over the season) = 1 - exp(-sum over games of attempts x probability), a Poisson accrual with parameter uncertainty.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.rationale: Non-shooters have an attempt rate that can change after an off-season shooting project; preseason attempts are the leading indicator, and the exposure window excludes playoffs and the Cup final.
nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.measurement: lambda_g = 3PA per 36 (last 2 seasons with weight 0.4/0.6, preseason attempts added at weight 2.0 per game) x projected minutes/36 x p3 (player's last two seasons shrunk to the position prior 0.30 with k=40 attempts); exposure = expected regular-season games with minutes = P(available) per scheduled game over the 82-game schedule plus the expected number of Cup knockout games the team plays before the final (the sampled rule counts Cup games before the Championship game, so group and knockout games add exposure only to teams that advance; the final is excluded); P = 1 - E[exp(-lambda_total)] under Gamma(k,theta) for lambda with k=3; update after every game with new attempts.

nba.opening_night_starter_signals.label: Opening-night starter signals (camp lineups, preseason starts, coach statements)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.mechanism: The first regular-season game's starting five is predicted from the preseason starting lineups, camp reports and coach statements, with strong incumbency.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.rationale: A season-opener market has no in-season history, so the signal is the preseason; the team's preseason starters in the final two preseason games are usually the opener's starters, but not always.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.measurement: Score for each player = 0.5 x indicator of starting both of the last 2 preseason games + 0.3 x last season's start share + 0.2 x coach statement (coded 0/0.5/1); map to probability via logistic fit on 8 seasons of opener starters; set to 0 if the status is out or doubtful; combine with injury probability; as-of 24 hours before the opener and again at confirmation.

nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.label: Two-player co-appearance probability with rest correlation
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.mechanism: The probability that both players appear in at least one same game (or in many) is a joint availability probability with positive dependence from team rest decisions.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.rationale: Treating two players' availability as independent overstates co-appearance when rest decisions are shared and understates it when injuries are independent.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.measurement: Per game, P(both play) = pA pB + rho sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)) with rho estimated from 5 seasons of pair data (team rest days, load management) shrunk to a role prior; over N games P(at least one overlap) = 1 - Π(1 - P_g) with a correction for injury duration (autocorrelation across games); update after each game.

nba.payout_schedule_operator.label: Payout schedule operator g(K) parsed from rules text
nba.payout_schedule_operator.mechanism: The contract's value is E[g(K)] where g is the payout table in the rules text, so the schedule is part of the model.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.rationale: The cubic schedule means value is dominated by the upper tail: for threes with mean 3 the payout at the mean is $0.027, but the expected payout is much higher because 5+ made threes pay $0.125 or more. The operator must therefore be part of the model, not a post-hoc transform.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.measurement: Implement the two live schedules exactly: points g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/50)^3)/10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s/2))); threes g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/10)^3)/10000 with y = min(10, s); parse any new schedule from rules_primary/rules_secondary into (band_lo, band_hi, payout) arrays and cap/void fields and check monotonicity against the formula; value = sum over k of P(K=k) g(k); compute sensitivity of value to mean, variance and P(K >= cap) by finite differences; version the parser by rules hash and flag unparsed tables.

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.label: Within-game make-rate dispersion (beta-binomial rho)
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.mechanism: Makes in a game are positively correlated beyond independent shots, so the count is overdispersed relative to a binomial.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.rationale: Independence understates the tail of makes, which a convex payout over-weights; the dispersion parameter is a key tail parameter.
nba.within_game_make_dispersion.measurement: Estimate rho by maximum likelihood of a beta-binomial model on 5 seasons of player-game (attempts, makes) for players with at least 200 attempts; pool by shot type (three, two, free throw) and by attempt count; shrink the player-specific rho to the pooled value with k=100 games; produce the pmf of makes given attempts n and rate p.
