nba.schedule_marquee_selection_model.label: Marquee-date schedule selection model (Christmas and opening games)
nba.schedule_marquee_selection_model.mechanism: The league selects Christmas and opening-week pairings for national TV from teams with star power, large markets, rivalries and last season's Finals or ring-night storylines, under arena and travel constraints.
nba.schedule_marquee_selection_model.rationale: Christmas and first-opponent markets are a choice among a few feasible pairings; team performance matters only via appeal, and the strongest predictors are prior-year national-TV allocation, star presence and storyline, plus pre-release leaks. A Finals rematch or ring night is close to a fixed rule, which a base rate over all pairings misses.
nba.schedule_marquee_selection_model.measurement: For each candidate pairing on the date compute features known before the schedule release: both teams' national-TV game counts last season, the league's announced broadcast-partner allocation if published before the as-of time (else last season's), number of All-NBA players on each team (last season), DMA rank of each market, whether either team was in the prior Finals or conference finals, rivalry flag, and the count of Christmas/opening-week appearances in the last 5 seasons. Fit a conditional logit over feasible pairings on 15 seasons of Christmas and opening-week slates with ridge shrinkage; enforce one game per team per date by sampling without replacement; update to near-certainty on credible tier-one leaks with a timestamp. nba.series_stat_leader_model.mechanism: The series leader is the player with the largest cumulative points or rebounds over the series, the maximum of about 16-20 rotation players' totals over a random number of shared games, correlated through series length and pace and negatively within a team.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.label: Market-free overtime probability and overtime scoring increment from the ratings-implied regulation margin
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.mechanism: A game goes to overtime only if the regulation margin is exactly zero, so P(OT) is the mass at zero of the regulation-margin distribution, highest for evenly matched teams; each five-minute overtime then adds scoring at both teams' per-minute rates, and a further overtime follows with the tie probability of a five-minute period.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.rationale: The catalog nba.ot_model conditions P(OT) on the closing-spread bucket (a market quantity) and says one OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure, not the combined one. A market-free version takes the regulation-margin distribution from team ratings and sizes OT correctly: roughly 11-13 points per team and 22-26 combined per period, with repeated overtimes possible. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.measurement: Step 1: regulation-margin mean mu from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (opponent-adjusted net ratings x expected possessions/100 + home advantage, as of tipoff, adjusted for confirmed inactives). Step 2: P(regulation tie) = logistic regression of the indicator "regulation margin = 0" on |mu| over the last 5 regular seasons (about 6,000 games; league base rate to be estimated), smoothed across 1-point |mu| bins. Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. Only team ratings, pace and results enter.

nba.team_bench_points_model.label: Team bench-points model: non-starter minutes times bench scoring rate, conditional on margin path and confirmed starters
nba.team_bench_points_model.mechanism: A team's bench points equal the minutes played by non-starters times their points per minute; bench minutes rise sharply in blowouts (for both teams) and when starters exit, and the confirmed starting five decides who is counted as bench.
nba.team_bench_points_model.rationale: A bench-points contract moves opposite to star ladders: a blowout or a starter's early exit increases bench minutes, while a pregame scratch of a starter promotes a reserve into the starting five and removes his points from the bench total. Neither the individual points inputs nor team-total inputs say who is classified as bench, which is fixed only at the starting-lineup announcement.
nba.team_bench_points_model.measurement: Step 1: expected bench minutes = 240 (+25 per overtime period) minus the sum of projected starter minutes, with starter minutes from nba.minutes conditioned on the margin-path curve of nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve and on confirmed starters (nba.starters_pit). Step 2: bench points per minute = minutes-weighted sum of each projected reserve's shrunk points per minute (prior weight 300 minutes toward the role mean) times the team's opponent-adjusted offensive-rating factor. Step 3: distribution by simulation over margin paths and starter-exit scenarios (foul-out, injury) with player-level negative-binomial points; calibrate dispersion on 3 seasons of team bench points from box scores with the starter flag. As-of: lineup confirmation (about 30 minutes before tip); earlier, a mixture over probable starting fives.

nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.label: League-wide first-passage race to a single-game scoring threshold (first 50-point game) with same-day ties
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.mechanism: The first 50-point game of the season is a race across all high-volume scorers: every game a candidate plays carries a small probability of 50+, and the winner is the candidate whose hit comes on the earliest calendar day, with same-day hits splitting the payout.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.rationale: A per-player 'scores 50 this season' probability is not the contract: the price depends on how many rival candidates exist, how early each plays and how often, and on same-day splits. Subtle: the race is usually decided in the first weeks or months, so early-season schedule density, minutes restrictions after the preseason and the number of credible candidates matter more than full-season rates.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.measurement: For each candidate i and remaining regular-season game g on date t_g: p_ig = P(points >= 50 | plays) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail (generalised-Pareto exceedance above 35 points with the overtime adjustment) times P(plays g) from the availability inputs. Simulate 20000 seasons in date order: draw hits game by game, stop at the first date with any hit and split 1/N among same-date hitters. Candidates: players projected at 20+ points per game or with a 45+ game in the last 2 seasons; all others enter as a residual field with a league-wide per-game rate fitted on 10 seasons. As-of: nightly; resolved once a 50-point game occurs.

nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.label: League-wide probability of extreme single-game events over the remaining regular season (325+ combined points, 15+ steals plus blocks)
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.mechanism: 'Any game' and 'any player' contracts are unions over all remaining games of rare events whose per-game probability depends on both teams' pace and offense plus overtime periods (game totals) or on a few high-activity defenders (combined steals and blocks), so the season probability is 1 minus the product over games of (1 - p_g).
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.rationale: These events sit far in the tail: a 325-point game needs exceptional pace and shooting and usually more than one overtime, and 15+ steals plus blocks by one player is extremely rare. Per-game probabilities are tiny and governed by tail shape (count of OT periods, heavy-tailed defensive activity), so fits to means can be wrong by orders of magnitude, and the union over about 1,230 games compounds the error.
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.measurement: Game total: for each remaining game, regulation total = mean from both teams' opponent-adjusted pace and offensive ratings as of the game date plus an empirical residual with a generalised-Pareto tail above the 99th percentile (5 seasons); add overtime periods and combined OT points from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin; P(total >= 325) by simulation. Steals plus blocks: per player-game, a bivariate negative binomial from shrunk per-36 rates (prior weight 1,000 minutes) times projected minutes, tail checked against 20 seasons of single-game maxima; P(any player >= 15) = 1 - product over player-games. Season probability = 1 - product over remaining games, Cup knockout games included and the Cup final excluded. As-of: nightly.

raw_data: Game totals with overtime periods (5+ seasons)

nba.season_plus_minus_projection.label: Season total plus/minus projection: on-court net margin rate times remaining minutes, combined across teams after trades
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.mechanism: Total plus/minus is the scoring margin while a player is on court summed over the season, so it equals on-court minutes times his lineups' net margin per minute; team strength and minutes dominate it, the player's own impact is a smaller part.
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.rationale: A plus/minus leader race is usually won by a heavy-minutes starter on the best team rather than the best individual player, and teammates on a dominant team compete with each other. Subtle: the rules combine a traded player's totals across teams, and games missed scale the total down linearly, so a durable starter on a 60-win team can beat a better player who misses 15 games.
nba.season_plus_minus_projection.measurement: For each candidate: remaining minutes = remaining team games x P(plays) x projected minutes per game (nba.injury_risk_season, nba.minutes). On-court margin per 100 possessions = team opponent-adjusted net rating (nba.ratings, as of date) + (1 - p_on) x on/off differential shrunk toward 0 with prior weight 3000 on-court possessions, where p_on = projected minutes share of 48 (this corrects the overlap between team net rating and on/off). Convert to points per minute using projected team pace (possessions per 48). Final total = official plus/minus to date (summed across teams for traded players) + remaining minutes x per-minute margin, simulated jointly with team season outcomes so teammates share team shocks; ties split 1/N. As-of: nightly, standings and plus/minus after final scores.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference player plus/minus pages (free, polite scraping)
raw_data: player season plus/minus and minutes to date (combined across teams)

nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.label: Probability of winning a game after trailing by D or more points (max-deficit comeback rate)
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.mechanism: A team wins after trailing by D only if the leader's in-game margin path reaches D and then reverses fully; large leads trigger starter rest and slower pace by the leader, so reversals from 30+ are rare and depend on when the lead was built.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.rationale: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK settles on any series game won after a 30-point deficit, a path event that no final-score model sees: a game can end close after a 30-point swing. Both the chance of a 30-point lead and the chance of reversing it depend on the strength gap, pace and how coaches manage big leads in the playoffs.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.measurement: From play-by-play for 15 seasons compute for each game the maximum deficit faced by the eventual winner, M. For each threshold D in {20,25,30,35} fit separately a logistic model P(M >= D) = f(own-model pregame margin mu, own-model margin sd, pace, playoff flag), pooling D by an ordinal-logit if counts are below 40 events, and shrink the playoff coefficient to the regular-season value with prior weight 200 playoff games. Output per-game P(winner trails by >= D) for each side as a function of mu. Series union = 1 - E[prod over games (1 - p_g)] using series length draws and the per-game mu; add a shared series random effect on the log-odds (variance estimated from playoff series) rather than assuming independence. As-of: before game 1 and after each game using realised results.

nba.playoff_round_event_counts.label: Joint distribution of round-level series event counts (sweeps, upsets, Game 7s) and team playoff losses
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.mechanism: Counts of sweeps, upsets and Game 7s in a round, and a team's total playoff losses, are sums over series whose pairings depend on earlier rounds and whose outcomes share common shocks.
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.rationale: KXNBASWEEP, KXNBAUPSET, KXNBAGAME7, KXNBAPOLOSE and KXNBAUNBEATEN settle on counts or exact totals; multiplying independent series probabilities ignores that second-round pairings and seed gaps are random, and that league-wide shocks (injury waves, officiating emphasis) make concurrent series dependent, which fattens the tails of the count.
nba.playoff_round_event_counts.measurement: Simulate the full bracket 50,000 times from nba.title_path with per-game probabilities from the series model, including a common per-round shock to home-court advantage (sd estimated from 20 seasons of round-level home win rates); record per round the number of sweeps, upsets (higher numerical seed beats lower, post-Play-In seeds) and Game 7s, and per team the total losses and the 16-0 indicator; output the joint pmf and marginal P(count >= N), P(losses = k). As-of: nightly during the playoffs; before the playoffs from the seed distribution.
raw_data: playoff series results with seeds and game-by-game outcomes (20 seasons)

nba.sl_mvp_award_model.label: Summer League MVP candidate model: individual production share, team advancement and games played
nba.sl_mvp_award_model.mechanism: The Summer League MVP goes to a player who combines a high scoring and usage share with a team that advances, and who plays most of his team's games; a candidate's chance is a conditional choice among the event's leading producers, weighted by his team's path to the final.
nba.sl_mvp_award_model.rationale: No other input gives an award outcome: team strength and game inputs price games, while the award depends on who plays enough games, per-game production relative to the field and voter emphasis on draft status and team success. Subtle: top picks often play two or three games and are shut down, so expected games played, not talent, is the first filter.
nba.sl_mvp_award_model.measurement: Step 1: for each candidate, expected games played = sum over the team's scheduled games of P(plays) from nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard, and expected points and usage per game from nba.sl_talent_translation and nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline. Step 2: team advancement probability from simulated event standings and the knockout. Step 3: conditional logit over candidates with covariates (expected total points, usage rank, team reaches the final, draft slot) fitted on past Summer League MVP winners and runners-up (at least 10 events, ridge penalty, prior weight 5 events). Step 4: renormalise across candidates; update after each game day with realised production. As-of: start of the event, then nightly.

nba.sl_first_half_share.label: Summer League first-half share of team points and margin by roster composition
nba.sl_first_half_share.mechanism: Summer League coaches give prospects and invited starters most first-half minutes and hand the second half to fringe players, so first-half points and margin depend more on top-of-roster strength than the full game.
nba.sl_first_half_share.rationale: First-half spread, total and winner contracts need the half distribution, not half the game distribution: the half margin carries a larger share of the roster-strength signal, its variance is not half the game variance, and the tie mass at zero is priced by KXNBASUMMER1HWINNER directly.
nba.sl_first_half_share.measurement: From the last five Summer League events compute, per game and team, first-half points / game points and first-half margin / game margin; regress the first-half margin on the minutes-weighted translated strength of the players who logged first-half minutes (from play-by-play substitutions) versus the full-game weighted strength; report the first-half share of mean total (shrunk to the pooled value with prior weight 40 games), the half-margin sd and the empirical integer tie frequency of first halves. As-of: pre-tip, using announced participation.

nba.sl_tournament_bracket_sim.label: Summer League tournament standings, tiebreak and knockout simulation
nba.sl_tournament_bracket_sim.mechanism: The Summer League champion is the winner of a knockout among the top teams of the group stage; qualification depends on a short record and a point-differential tiebreak, and later rounds are single games.
nba.sl_tournament_bracket_sim.rationale: With four group games per team, ties in record are common and point differential decides qualification, so a team's title chance depends on margin as well as wins; rosters also change between stages as prospects are shut down, so the knockout strength must be re-estimated, not carried over.
nba.sl_tournament_bracket_sim.measurement: Encode the current event format (group games per team, number of knockout qualifiers, tiebreak order including point differential) from the league's published rules; simulate remaining group games from the game-level margin distribution (nba.sl_format_scoring_baseline with team means from nba.sl_talent_translation and participation from nba.sl_minutes_plan_hazard), apply the tiebreaks, then simulate the bracket with per-round strength that drops by the expected shutdown share; 20,000 paths; output P(qualify), P(reach final), P(champion). As-of: after each game day.

nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.label: Probability a player reaches N points in at least one playoff game (union over a random, correlated run)
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.mechanism: A playoff-long single-game threshold pays on the maximum game score over a random number of games whose length depends on advancement and the player's own health, with per-game tails correlated through form and matchup.
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.rationale: Multiplying a regular-season per-game tail by expected games overstates the price: playoff pace and defense compress the tail, the number of games is zero with positive probability, health and advancement are linked, and a series against one elite defender correlates several games. The union must be computed jointly, not from marginals.
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.measurement: Simulate 20,000 playoff runs: draw the team's qualification and series path from the bracket simulation (nba.title_path, nba.series_length_distribution, nba.play_in_path_model), the player's availability per game from nba.playoff_star_health_hazard, a run-level form factor (log-normal, sd fitted from the player's game-to-game residual autocorrelation, about 0.1), and per-game p_g = P(points >= N) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail rescaled by playoff minutes (nba.playoff_rotation) and opponent defender shift (nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift); P(YES) = share of runs with at least one game >= N. Validate on historical playoff 40+ and 50+ games (rates too low for 50 alone). As-of: nightly from the end of the regular season.

nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.label: All-Star Weekend format and rules ledger by event and year
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.mechanism: Each event's winner is a deterministic function of the format: racks, balls, money-ball value, time limit, number of rounds, how many advance, tiebreak or shoot-off, dunk attempt caps and judging scale, All-Star Game length, target score and team structure.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.rationale: The formats are changed almost every few years (the Game has switched between East-West, captains' draft and a multi-team mini-tournament), so a historical result is only a label for the same process if the format parameters are matched. The subtle part is that a rule change moves variance and ties, not just level: a shorter game or a single-elimination final increases upset probability.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.measurement: Per event-year and per series (3PT, dunk, ASG, Rising Stars, Shooting Stars, MVP): participants, rounds, advancement count, balls per rack, racks, points per ball type (regular, money ball, deep-zone ball), seconds per round, shoot-off rule, dunks per round and attempt limit, judge count and score range, ASG game length or target score, number of teams, team-assignment rule (conference, draft, nationality), round-robin tiebreak order, Rising Stars semifinal/final targets, Shooting Stars team size and scoring, MVP selection method. Each field carries a provenance flag: RULES_TEXT (quoted Kalshi rule, e.g. 70 s, 40/25 targets, 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak), LEAGUE_RELEASE, or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; as-of = the league announcement date. Every historical label joins to its own format vector.

nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.label: Three-Point Contest round-score distribution and winner simulation
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.mechanism: Each shooter's round score is a sum over racks of correlated Bernoulli makes with different point weights; the winner is the maximum over finalists after advancement, with ties broken by a shoot-off.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.rationale: The winner is a max-of-noisy-scores over a field of about eight, so the favourite's chance is capped well below his skill edge; the round-score SD is several points, comparable to the skill gap between the best and median shooter (per-ball make probability is a parameter to be estimated, not a fact). Only the final-round score decides (rules), so round-1 advancement variance and final-round tie mass both matter.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.measurement: For each entrant simulate ball by ball: P(make) per location from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile (regular, money-ball and deep-zone balls), the shooter's chosen all-money-ball rack location, balls actually released within 70 s from the tempo distribution (unreleased balls score 0), rack-level correlation rho with a beta-binomial prior from nba.within_game_make_dispersion, point weights from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger; run 20000 simulations of round 1, top-three advancement, final round (score resets) and a shoot-off on ties; output P(win), P(advance). As-of = last field change or rack-placement announcement.

nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.label: Transfer of shooter skill to the contest's rack conditions
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.mechanism: Contest make probability is stationary-catch-and-shoot skill from fixed rack spots, with no defender, no movement, rhythm over about a minute and fatigue; it is only partly predicted by game 3P%.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.rationale: Game 3P% mixes shot difficulty and defence, so contest make rate is better proxied by catch-and-shoot or open-shot 3P%, free-throw skill and past contest make rate, each shrunk because contest samples are 25 balls. Deep-range pull-up shooters can underperform because the contest rewards form repeatability, and a venue's backdrop and rims add a shared level shift.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.measurement: Per entrant: posterior make rate = precision-weighted mean of (a) catch-and-shoot 3P% on open and wide-open attempts, last 3 seasons, half-life 1 season, shrunk toward league mean with a prior strength k (placeholder 300 attempts, to be fitted by cross-validation on past contests), (b) FT% logit scaled by a fitted slope, (c) past contest make rate shrunk with k (placeholder 75 balls); contest-conditions offset = mean residual of all entrants in the same contest-year (venue-year effect); units = P(make) per ball before location adjustment; as-of = day before.

nba.dunk_judge_score_model.label: Dunk Contest judging panel score and tiebreak model
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.mechanism: The winner is selected by a panel's subjective scores per dunk; round-one two-dunk totals pick the two finalists and the finalists' two final-round dunks alone decide the champion (rules); panel composition, scoring scale and the compression of scores near the maximum decide who wins and whether a dunk-off is needed.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.rationale: Scores cluster at the top of the scale so many dunks tie, and a run of 10s from celebrity judges can erase a difficulty advantage. Judges anchor on crowd reaction and narrative as well as difficulty, creating a first-mover and last-mover effect, and repeat winners can be penalised or rewarded depending on the panel's era.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.measurement: From past contests extract every dunk's judge scores; fit an ordinal model of dunk score on (attempt number, make flag, prop use, dunker's reputation, round, panel mean leniency) with a partial-pooling judge effect; estimate per-panel mean and SD and the probability of a perfect score; store panel composition as announced (as-of = announcement); output expected round-one totals, P(advance), final-round two-dunk totals (round one does not carry over) and P(tie) per finalist pair. Use only rounds since the current scale was introduced.

nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.label: Dunk difficulty tier and make probability under attempt caps
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.mechanism: A contestant's score depends on choosing a dunk of a given difficulty tier and converting it within the attempt allowance; misses burn time or attempts and zero or lower the score.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.rationale: Hard dunks have a high ceiling but a real miss rate, and the attempt cap makes the score a mixture between a clean mid-tier dunk and a failed high-tier one. Props, teammate assists and limited rehearsal affect conversion; contestants who tend to over-script get penalised for misses.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.measurement: Classify each past dunk by difficulty tier (360 or windmill, leap over a person, double-ball, two-step, prop-assisted) from video-coded tags; compute per-dunker attempt success by tier with Beta(2,2) shrinkage, and expected score per dunk = P(make before cap) times mean judged score of the tier plus (1 - P) times the miss score; as-of = last contest participated; units = points per dunk.

nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.label: Dunker athletic profile and prior contest record
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.mechanism: Contest strength comes from leaping ability, creativity and show experience, none of which appear in regular-season box scores.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.rationale: Contest entrants are often bench or G League players whose NBA stats say little, so talent is measured by prior contest finishes, highlight dunk rate, vertical measures from draft combine and age. The sample is tiny and selection is heavy, so pedigree must be shrunk toward a field mean and treated as a ranking, not a number.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.measurement: Per announced entrant: pedigree = mean of within-field percentile ranks of (a) contest score = sum over prior contests of points (win 3, final 2, appeared 1) * 0.7^(years since), (b) max vertical z-score from the Draft Combine (missing: field mean plus a missing flag with 0 weight), (c) dunks per 100 minutes over the last two seasons (NBA plus G League), shrunk to the position mean with prior weight 200 minutes; equal weights 1/3 each, plus a G League/non-NBA flag reported separately. Rank within the announced field; as-of = field announcement date.

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.label: All-Star Game team roster strength and composition
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.mechanism: The Game winner is the team whose assigned players are collectively better at scoring in an open-court, low-defence environment, built from impact, shooting and creation of the players who actually appear.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.rationale: Because the same selected stars are split among teams, gaps are small and dominated by composition: shooters and creators gain more than rim protectors in a low-defence game, and replacements change rosters late. In 2026 teams were built by nationality (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), so one team can be systematically stronger, unlike a draft; in 2025 the drafted teams faced a Rising Stars team of first/second-year players.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.measurement: For each team sum over rostered players minutes_share_i * (0.6*OffImpact_i + 0.25*z(3PA per 36 * 3P%) + 0.15*z(AST%)), where OffImpact_i is multi-season offensive RAPM/EPM shrunk to 0 with prior weight 1,500 possessions; minutes_share from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan normalised to 1. Convert the team difference to expected margin per 12 minutes with a scale factor fitted by one-parameter ridge regression on past exhibition margins (2013-2025, pooled over formats; the three weights are fixed, not fitted), applying a -0.5 point adjustment per missing big. As-of = final roster after the replacement window; output every team pair.
raw_data: Player offensive impact per 100 possessions (RAPM/EPM or on/off)

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.label: All-Star exhibition effort, pace and score variance baseline, conditional on timed vs target format
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Exhibition scoring and margin come from low defensive effort, extreme three-point volume and random clustering of makes; how effort evolves depends on whether the game is clock-timed (2026: 12-minute games) or untimed race-to-target (2025 ASG, Rising Stars).
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.rationale: Margin variance is large relative to talent gaps, so short games raise the weaker roster's chance. In timed games effort rises in the final minutes and point differential can matter for the tiebreak; in target-score games there is no clock and the end is a race, so the two regimes must not be pooled. The contract year fixes the regime: 2026 KXNBAALLSTARGAME is timed (rules text), KXNBARISINGSTARS is target (rules text).
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.measurement: Split all exhibition games by format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger. Timed games: points per team per minute, 3PA rate, margin SD per 12 minutes and late-compression coefficient (margin SD change over the final 4 minutes). Target games: points per possession for each team and possessions to reach the target, fed to nba.target_score_race_model. Shrink current-format estimates toward the pooled same-regime value (few games per format); as-of = last completed event; units = points and margin SD.

nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.label: All-Star Game minutes plan, rest and multi-game fatigue
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.mechanism: All-Star players play capped minutes with fairly even distribution, and in a multi-game format starters and replacements are managed across games, which changes who is on court in the decisive game.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.rationale: Minutes are not set by merit: coaches are mostly told to share minutes, and players with injuries or heavy loads often log little. In a mini-tournament, a team that must play two games may rotate its stars, while the fresh final-game lineup matters more than the roster list.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.measurement: For each All-Star in the final roster: rank-based minutes prior m0 = mean All-Star minutes of past players in the same season-minutes tercile and starter/reserve role (2010+), shrunk to the pooled mean with prior weight 10 player-games. Fit a logistic model for P(minutes < 15) on age, season minutes per game (z), starter flag and an injury-flag dummy (Questionable/Probable listed by 24h before tip) with ridge penalty 1.0; for multi-game formats add the fitted game-2 minus game-1 minutes drop by tercile. As-of = last injury-report vintage at least 2 hours before tip; units = minutes and probability of reduced role.

nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.label: Contest field changes: withdrawal and replacement hazard
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.mechanism: The entrant list for the 3-point and dunk contests is announced weeks ahead and changes through injury, rest, ASG replacement and sponsor negotiation, which changes both the field strength and the winner's probability.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.rationale: A late replacement is usually weaker or different in type, and a withdrawal of the favourite lifts every remaining entrant; the market question requires a specific named player so this is also an eligibility risk.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.measurement: Per announced entrant: base withdrawal rate w0 = (withdrawals + 1)/(announced entrants + 8) counted over 3PT/dunk/skills fields 2010-2026 from NBA.com announcements; logistic update with covariates current injury status (Out/Doubtful/Questionable from nba.injuries_pit at the latest vintage), also-in-All-Star-Game flag and also-in-Rising-Stars flag, ridge 1.0. P(participates) = 1 - P(withdraw). P(win | participates) from the contest score model for the actual announced field; replacements drawn from the next-ranked non-entrants by prior contest pedigree. As-of = each daily injury report and announcement time.

nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.label: Three-point contest location, deep-ball and release-tempo profile per shooter
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.mechanism: Contest score depends on accuracy at each rack location, on deep-range accuracy for the bonus balls between racks, on where the shooter places the all-money-ball rack, and on how many balls he releases before 70 seconds expire.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.rationale: Pooled open 3P% hides location splits: a corner specialist gains by placing the all-money rack in his best corner, and the deep bonus balls reward a 27+ ft make rate that many spot-up shooters lack. The 70-second limit (rules) means slow releasers leave balls unshot, a zero that pooled accuracy never sees.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.measurement: Per shooter: map shotchartdetail 3PA coordinates (LOC_X, LOC_Y) to the five contest racks (corner left/right, wing left/right, top) by distance from the rack position; 3P% by rack over the last 3 seasons shrunk to the shooter's pooled 3P% with k estimated by method of moments (default 150 attempts until estimated), 27+ ft 3P% shrunk to the league deep rate with k estimated (default 100). Tempo = balls released per round and seconds remaining from his past contest rounds (median and sd); if none, impute from the median of previous contestants with a similar release speed from tracking (labelled imputed). Rack placement = announced choice, else the rack maximising expected points. Output P(make) by ball type and balls released; as-of: rack announcement.
free_sources: NBA Stats shot dashboard and shot-location splits
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with x,y location and distance

nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.label: All-Star / Rising Stars tournament path simulation (round robin, tiebreaks, final)
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.mechanism: Champion probability is the result of a multi-game path: in 2026 three teams play a round robin of 12-minute games where margins feed the point-differential tiebreak, then the top two play a championship; brackets (Rising Stars, 2025 ASG) chain two target-score races.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.rationale: A pairwise team gap is not a winner probability: in the 2026 round robin a team's chance depends on its margin distribution in two games (point differential decides a 1-1-1 tie, per rules) and on who it meets in the final; Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1's result, so the path is sequential. In 2025 the fourth ASG team was the Rising Stars winner, an entrant unknown until two days before.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (50,000 runs) over the format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger: for timed games draw margin ~ Normal(expected margin from nba.asg_roster_strength_composite adjusted for minutes, SD from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline); apply the Game-2/Game-3 pairing by Game-1 result; rank by record then point differential and break remaining ties randomly (flagged); play the championship; for target-score formats call nba.target_score_race_model per game. Where the entrant list is not yet announced, draw each entrant from the nba.rising_stars_roster_strength rank order, never from market prices. Output P(champion) and P(final) per team; as-of = last roster change.
free_sources: Format parameters from the rules ledger
Basketball-Reference All-Star box scores for calibration
raw_data: Pairwise expected margins from roster-strength input

nba.target_score_race_model.label: Race-to-target exhibition game model (first to 40 / first to 25)
nba.target_score_race_model.mechanism: In an untimed game the winner is the first team to reach or exceed a target score, so the outcome is a first-passage race of two scoring processes rather than a margin over fixed time.
nba.target_score_race_model.rationale: A race to 25 has few possessions, so a per-possession efficiency edge converts to a much smaller win probability than in a 48-minute game, and a single three or and-one near the target is decisive (a made shot can overshoot). There is no garbage time and no clock-driven fouling, so timed-game variance estimates do not transfer. Relation to the existing nba.first_passage_race_table: that input is a first-to-N race inside a regular 48-minute game at full effort and does not end the game; here reaching the target ends the game at exhibition effort, so the table is only a structural prior/cross-check for N=25 and is not reused as the estimate.
nba.target_score_race_model.measurement: Model each possession as points in {0,1,2,3,4} with team-specific probabilities from offensive rating vs opponent defence under exhibition effort (from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline target-regime estimates), alternate possessions with a possession-start Bernoulli, simulate to target T (40 semifinal, 25 final per KXNBARISINGSTARS rules) 20000 times; output P(win) and expected possessions; validate on past target-score exhibitions; units = probability.
free_sources: NBA.com play-by-play of Rising Stars and 2024-2025 All-Star target games

nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.label: Rising Stars team strength from first/second-year and G League rosters
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.mechanism: Rising Stars teams are drafted from first- and second-year NBA players plus a G League team, so team strength rests on young-player offensive ratings with small samples and a cross-league adjustment for the G League side.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.rationale: Rookie and sophomore impact estimates are noisy and the G League team's stats are in a weaker league, so naive per-game scoring over-rates high-usage players on bad teams and mis-rates the G League side. Honorary coaches draft the teams, so team balance depends on the draft, and Rising Stars participants doubling into other events may play reduced minutes.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.measurement: Per player: offensive impact per 100 possessions this season (box-score composite) shrunk to a draft-slot prior with weight k = number of possessions at which sampling variance equals prior variance (estimate from rookie seasons 2015-2025, not 800 by assumption). G League players: rating x translation factor estimated as the regression slope of NBA first-year impact on prior G League impact over players who moved between leagues (report the estimate and its se; use 1.0 shrunk toward 0.7 if fewer than 30 players). Team strength = sum over rostered players of minute share x rating with minutes from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan; output per-possession scoring rate and sd for nba.target_score_race_model. As-of: Rising Stars draft and final roster announcement.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference rookie and G League stats

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.label: Shooting Stars team shooting skill and format conversion
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.mechanism: A Shooting Stars team (franchise-named; recent editions mixed current players with retired or other-league shooters) scores by making shots from a sequence of locations within a time limit; the team with the higher score wins.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's rules give only team and date; the 2026 league format (four trios of two current players plus one legend, seven spots in fixed order, 70 seconds, two rounds) is verified, but the per-spot point values and tie rule are not, so the conversion of makes to score is still incomplete. Legends have no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current catch-and-shoot rates with old evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: 2026 format (verified NBA release coverage): four teams of three, two current players plus one legend; seven designated spots shot in a fixed order of spots and players; 70-second limit; round 1 all four teams, top two to the final. Current players: P(make) by spot from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. Legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to the past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots; a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts within the clock. Point values per spot and the tiebreak are taken from the league's rules document for the year (not verified here); simulate 20,000 contests and report P(win); without the point table output only a labelled rank composite.
free_sources: NBA.com Shooting Stars announcements and recaps
raw_data: current-season shot-location data for active players

nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star MVP selection model (production on the winning team and voter choice)
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is chosen by a selection panel after the event; winners almost always come from the champion team and are the standout scorer or narrative figure, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(selected | team wins, box score, narrative).
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: In a tournament with short games the MVP depends on the whole path, and home-market or farewell narratives can beat raw points. The selection method (media panel, any fan component) and whether it covers only the championship game are not in the Kalshi rules, and a withdrawn named player resolves No.
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: 2026 rule: media panel vote right after the championship game combined with a 25% in-game fan vote; scope = the whole tournament (Edwards 2026, totals across three games, 10 of 14 panel votes). Panel part: P(panel pick) = sum over teams P(team wins the tournament) from nba.asg_tournament_path_sim x conditional logit over that team's players on tournament points share, made threes, minutes, home-market flag and prior All-Star MVP (fit on 20+ events), plus a residual for a non-champion MVP from the historical share; final score = 0.75 x panel share + 0.25 x nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share; multiply by P(participates). As-of: final rosters.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference All-Star MVP history and box scores
raw_data: Starter status, home-market flag, prior MVP flag

nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.label: Game-by-game series simulator for the joint law of series length, cumulative total and cumulative point differential
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.mechanism: Draws each game's (home points, away points) jointly, records the winner, stops when one side reaches four wins, and sums points and margins over the realised games, so length and points are generated by one process rather than combined independently.
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.rationale: This is an aggregation model, not a raw information input: it is listed because every rung is a tail probability of its output and the catalog needs its definition. The series total is a random sum over a random number of games, and the number of games depends on the same per-game margins that the spread contract sums. Multiplying an expected length by an expected per-game total loses the multimodal shape (one mode per possible length) and the negative coupling between lopsided margins and short series, which is exactly where rung probabilities live.
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.measurement: Monte Carlo (>=200k paths) over the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern from the current series state; per game draw team points from a bivariate distribution with means from own-model pace x points per possession for that game's venue, rest and projected lineups, a series-level random effect shared across games, and a correlation between total and |margin| fitted on 2004+ playoff games; output P(N=k), P(total>=K) and P(diff>=S) for every listed rung, recomputed at each as-of timestamp.
free_sources: Derived from Basketball-Reference / NBA Stats playoff box scores and own-model ratings
raw_data: playoff game box scores (team points by period incl. OT, home team, series id and game number)
own-model expected possessions and points per possession

nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.label: Series-level shared TOTAL (scoring-environment) random effect and its covariance with margin residuals
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.mechanism: Two teams meeting four to seven times in two weeks share a scoring environment (tempo, scheme, shooting conditions) that persists across games, so game totals inside a series are positively correlated beyond pre-series ratings; this input owns the total-side dependence and the total-margin covariance only.
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.rationale: If games were independent, the sd of a five-game series total would be about sqrt(5) times the single-game sd; a positive intraclass correlation inflates that, fattening both tails of the series total and shifting probability toward far rungs. The margin-side series random effect (sd about 2 points), the previous-game margin and the elimination dummy are already defined in nba.series_game_conditional_state and are consumed from it, not re-estimated here. The size of this effect is small-sample and must be estimated with shrinkage.
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.measurement: Fit a random-effects model on playoff games 2004-present: residual of GAME TOTAL versus the pre-series own-model expectation, with a series random intercept; report the intraclass correlation and its posterior sd, shrunk toward a regular-season back-to-back-matchup estimate; update the series effect after each completed game with a normal-normal conjugate step. Also estimate the covariance between the total residual and the margin residual within game; the margin random effect itself is taken from nba.series_game_conditional_state so that the simulator holds a single fitted margin-dependence parameter.
raw_data: playoff game totals with series id and game number

nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.label: Playoff-versus-regular-season pace and efficiency shift by round
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.mechanism: Playoff games are played slower, with tighter rotations of better players, more half-court sets and more physical defence, so possessions and points per possession differ from the same teams' regular-season rates, and the shift grows by round.
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.rationale: Regular-season ratings applied directly overstate playoff possessions; summing the bias over four to seven games makes it a material miss on a series total ladder whose rungs are spaced a few tens of points apart. The shift is also matchup-dependent: fast teams lose more pace than slow ones.
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.measurement: For each playoff game since 2004, compute actual possessions and offensive rating minus the regular-season opponent-adjusted expectation for that pairing; pool by round with a hierarchical model (round level, team-tempo slope); report mean shift in possessions per 48 and points per 100 with sd, using a 6-season half-life to track era changes.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference / NBA Stats team game logs (regular season and playoffs)
raw_data: team game logs with possessions, points, opponent (regular season and playoffs, 2004-present)
regular-season opponent-adjusted team ratings and pace

nba.series_game_number_drift.label: Within-series drift of game TOTALS by game number (adjustments and familiarity)
nba.series_game_number_drift.mechanism: Coaches adjust coverages and rotations after each game and players learn the matchup, so later games in a series tend to be scored differently from game 1 (total-side fixed effects by game number 1-7); margin-side game-number, previous-game bounce-back and rest effects are owned by nba.series_game_conditional_state (its 'games played' and previous-margin features) and only consumed here.
nba.series_game_number_drift.rationale: Late games (5-7) exist only in longer series, so a drift by game number changes the per-game total exactly in the paths that cross high rungs, ; the margin level by game number is not re-fitted here because nba.series_game_conditional_state already carries games played as a margin feature and home margin by game number is confounded with the 2-2-1-1-1 venue alternation.
nba.series_game_number_drift.measurement: From playoff games 2004+: regress GAME TOTAL residual (vs pre-game own-model total) on game-number fixed effects 1-7 with series random effects, after partialling out rest days using the coefficients from nba.series_game_conditional_state (not re-fitted here); margins are not modelled here (margin by games played comes from nba.series_game_conditional_state); shrink game 6-7 coefficients toward game 5 because of sparse counts; output per-game total mean adjustments used by the simulator.

nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.label: Margin spread, blowout and starter-truncation profile in close-out and elimination games
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.mechanism: When one team can clinch or is facing elimination, effort and rotation decisions change the SPREAD of margins and the blowout and garbage-time profile (a team down 0-3 may concede late; game-7 margins are compressed); the mean shift for elimination games is the dummy in nba.series_game_conditional_state and is not re-estimated here.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.rationale: The final game of every series is a close-out game, so its margin enters every cumulative differential; if close-out games are more lopsided (or, for game 7s, tighter) than ratings imply, the differential's tails move. Effects are asymmetric by which side is on the brink.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.measurement: From playoff play-by-play 2004+: classify each game by state (clinch opportunity for home/away, elimination for both, neither); fit margin sd, blowout (>=20) probability and starter minutes after a 20-point lead by state, controlling for rating gap and venue, taking the mean elimination shift from nba.series_game_conditional_state; shrink state effects toward the neutral-game values with a prior sd of 2 points on sd-ratio terms.

nba.playoff_whistle_regime.label: Round-level playoff foul and free-throw environment with unknown future crews
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.mechanism: Playoff officiating tolerates more contact, cutting fouls and free-throw attempts relative to the regular season; crews are assigned game by game and announced on the morning of each game, so for later games only the round-level pool distribution is knowable.
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.rationale: Free throws are a large share of points and also add stoppages that change late-game possessions; a series-long shift of a few attempts per game sums to a material number of points. Using a single named crew for the whole series would be wrong because each game draws a different crew.
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.measurement: Per playoff game since 2010: personal fouls and FTA per 100 possessions minus each team pair's regular-season rate; model by round with crew random effects; for unplayed games integrate over the round's officials pool (empirical frequency of crew chiefs assigned in that round) and use the announced crew only for the game whose assignment is out.

nba.series_banked_points_state.label: Points already banked in completed series games (running team totals, running combined total and running differential)
nba.series_banked_points_state.mechanism: Both contracts sum over every game of the series, so once k games are final the sum splits into a known banked part and an unplayed remainder; the decision-time probability is a tail probability of the remainder measured from the shifted strike, not from the full strike.
nba.series_banked_points_state.rationale: For any decision after game 1 the banked sum is the largest single determinant of both contracts: a 900 total rung after three games with about 650 banked needs only about 250 more points, which is a length question (one more game or two), and the rung can already be decided (YES with certainty) once the banked sum reaches the strike. For the spread, a banked differential of +30 turns a 9.5 strike into a bet that the opponent outscores the leader by less than the remaining cushion. Using a series-start distribution after games are played would ignore this realised state.
nba.series_banked_points_state.measurement: As of timestamp T (decision time), take every series game with a final official box score published before T: for each, team points including overtime. Compute B_total = sum over completed games of (home pts + away pts); D_team = sum of (named team pts - opponent pts). Rung conversion: remaining requirement for the total is K_rem = K - B_total (P=1 if K_rem <= 0, otherwise tail probability of the remaining-games total under nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator started from the current series score); for the spread S_rem = S - D_team on the remaining-games differential. Games in progress at T contribute nothing unless the decision uses a live-score feed (excluded here); a game with a pending or corrected score is flagged and re-read after the correction window; units are points, no shrinkage because the quantity is realised.

NBA Stats leaguegamelog (final team points per game)

nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model.label: Award-eligibility Extraordinary Circumstances challenge: filing and grant probability
nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model.mechanism: A player who misses the 65-game line can file an Extraordinary Circumstances challenge decided jointly by the NBA and NBPA (or an independent arbitrator), so eligibility is ledger slack plus a discretionary appeal branch, not a pure count.
nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model.rationale: Verified for 2025-26 (announced 16 Apr 2026): Doncic (64 games) and Cunningham (63) were granted eligibility on the totality of circumstances, while Edwards (60 games, 58 counting) was denied by an arbitrator. An MVP or All-NBA price that treats a 62-64 game candidate as ineligible ignores a branch that was granted twice in one season; the branch is near zero far below the line.
nba.eligibility_appeal_grant_model.measurement: Per candidate below the qualifying line at season end: P(file) = 1 if qualifying games >= 60 and the player is an award contender (top-15 award score in nba.award_stats), else 0.2; P(grant | file) from a logistic on shortfall (65 - counting games), share of absences with documented injury, and whether absences were team-imposed rest, fitted on the challenge record since 2023-24 (2025-26: 2 granted of 3 reported) with a beta(2,2) prior and pooled shortfall slope; P(eligible) = P(ledger) + (1 - P(ledger)) x P(file) x P(grant | file). As-of: nightly; decisions dated from league/NBPA announcements.
free_sources: NBA and NBPA joint announcements (AP coverage, 16 Apr 2026)
raw_data: Challenge filings and outcomes by season with announcement dates

nba.allstar_nationality_quota.label: All-Star nationality composition (US vs international) and Commissioner additions
nba.allstar_nationality_quota.mechanism: Under the 2026 USA-vs-World format the 24 voted All-Stars must contain 16 US and 8 international players; if voting does not produce that split the Commissioner adds All-Stars to the short group, so a player's selection probability depends on his nationality group's depth.
nba.allstar_nationality_quota.rationale: Verified in the NBA's 2026 format release: if voting does not produce 16 US and 8 international players the Commissioner adds players to reach the minimum (international can include US-born players with ties to another country). A ninth-best international or seventeenth-best American can therefore be selected or pushed out independently of conference rank; the 2027 format has not been announced and may differ.
nba.allstar_nationality_quota.measurement: For each candidate tag nationality group from the league's roster designation (US / international, with dual-tie players flagged per the release); in each simulation draw of starters (nba.allstar_fan_vote_composite) and reserves (nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote) count US and international selectees; if a group is short of 16/8, add the highest-ranked unselected players of that group by the coach-vote score until filled (Commissioner choice modelled as rank order with 20% random swap among the top three); P(All-Star) = share of 10,000 draws selected. Apply only when the season's format release states a nationality rule; else set inactive.
raw_data: Voted starters and reserves with conference

nba.hustle_stat_index.label: Hustle Award index: per-minute rank aggregate over the nine tracked hustle categories
nba.hustle_stat_index.mechanism: The Hustle Award is not voted: the league ranks qualifying players per minute in nine tracked hustle categories and the best aggregate wins, so the winner is a deterministic function of tracked counts and minutes.
nba.hustle_stat_index.rationale: The league's award releases state the nine categories (deflections, charges drawn, screen assists, contested 2PT and 3PT shots, offensive and defensive loose balls recovered, offensive and defensive box-outs) measured per minute; Diabate (2025-26) ranked top-11 in six, Green (2024-25) top-40 in all nine. The weights are not published, so the index must be fitted to past winners rather than assumed; low-minute energy players are favoured by the per-minute basis subject to the qualification floor.
nba.hustle_stat_index.measurement: For each player meeting the qualification floor (league hustle leaderboard minimum, default 58 games and 24 minutes per game until confirmed for the award): per-36 rate in each of the nine categories from the league hustle-stats tracking, season to date; rank each category; index = weighted sum of category percentile ranks with weights fitted by rank-ordered logit to winners and top-5 finishers 2016-17 to 2025-26 (equal weights as prior, ridge lambda chosen by leave-one-season-out); project end-of-season rates with shrinkage k = 600 minutes toward the player's prior-season rate; P(win) from 10,000 draws of remaining-season rates and the qualification ledger. As-of: nightly.
raw_data: Hustle Award winners and finalists by season

nba.expansion_realignment_joint_tree.label: Joint governance scenario tree: expansion award -> conference realignment -> NBA Europe announcement
nba.expansion_realignment_joint_tree.mechanism: Expansion, realignment and the European league are sequential Board of Governors decisions on one calendar: awarding Seattle and Las Vegas forces a 16/16 conference split (one Western team moving East) and shares negotiating bandwidth with the Europe project, so the three contracts are dependent events.
nba.expansion_realignment_joint_tree.rationale: Verified: on 25 Mar 2026 the Board approved exploring two franchises in Las Vegas and Seattle (23 of 30 votes needed), with a later final vote, a 2028-29 target and Memphis or Minnesota the likely team to move East. KXNBAJOINCONF has near-zero probability unless expansion is awarded, and KXNBACITYEXPAND, KXNBAJOINCONF and KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE priced as independent hazards mis-state every joint and conditional price.
nba.expansion_realignment_joint_tree.measurement: Tree with dated nodes keyed to Board of Governors meeting calendar: node 1 P(final expansion vote passes by window end) from nba.governance_approval_pipeline stage (exploration approved -> bids -> final vote, 23/30 threshold); node 2 P(realignment announced | expansion) and the moving-team pmf (Memphis, Minnesota, other) from geography and reported statements, P(realignment | no expansion) = 0.02; node 3 P(Europe inaugural season announced) with a shared Board-calendar factor (correlation estimated as a beta-distributed shift of +/-0.1 in node-3 hazard when expansion votes occupy the same meeting). Each contract's price = the tree marginal for its window; joint and conditional values come from the same tree. As-of: after each Board meeting and dated report.
free_sources: AP/ESPN coverage of Board of Governors votes (25 Mar 2026)
raw_data: Board of Governors meeting dates and agenda reports

nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.label: Joint second-half margin: regulation-only and overtime-inclusive outputs from one simulated game
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.mechanism: The OT-inclusive second-half margin equals the regulation second-half margin plus the overtime margin, and overtime happens only when the regulation full-game margin is zero, so both 2H contract versions come from one draw.
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.rationale: Rules text: KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD and KXNBA2HTOTAL count the 2nd half including overtime, KXNBA2HWINNER excludes it. Pricing the two separately breaks the identity that they differ only in games tied after regulation; e.g. a 2H tie under KXNBA2HWINNER plus OT gives a decided KXNBA2H.
nba.second_half_reg_ot_joint_margin.measurement: Per simulated game: draw H1 and regulation H2 margins from nba.period_margin_pmf (correlated via nba.second_half_adjustment_effect); regulation full margin = H1 + H2reg; if zero, draw number of OT periods and each OT margin from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin (5-minute periods, repeat while tied); outputs: M2H_reg = H2reg (settles KXNBA2HWINNER, tie possible), M2H_ot = H2reg + sum(OT margins) (settles KXNBA2H, KXNBA2HSPREAD; totals add OT points); 50,000 draws per game; as-of tip. Check on settled pairs from every overtime game.

nba.live_period_state.label: In-play game state for later-period markets (score, clock, on-court lineups, team fouls, timeouts)
nba.live_period_state.mechanism: Later-period and second-half markets keep trading after tipoff, so their value is conditional on the realised state at the quote time rather than the pregame distribution.
nba.live_period_state.rationale: Verified on the Kalshi API (8 Nov 2026): KXNBA2H markets for 9 Nov games have close_time 12 Nov 03:00Z, two days after the game, with early close 'after a winner is declared', so they trade in play. Q2-Q4 and 2H prices then depend on the current margin, period, on-court five, team fouls toward the bonus, and timeouts left, none of which a pregame input carries.
nba.live_period_state.measurement: At each quote timestamp: period, game clock (seconds), score by team, score at the start of the current period, five players on court per team, team fouls in the period (bonus at 5), timeouts remaining, possession; source cdn.nba.com liveData play-by-play and boxscore JSON polled every 5-10 s with receipt timestamps; the period-margin model is re-run conditional on elapsed time and remaining possessions (nba.period_possession_split scaled by remaining clock) and the on-court units' ratings from nba.quarter_unit_projection. As-of: quote timestamp minus feed latency (record both).
free_sources: cdn.nba.com liveData play-by-play and boxscore JSON (free, unofficial)
raw_data: Live boxscore with on-court flags and team fouls

nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.label: All-Star MVP in-game fan vote share (25% of the MVP decision)
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is decided by a media panel voting right after the championship game plus a fan vote that counts 25%, so a popular player on the winning team can win with a weaker box score than the panel favourite.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.rationale: 2026 coverage: fans counted 25% and the panel gave Edwards 10 of 14 votes, with the award covering the whole three-game tournament. The fan vote is cast during the event, not in the January starter ballot, so it depends on popularity plus visible tournament moments; the January fan-ballot rank is only a prior for it.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.measurement: Per participant on each team: fan_share = softmax over the team's players of (a x log January All-Star fan-ballot votes from the last published returns + b x tournament points share + c x home-market flag), a, b, c fitted on past All-Star MVP fan-vote outcomes where published (else fixed a=1, b=2, c=0.3 as placeholders labelled unverified); MVP score = 0.75 x panel vote share (from nba.asg_mvp_vote_model) + 0.25 x fan_share; P(MVP) from 10,000 tournament draws. As-of: final rosters; fan-ballot snapshot dated.
raw_data: All-Star fan-ballot vote totals by player (January returns)
All-Star MVP results and reported vote splits

player_points.mechanism: Points = minutes x (field-goal attempts per minute x points per attempt + FT contribution). The distribution is a mixture over minutes scenarios (normal, blowout-truncated, foul trouble, early exit) times an overdispersed attempts process. Teammate availability reallocates usage; opponent rim protection and scheme change shot quality; shooting luck is mostly noise to regress. The ladder structure and the sharp line already embed much of the average, so value concentrates in scenario weights, tails and stale prices after news.

An overtime adds about five minutes for the starters still on the floor, which is the main route to the 40+ rungs; P(OT) must come from the ratings-implied regulation margin, not from a spread bucket.

interactions.hypothesis: Usage gain from teammate absence is strongest when the absent player shares position/role, and efficiency typically falls as usage rises.
Stars on big favorites have reduced minutes tails; the 30+ rung is far more sensitive than the 15+ rung to blowout probability.
Rim-attack scorers vs drop coverage and pull-up scorers vs switching have different expected efficiency than the team-level defense rating.
Attempts rise with team total only partly; an inflated total through efficiency does not increase attempts.
Foul-prone crews raise FTA for rim attackers; effect compounds with opponent foul rate.

When a co-star is out the scorer's usage rises but true shooting typically falls (harder shots, fewer assisted looks), so points rise by far less than usage; the loss is largest when the absent player is a primary creator whose assists generated the scorer's easy shots.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points-per-possession on usage change interacted with absent-creator indicator using stint data; check that the slope on usage is below 1 only for assisted-shot-heavy scorers.

interactions.hypothesis: Blowout probability trims minutes only in the fourth-quarter tail, which removes the high-minutes branch where 30+ outcomes live; the 30+ rung is therefore several times more sensitive to blowout probability than the 15+ rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot realised hit rate of 15+, 25+ and 35+ against pregame blowout-probability tercile; the log-odds slope should grow with the rung.

interactions.hypothesis: A drop-coverage defense raises expected points for a pull-up midrange scorer and lowers it for a roll finisher with the same usage; a switching defense does the opposite via mismatch creation, so scheme effects are conditional on shot type, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact opponent scheme label with scorer play-type share in a shot-level make model; test cross-term significance out of sample.

interactions.hypothesis: A bench total sums several reserves whose points co-move: a fast game raises all their counts together and a blowout raises all their minutes together, so the variance of the bench sum is well above the sum of individual variances; within a fixed minutes pool, reserves also compete for shots, giving negative pairwise correlation that partly offsets it.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised variance of team bench points with the sum of reserves' predicted variances, split by pace tercile and by blowout versus close games.

interactions.hypothesis: A player flagged questionable or just back from injury lives in a different minutes regime where the early-exit hazard rises several fold; the standard ladders refund only inactive players, so exits in the active state settle NO.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the fraction of early-exit games across status vintages and check the calibration of the mixture weights against realised short-minute rates.

interactions.hypothesis: Bench points jump once the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early in the fourth quarter, the same event that removes the 30+ branch for starters, so the bench total and star rungs of the same team move in opposite directions; a pregame starter scratch shifts the bench pool itself and has the opposite sign to an in-game exit.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team bench points on the margin entering Q4 in bins and on starter-scratch versus in-game-exit indicators; check for a kink at the coach-specific pull threshold.

nonlinearities.shape: concave: points per possession falls as usage rises
nonlinearities.why: Marginal shots taken by a scorer inheriting a teammate's usage are lower-quality (more contested, fewer assisted), so the points response to usage is below proportional and flattens above roughly 30% usage.

nonlinearities.shape: convex rung probability in expected points: heavy right tail lifts 30+ and 40+ rungs
nonlinearities.why: Rung probabilities for 30+ and 40+ rise faster than linearly with expected points and minutes because they sit in the upper tail, where hot shooting, free-throw surges and overtime stack; a mean-calibrated model misprices them.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise: near-linear 20-34 minutes, then flattening, with a bump from OT
nonlinearities.why: Per-minute scoring is roughly constant for starters, but rungs above 30 points need >34 minutes in most cases; OT creates a step increase that matters for the tail.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at margin about 18-20 with 6-8 minutes left
nonlinearities.why: Starters are pulled only after a decisive margin, so the minutes effect is small until blowout probability exceeds roughly one-third and then steep.

mechanism_review.summary: Points are minutes times a possession-and-usage-driven attempt rate times conversion, with free throws added. The causal chain is: availability and minutes scenario (a mixture, not a mean), team possessions available while he is on court (matchup pace and game script), his share of those possessions given the specific five-man unit on the floor, shot mix and shot quality against this defense, free-throw trips from foul drawing and the opponent's foul rate, game-script truncation or extension (blowout rest, late intentional fouling, overtime), and finally the settlement form, which differs across the series in this archetype (standard and ladder thresholds, the protected rung with its first-half-only refund, and a team bench-points total). Each stage adds variance of a different shape: discrete mixture for minutes, overdispersed count for attempts, Bernoulli noise with heavy shrinkage for makes, so the upper rungs are governed by scenario weights and tails rather than by the mean.

stages.name: Availability and minutes scenario mixture
stages.description: The scorer either enters the game or is voided; conditional on entering he plays under one of several scenarios: a normal starter workload of 32-36 minutes, a blowout trim to 26-30, foul-trouble stretches, a minutes restriction, an early exit, or overtime adding about five minutes if the contract counts it (the sampled ladder text does not say). The 30+ and 40+ rungs are reachable only in the full-load branch, so scenario weights set rung probabilities more than the player's mean points do. Status vintages and the calibrated probability that a questionable player plays feed this stage.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture with a long left tail and an OT bump; weights depend jointly on status, margin and fouls; not unimodal.

stages.name: Possessions available on court
stages.description: The number of possessions in the game is a joint product of both teams' pace, not either team's average, and a scorer's share of the possessions he is on court for is minutes divided by 48 weighted by stint timing. Pace shifts with lineup (a slow big lineup vs a small-ball unit) and with game state (trailing teams speed up late). Possessions scale attempts nearly proportionally, but the market total is a price and cannot stand in for it.
stages.distribution: Roughly Gaussian game possessions (sd about 6-7) but with lineup-dependent mean shifts and right skew from OT; fed into a Poisson-like attempt process.

stages.name: Usage allocation within the on-court unit
stages.description: Given possessions, the team's shot, free-throw trip and turnover events are divided among the five on court. A scorer's share rises when specific teammates are absent (a ball-dominant guard out raises a wing's share more than a rim-runner's), and falls when another creator enters. This is estimated better by a unit-level allocation model with creation archetypes than by per-teammate with/without splits.
stages.distribution: Dirichlet/multinomial shares; negatively correlated across teammates; attempts per game overdispersed relative to Poisson, variance rising with usage.

stages.name: Shot quality and conversion
stages.description: Points per attempt depend on the shooter's mix of rim, midrange and three attempts, defender proximity, and the opponent's scheme (drop gives pull-up midrange and threes, switch gives post mismatches, blitz gives short-roll chances). Single-game make rates are noise around talent, and shrinkage constants differ by shot type, so recent hot streaks should be heavily discounted except for rim finishing and free throws.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli sums with heterogeneous probability; variance dominated by binomial noise (for 18 attempts, sd of points about 5); heavy shrinkage required.

stages.name: Free-throw trips and officiating
stages.description: Free throws add points at 75-90% conversion depending on the shooter; trips are generated by drives and post touches and by opponent fouling, with crew-level foul-call tendency and the team-foul bonus state adding variance. Late-game intentional fouls add attempts for ball handlers. A scorer with a high free throw rate has a less volatile points distribution than a three-point-dependent one.
stages.distribution: Count of trips overdispersed; conversion binomial per trip with high-probability tail; a few late-game extras skew guards' right tail.

stages.name: Distribution, dependence and settlement form
stages.description: The live forms are the standard and ladder rung (a threshold probability on one player's points, nested across rungs so the curve must be monotone), the protected rung (the KXNBAPTSPROT text refunds at the pre-tip fair price a first-half-only appearance unless the strike is already met; the weight of that branch is nba.early_exit_hazard, which includes a coach-rested second half, not only injury exits) and the bench total, which is a sum over the non-starters fixed at the lineup announcement. Tail shape matters most for the 30+ and 40+ rungs, and the bench sum needs the dependence between reserves' minutes created by the margin path.
stages.distribution: Integer-valued, right-skewed, heavy upper tail for star rungs; the bench total is a sum of positively dependent reserve counts whose mean rises with the blowout probability.

stages.name: Team bench-points total filed here (KXNBABENCHPTS)
stages.description: KXNBABENCHPTS is not a player contract: the Kalshi series metadata (checked 8 Nov 2026) uses the BASKETBALLENTITYSTAT terms with scope 'Bench Points' and ESPN/NBA as settlement sources, the same team-entity stat as KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS. It is a team sum over players who did not start, so who counts as bench is fixed by the starting five at tip, blowout minutes for reserves raise it on both sides, and a late scratch moves a starter-calibre player into or out of the bench pool. It is modelled with the team-level bench inputs, not the single-player ladder.
stages.distribution: Team bench points are roughly normal (mean 30-40, sd 9-11) with right skew in blowouts and a mixture over who starts; no listed markets yet, so strike construction is unseen.
