DNP/void and stat-source rules define the settled quantity.
Sportsbook prop line is the strongest prior on the mean and the disagreement is the edge.
Reliability curve by price bucket and side shows how far to shade model probabilities for this market family.
Liquidity rank of the rung scales how much edge to discount for better-arbitraged main lines.
Taker-side prints before moves are a candidate informed-flow signal and set realistic fill assumptions.
Settled values (and their timing) are the labels for calibration and need reconciling with the named stat source.
Post-game stat corrections can flip a rung sitting exactly at the threshold, so settlement timing and source matter.
More possessions mean more fouls drawn; opponent-adjusted pace scales attempts.
A trip-based model gives both mean and clustering, which settle N+ strike rungs.
Bonus time is a mechanical pathway that scales every ball handler's attempts.
The right tail of free throws comes from these games and is concentrated among a few players.
Distinguishes a 60% center from a 75% guard and gives uncertainty for new players.
Own status vintage sets participation (void or zero-minute branch) and teammate status vintages set who takes the drives and rim attempts that generate shooting fouls; previously unattached.
With/without splits of teammates' absence on a player's drives, rim attempts and free-throw trips; the usage-redistribution channel for free-throw attempts.
Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_free_throws: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.

interactions.hypothesis: Attempt volume is crew-dependent, with biggest effect on rim-attacking guards and bigs.
Leading-team ball handlers gain FTA in close games; in blowouts the pattern vanishes.
Low-FT% bigs have high variance outcomes with attempts; Hack-a-style fouls raise attempts when game is close.

Crew whistle scales shooting-foul rates, and attempts scale with the player's rim and post volume, so the crew effect is multiplicative with exposure: a rim attacker gains more from a high-foul crew than a spot-up shooter.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with drives per minute and test the slope in a Poisson regression of trips.

interactions.hypothesis: Hack-a policies are triggered when a player's free-throw percentage is below about 60% and the game is within a possession or two; outside that state the target probability is near zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the target probability by FT% bucket and margin to find the thresholds.

interactions.hypothesis: The variance of makes depends on both attempts and rate: for a 60% shooter the binomial variance per attempt is larger than for an 85% shooter, so high-volume poor shooters have a wider count distribution than high-volume good shooters with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare residual variance of makes across FT% terciles at the same expected attempts.

interactions.hypothesis: The bonus effect applies in the minutes after the opponent reaches five team fouls in the period, so attempts depend on when in the quarter the player is on court; a player resting in late quarters misses the bonus window.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare FTA per minute in bonus versus non-bonus minutes by player and quarter.

interactions.hypothesis: In a close game the last minutes produce many free throws for ball handlers, while in a blowout those minutes are played by bench players and no intentional fouls occur; the regime depends on the margin at 5:00 left.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare attempts in the last five minutes conditional on margin buckets.

nonlinearities.shape: Binomial variance p(1-p), maximal near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: The uncertainty of makes given attempts is largest for poor shooters, so the response of P(N+) to attempts differs by percentage.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in FT% near 0.60 and in margin within about 6
nonlinearities.why: Target probability is near zero above the threshold and then jumps, so linear FT% effects misprice both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Compound (clustered) count with 1-3 attempts per trip
nonlinearities.why: Attempts arrive in pairs and triples, giving a variance higher than Poisson and a lattice that matters at specific N.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in late-game minutes
nonlinearities.why: The last five minutes are about 10% of the 48 game minutes (roughly 12-15% of a star's minutes in a close game) yet carry a disproportionate share of his free throws, perhaps 20-25% (recalled, unsourced), so total minutes understate the weight of the closing period.

mechanism_review.summary: Free throws made = free throw attempts x make probability, and the two factors have very different properties. Attempts are an event count generated by foul-drawing: trips to the line come from shooting fouls on drives and post-ups, non-shooting fouls once the opponent is in the bonus (five team fouls in the period), technicals, and intentional fouls late in close games. Each trip yields one to three attempts, so attempts are clustered, not independent. The make probability is a stable skill, around 0.75-0.85 for guards and 0.55-0.70 for many bigs, and conditional on attempts the number of makes is nearly binomial. So variance comes mostly from attempts, which depend on minutes, the player's drive and post frequency, the opponent's foul rate, the crew's whistle, the game's closeness (late-game fouling targets poor shooters and rewards the trailing team's fouls on stars), and on the bonus state. The count has a heavy right tail from close games with intentional fouls and is zero for many games for low-volume players.

stages.name: Floor time and role in the offence
stages.description: Free throws are drawn while on court and mostly while attacking the rim or posting up, so minutes and the number of such actions set exposure. A guard who attacks the rim 8 times per game and a spot-up wing with 2 rim attempts have attempt means of about 6 versus 1.5. Blowouts remove the late free-throw-rich minutes, while close games add them for the leading team's ball handlers.
stages.distribution: Mixture over minutes regimes; attempts per minute vary by role by a factor of five or more; count of trips overdispersed.

stages.name: Trip generation: shooting fouls and bonus state
stages.description: Trips arise from shooting fouls (rate per drive or rim attempt), non-shooting fouls in the bonus, offensive fouls that do not give shots, and technical or flagrant calls. The opponent's foul-committing rate, its defensive style (rim protection without fouling vs aggressive), the crew and the team-foul state of the period determine how many of the player's actions end at the line. The trip count is clustered and has a handful of possible attempt sizes (1, 2, 3).
stages.distribution: Poisson-like trip count with overdispersion; attempts per trip 2 with probabilities of 3 and 1; bonus state creates time-varying hazard within each quarter.

stages.name: Late-game fouling and intentional-foul targets
stages.description: In the last two minutes of close games the trailing team fouls to stop the clock, choosing who is fouled: poor free-throw shooters are targeted when the rule allows, and the leading team's ball handlers collect many attempts. The probability that a given player is a target depends on his free-throw percentage, his role as a ball handler and the margin and time left. This creates a right tail concentrated in close games and a hack-a-big regime for low-percentage shooters. Mid-game hack-a-player fouling away from the ball in Q1-Q3 is a separate, rarer route that depends on the opposing coach and the target's free-throw percentage and is carried as an extra bonus-state term.
stages.distribution: Conditional tail: in games within 6 points with two minutes left, attempts jump by 3-6 for ball handlers; the target rate depends on a threshold in FT% below about 60%.

stages.name: Per-attempt conversion skill
stages.description: Each attempt converts with the player's free-throw skill, which has a high signal-to-noise ratio: 200 attempts pin a rate to about 3 percentage points, and rates are persistent across seasons. For young or low-volume players the career-based estimate is noisy and informative priors come from other shooting (three-point, mid-range) and pre-NBA free-throw records. Within-game, makes are close to independent, so conditional on attempts the count is binomial.
stages.distribution: Binomial given attempts with p known to within about 3-5 points; variance largest at p near 0.5.

stages.name: Count distribution and threshold
stages.description: Making N free throws requires at least N attempts, so P(FTM >= N) = sum over attempts a >= N of P(attempts = a) times Binomial tail; the zero mass for low-volume players and the heavy right tail for stars at the line make the distribution far from normal. Settlement via the official box score is unlikely to be corrected often, but the half-point strike at integer counts means adjacent rungs differ by P(FTM = k).
stages.distribution: Mixture of a negative-binomial attempt distribution with a binomial thinning; mean 4-7 and sd 3-4 for high-volume players; zero-inflated for low-volume.

contract_review.settlement_definition: One live series, KXNBAFTM (rules text recovered). It settles Yes if the named player records N+ free throws made (integer 'N+' strikes, e.g. '5+') in the named game, identified by its original schedule date. If the player is active but never takes the court, the market settles to the last fair market price; once he enters, it settles on his number of made free throws, so zero makes after entering is a valid No. The text does not say whether overtime free throws count, whether technical or flagrant free throws are included, how stat corrections are handled, or what happens to a postponed or cancelled game; these are CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS (u1).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official box-score free-throws-made count for the named game (the rules name no source explicitly); stat-correction handling is not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction is 'N+' on an integer count, so the ladder is a survival curve P(FTM >= N) of a zero-inflated, binomially thinned attempt count; adjacent rungs differ by P(FTM = N).

An active player who never enters settles at the last fair market price; a player who enters for any time settles on his count, so a 2-minute injury exit is a No for any N >= 1 he has not reached. A player ruled inactive is not addressed by the text (only "active but never takes the court" is), see u1.

Overtime free throws (concentrated in intentional-foul end games) are not mentioned in the rules text; inclusion is likely because the settlement is the player's game count, but it is not stated (u1).
Technical, flagrant and clear-path free throws are box-score free throws made, but the text does not say they count (u1).
No protected variant exists for this series (unlike KXNBAASTPROT / KXNBAPRAPROT); a short appearance is fully at risk.
Postponement or cancellation handling is not in the sampled free-throw text (the game-level series use a 48-hour rule); treat as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS (u1).

player_milestones.label: NBA double-double / triple-double
player_milestones.target: Player records a double-double or triple-double
player_milestones.mechanism: Binary conjunction of count thresholds; probability depends on the joint distribution of points, rebounds and assists, each of which depends on minutes and role. The marginal probability for each component to hit 10 is highly sensitive to minutes and teammate availability; triple doubles are rare and dominated by high-assist bigs. Rules text defines the box score source and DNP treatment.

Minutes shortfalls kill the conjunction.
Joint stat distribution for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Dependence among components for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Rebound opportunities for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Assist opportunities for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Scoring component for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Blowouts reduce chance to reach 10 in the weakest component.
Teammates out raise assist or rebound counts selectively.
Own and teammates' status for NBA double-double / triple-double.
Price path and the timing of moves relative to injury-report vintages show what is already priced.
DNP/void and stat-source rules define the settled quantity.
Sportsbook prop line is the strongest prior on the mean and the disagreement is the edge.
Post-game stat corrections can flip a rung sitting exactly at the threshold, so settlement timing and source matter.
Opponent allowance by position shifts rebound and assist expectations toward or away from the milestone.
Pace scales every component of a double-double.
Lets the DD forecast respond correctly when a missing teammate changes which category pair is available (e.g. a guard's reb+ast path versus a big's pts+reb path).
DD is a threshold on cumulative production, so lost minutes from an in-game exit are not refunded; this tail is invisible in season-average minutes.

HYPOTHESIS ONLY, not a required input (see unresolved pm-stat-chase-size): Corrects the mechanical over-penalty of blowout branches for near-threshold players; sign is opposite to the naive minutes-cut story.
A DD for a center is gated by whether the second big plays beside or behind him; the existing frontcourt competition input is not attached to this archetype.
Double and triple doubles need 10+ in two or three categories, so minutes lost to a lead entering Q4 removes the final rebounds and assists; this is the market-free minutes-loss driver.
Gives the per-game playoff triple-double probability and its compounding over the run, the core of KXNBAPLAYOFF3D.
Converts series-length uncertainty and game-to-game absence persistence into the number of playoff games and minutes the named player gets.
Series length per round sets how many triple-double chances each round contributes to KXNBAPLAYOFF3D.
The named star must be healthy in each round to accrue games; his health also moves his team's advancement, coupling the two.
Playoff minutes inflation and shorter rotations change rebound and assist shares, so regular-season TD rates must be re-based.
KXNBAPLAYOFF3D exposure is the number of playoff games the team plays, read from the shared bracket paths.

interactions.hypothesis: Double-double probability has a steep threshold in minutes; blowout risk reduces probability disproportionately.
A big who creates (high assists) has TD probability driven by both opportunity counts; shooters rarely get a third category.
Teammate absences can push a player over a threshold; historical rates in similar absence scenarios beat season averages.

DD probability is nearly flat above ~34 minutes and falls steeply below ~26, so a blowout that trims a starter from 35 to 28 minutes costs far more than one trimming 38 to 33; the effect is largest for players whose second category is marginal (rebounds around 8).
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(DD) against projected minutes in 3-minute bins separately for blowout-probability terciles; look for a kink near 28-30 minutes that differs by tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: A center's rebound chances are shared with the other big only when both are on the floor, so the same rebound pool yields different counts depending on the fraction of minutes spent paired versus alone; direction is positive for the survivor when the co-big is out.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare a center's DD rate in games with vs without each frequent co-big (matched on minutes, opponent pace) and test against the lineup-weighted share prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: A fast game raises misses, possessions and assist chances together, which fattens the joint upper tail of rebounds and points more than the marginals alone; this correlates the two required components of a pts+reb DD and increases conjunction probability beyond the product of marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(pts>=10 and reb>=10) versus the product of marginals by opponent-pair pace tercile; the excess ratio should rise with pace.

interactions.hypothesis: A designated player is in one of two regimes: normal-load or limited/returning; in the latter the exit hazard and minute cap shift probability mass to very short appearances which settle NO, and the voiding rule does not help.
interactions.how_to_test: Split historical entries by pregame status vintage and compare the fraction of games with <55% of expected minutes and the resulting DD rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Inside the blowout branch, a player at 9 in a category late is more likely than his per-minute rate implies to finish, because teammates funnel the last opportunity; this partially offsets the minutes loss, in the direction opposite to the naive blowout penalty.
interactions.how_to_test: Among decided games, regress P(reach 10) from count 8-9 entering the last 8 minutes on baseline per-minute rate and a stat-chase coach indicator.

interactions.hypothesis: The playoff triple-double probability compounds a per-game rate over a random number of games: doubling expected games less than doubles P(YES) for high-rate creators, but nearly doubles it for occasional triple-double players, so advancement matters most for the long shots.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised playoff triple-double incidence by player rate bucket against 1 - (1-p)^G versus the linear p x G approximation across 15 playoff seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped/saturating: steep between ~24 and ~34 projected minutes then flat
nonlinearities.why: The count window for every category scales with minutes but the ten-count threshold turns a linear mean into a sigmoid probability; extra minutes beyond 36 add little for a player who already clears 10 in one category.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in per-minute category rate near the threshold
nonlinearities.why: A per-minute rebound rate that implies a mean of 8.5 versus 10.5 in 34 minutes changes P(>=10) from ~35% to ~60%; conjunction of two such events makes the DD probability convex in each category mean.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold: little effect below ~15% blowout probability, steep above ~35%
nonlinearities.why: Starters' minutes are cut only when the margin crosses ~15-20 with a few minutes left, so blowout probability matters mostly in the tail; the effect is non-linear in the team-rating gap.

mechanism_review.summary: A double or triple double is a conjunction over counting categories, each of which is (minutes on court) x (per-minute opportunity rate) x (conversion), so the event is the upper tail of a jointly distributed vector with a common minutes factor. The chain is: does he enter and how long does he stay (scenario mixture: normal starter load, blowout cut, foul trouble, in-game exit, overtime), which teammates share the floor (which determines board and assist shares), how many possessions occur (pace), the per-category counts conditional on minutes with the right dependence structure (positive through minutes and pace, negative between a guard's scoring and passing), the discreteness of crossing exactly ten, and settlement by official box score. Because a rare binary event is driven by a few tail scenarios, scenario weights and the choice of category pair matter more than season-average per-game stats.

stages.name: Entry and early-exit truncation
stages.description: The market voids inactive or never-entered players, so participation only matters conditional on entering; but once he enters the contract settles on whatever he accumulates. The relevant first stage is therefore the probability mass on very short appearances: a questionable player on a minutes restriction, a player who rolls an ankle in the first quarter, an ejection or early foul-out. These branches deliver a near-zero chance of a DD and are priced as part of a normal game by anyone using average minutes.
stages.distribution: Mixture: majority mass at normal rotation minutes, a small discrete mass (a few percent, higher with injury designations) at under 15 minutes; not Gaussian.

stages.name: Minutes scenario given game script
stages.description: Conditional on a normal game, minutes depend on the projected margin: blowout favorites cut starters' fourth quarters, close games push stars past 38 minutes, overtime adds about five. Foul trouble forces bench stretches in the first half. DD probability is steeply increasing in minutes between roughly 26 and 36 and then flattens, so the distribution of minutes (not its mean) sets the probability.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed with a heavy left tail for blowouts and a point mass bump at 40+ for OT/close games; minutes and absolute margin are strongly (negatively) dependent.

stages.name: Lineup-conditional opportunity shares
stages.description: Each category's opportunity count is a share of a team-level pool: rebound chances come from missed shots by both teams times the player's board share, which is lower when another big is on the floor; assist chances come from teammate made shots on passes, which are lower when the primary creator is on the floor beside him. Teammate absences therefore reallocate production unevenly across categories, which is what turns a 20% DD player into a 45% one when the co-big sits.
stages.distribution: Multinomial-style allocation: shares are bounded and negatively dependent among teammates; pool size (pace x misses) is overdispersed.

stages.name: Category counts and their dependence
stages.description: Within minutes bucket, points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks are discrete, overdispersed counts. They co-move positively through shared minutes and pace but trade off within player: a high-usage scorer's assists fall as shots rise. A DD needs two of them to clear ten, so the dependence structure (how often pts and reb are both high) matters as much as the marginals, and the category pair differs by player archetype.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed negative-binomial-like marginals with role-dependent correlation of roughly +0.2 to +0.35 between reb and pts for bigs and slightly negative between pts and ast for guards; discrete threshold at 10.

stages.name: Threshold crossing, stat credit and settlement
stages.description: The final count is the official box score. A player at 9 with a few possessions left is a discrete lottery; late-game teammate gifting, intentional fouling and OT affect this tail. Assist and block credit are assigned by scorers with arena-specific habits, and post-game corrections can move a count across the line. The contract voids only inactive players, so no void protects an early-exit case.
stages.distribution: Binary indicator on integer counts; probability mass concentrated at 8-10 counts so single-event credit decisions flip outcomes.

stages.name: Playoff-run exposure for the playoff triple-double series
stages.description: KXNBAPLAYOFF3D pays if one playoff game of the run contains a triple-double, so the opportunity set is the player's playoff games: none if his team misses or loses in the Play-In, four to seven per round reached, up to 28 for a finalist. Per-game triple-double probability rises in the playoffs because rotations shrink to eight or nine and stars gain two to four minutes, but pace drops and opponents scheme against the primary creator for a whole series. Star health hazard and advancement are positively linked: the team goes deeper when he is healthy, which is also when he accrues games.
stages.distribution: Games played G is lumpy on {0, 4..28}; P(YES) = 1 - E[prod_g (1 - p_g)], concave in G and close to p x E[G] for low-rate players; per-game rates are correlated within a series through matchup and role.

talent_strength.note: Player-level DD base rate and path-specific rates by minutes bucket carry the talent signal; team strength enters only through game script.

opponent_matchup.note: Positional allowance is weak; opposing frontcourt size and assist-suppressing schemes act mainly through the lineup-conditional shares.

role_personnel.note: Who shares the floor determines board and assist shares; this is the most important category for DD.

availability_news.note: Own and teammate status, plus the in-game exit hazard that the voiding rule does not refund.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach-specific rotation length and stat-chase tolerance in decided games.

environment.note: Altitude, arena and travel effects on a single player's DD probability are second-order and are only reachable through minutes and pace; no separate venue variable is justified for this contract.

game_context_script.note: Blowout and close-game minutes truncation and OT extension of the count window.

pace_volume.note: Possession count scales rebound pool and assist chances.

efficiency_conversion.note: Assist conversion depends on teammate shot-making (potential assists strip it); scoring efficiency matters little for reaching ten points.

distribution_variance.note: Joint overdispersed counts and tail co-occurrence are the core of the model.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Back-to-back and clinch/rest effects on minutes for individual stars are not represented by any input of this archetype and are folded into projected minutes without an explicit variable.

officiating_rules.note: Scorer credit for assists, rebounds and blocks and post-game corrections matter at the 9/10 boundary.

settlement_contract.note: Five-category definition, voiding rule and postponement window are in the sampled rules. KXNBAPLAYOFF3D is a union over playoff games with no fair-price void.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Two single-game forms and one playoff-long form. KXNBA2D/KXNBA3D: YES if the named player records 10 or more in two (double double) or three (triple double) of points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks in the named game (floor_strike 0.5, strike_type greater); inactive players, and active players who never take the court, settle at a fair price, and once the player enters the market settles on his actual statistics; a game postponed but starting within 48 hours stays open, otherwise fair price. KXNBAPLAYOFF3D: YES if the named player records at least one triple-double in any single playoff game of the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs; cumulative stats across games do not count, and the text states no fair-price void, so missed games simply remove chances. None of the texts says whether overtime statistics count; the single-game text is cut off before naming the source agency, and the playoff text does not say whether Play-In games are playoff games.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official game box score as reported by the sports data sources named in the full rules; the sampled rules_secondary is truncated before naming them, so the exact source agency and stat-correction policy are unverified (see unresolved).
variants_and_edge_cases: Triple double (KXNBA3D) requires three categories at >=10; same five-category list, same voiding text, but a far thinner positive class dominated by a handful of high-assist bigs and guards, so base-rate shrinkage matters more than any matchup variable.
Steals and blocks are valid categories, so a rim protector can complete a DD with points+blocks or a TD with reb+blk; the common 'pts/reb/ast' simplification misses these paths.

Overtime is not mentioned in the sampled text; 'in a single game' on the official box score ordinarily includes OT minutes, which adds roughly 5 minutes to starters in ~6% of games and shifts DD probability materially for players at 8-9.

Inactive or never-entered player settles at a fair price (not NO), so unconditional participation modelling is unnecessary but the conditional-on-entering distribution needs a left tail for early exits.

KXNBAPLAYOFF3D (rules read): 'Cumulative stats across multiple games will not be considered', so the event is 1 - E[prod over his playoff games (1 - p_game)]; the number of games is set by qualification and series advancement, per-game rates must be re-based on playoff minutes (+2-4 for stars) and pace, and the sampled text states no fair-price void for an injured or eliminated player. The sampled KXNBAPLAYOFF3D market (2026 playoffs) is finalized; later editions must be re-read for list, Play-In and void wording.

player_h2h_series_stats.label: Player head-to-head, series and Summer League player stats
player_h2h_series_stats.target: Player A vs player B stat comparison, series total/average, or Summer League player stat
player_h2h_series_stats.mechanism: Head-to-head compares two players' stat counts (difference distribution with positive correlation through game script), series stats accumulate across games with injury and minutes variance, and Summer League stats are driven by unstable rosters and minute plans. Each depends on the same player-stat drivers but the target is a difference or sum over games, so correlation and game-count uncertainty dominate.

The compared stat is often made threes (the only live head-to-head series is KXNBAH2H3PT), where three-point shooting luck dominates the variance of the difference and the tie mass; the regression of recent 3P% to talent gives the per-attempt rate.
Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_h2h_series_stats: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
Series leader markets need the probability of being the maximum among many players' series totals, which pairwise difference inputs do not give.
KXNBAPTSALLGAMES is a run of per-game threshold hits over a series that a missed game or cold night breaks, which is exactly the run-length process this input models.

interactions.hypothesis: Head-to-head between players on the same team is correlated via minutes and game flow; opposing players are correlated via pace.
Series total depends on number of games (sweep vs 7) and minutes tightening; sweep-prone series reduce totals.
Summer League minutes plans are announced late and capped; the distribution is bimodal for rookies.

The variance of a difference is var_A + var_B minus twice the covariance, so a positive correlation between opposing players narrows the distribution and raises tie probability, while a negative correlation between teammates widens it; the pair type reverses the effect of the same marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation by pair type and test calibration of P(tie) and P(A>B) on held-out pairs.

interactions.hypothesis: A series total is a sum over a random number of games, so a longer series disproportionately raises the upper tail; mean games enter linearly but sd of the total depends on the variance of game counts, which is larger for even matchups than for mismatches.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate series totals under different series length distributions and compare the upper-quantile differences.

interactions.hypothesis: If a star is lost for the rest of a series his total stops accumulating and the head-to-head may void; the probability of staying healthy across games declines multiplicatively with persistence, creating a threshold-like drop in total after the first injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a model of games played given injury status after game 1 and compare series totals with and without an injury.

interactions.hypothesis: The position-based allowance matters only if the assigned defender follows the position; when a coach assigns a wing stopper to a guard the position average is wrong, so the assignment overrides it.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predictions using position allowance versus assigned-defender allowance on past series.

interactions.hypothesis: A top pick plays a fraction of Summer League games with capped minutes, while a veteran plays all games with full minutes, so stat accumulation is a regime-dependent mixture that depends on the draft-slot bucket.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare per-game minutes and games played across draft-slot buckets for the last six Summer Leagues.

nonlinearities.shape: Discrete, right-skewed series length (4 to 7)
nonlinearities.why: The number of games has a lattice distribution that is bimodal for mismatches and concentrated at 6-7 for even teams, so linearising by an expected length misprices totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating minutes inflation near 40
nonlinearities.why: Playoff minutes for stars rise from about 35 to about 40 and cannot rise further, so the inflation factor saturates with role intensity.

nonlinearities.shape: Lattice with a tie mass at zero difference
nonlinearities.why: For low counts (threes, assists) the difference has a notable mass exactly at zero (about 12-20% for threes), so a continuous approximation underprices ties.

nonlinearities.shape: Bimodal minutes (capped versus full)
nonlinearities.why: Summer League minutes cluster at a cap for rookies and at a high value for veterans, so mean minutes are rarely observed.

mechanism_review.summary: The three variants share one structure: a comparison or accumulation of player-game counts where the quantity of interest is the distribution of a difference or a sum rather than a threshold on one count. For a head-to-head the difference X_A - X_B has a mean given by the two players' expected counts and a variance that depends on each count's variance and on their correlation, which differs by pair type: same-team players are negatively associated at fixed team output because they split the same shots, rebounds and assists, opposing players are positively associated through shared pace, and players in different games are independent. A tie is possible for integer counts and its probability depends on the discreteness. For a series, the sum runs over a random number of games (the series length is itself uncertain and depends on the team strengths), each game's minutes are inflated in the playoffs, injuries attrite exposure, and the games are not independent because opposing coaches adjust. Summer League adds unstable rosters, announced minute plans, and rookies who play a fraction of the games. So the key information is exposure (games and minutes), dependence between the two sides, and discreteness at ties. Two further live series types are not pairwise: a series stat leader is the maximum of many players' cumulative totals over a random number of shared games, and points in every game is a run of threshold hits that any cold night or missed game breaks (stage s6).

stages.name: Exposure: games played and presence of both players
stages.description: Both players must play for a comparison to be meaningful, and in a series the number of games played by each depends on series length, injuries and rest decisions. A star out for part of a series reduces his total; the head-to-head may void or favour the player who plays. Exposure is the product of the number of games in the series (random) and the probability of availability in each game (autocorrelated through injuries).
stages.distribution: Series length P(4,5,6,7) with mean about 5.7 for evenly matched teams and 4.8 for mismatches; availability per game with persistence across games.

stages.name: Minutes and role in each game
stages.description: For each player the minutes mixture defines how many opportunities he has; in the playoffs the rotation tightens and stars play 38-42 minutes, so per-game counts inflate relative to the regular season, while in Summer League minutes are set by a plan, rookies may be capped and veterans may be rested in back-to-back games. Minutes are correlated across the two players when they are teammates in the same blowout or in opposing teams in the same game flow.
stages.distribution: Truncated normal in the playoffs (sd 3-4 minutes) versus bimodal in Summer League (limited or full minutes); correlation of minutes between the two players depends on the pair type.

stages.name: Per-minute rates and the opponent assignment
stages.description: Per-minute stat rates come from the player's usage and role, adjusted for the opponent's defence by position and, in series, by the primary defender assigned to him; the playoff matchup assignments suppress or boost a star's counts in a way not visible in regular-season splits. Across games in a series coaches adjust coverage so the effect changes over the series.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed counts around a rate that is itself shifted by matchup assignments; matchup shifts of 5-15% of the stat in a series (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts and ties
stages.description: The difference distribution depends on the correlation of the two players' counts: for opposing players it is positive through pace and through shared game script, shrinking the difference variance; for teammates it is negative at fixed team output (one player's shot is not the other's) but positive through team pace, so the net sign depends on the stat. With integer counts, ties have positive probability, 12-20% for made threes and a bit lower for assists, and the tie rule matters.
stages.distribution: Difference of two overdispersed counts with correlation from about -0.2 (teammates, shot-based stats) to +0.3 (opponents, pace-driven stats); discrete with a mass at zero.

stages.name: Summer League and series settlement structure
stages.description: Summer League points ladders (KXNBASUMMERPTS, 'N+' in one game) hinge on roster churn, unannounced minute plans and game participation (top picks play two or three games, others play five), with a pre-game fair-price void if the player is active but does not enter; scoring rate is the rookie's or prospect's usage at Summer League level. For series totals (KXNBASERIESPTS) the settled quantity is the sum over all games the player enters in a random-length series, with overtime included and a void only if he enters none, so the pmf is a compound distribution over games played.
stages.distribution: Compound distribution (random games times random per-game counts); Summer League participation is a discrete choice with strong draft-slot dependence.

stages.name: Series leader maximum and every-game threshold runs
stages.description: Series leaders for points, rebounds, assists and made threes are the argmax of cumulative totals across both rosters over four to seven games, decided among the top producers by expected per-game rate times games played; ties pay 1/N, which matters most for made threes where top totals are small integers. Every-game runs (25+ points, 2+ threes) need the threshold in each game of a random-length series and any missed game is a No, so a longer series lowers them geometrically, a cold-shooting or foul-trouble night breaks them, and per-game hits are positively correlated through role and health; the threes run is much more fragile because per-game threes are low-count and overdispersed.
stages.distribution: Leader: categorical over about six serious candidates, sharper than a single-game leader because summing 4-7 games cuts noise. Every-game: product of correlated per-game Bernoullis over a 4-7 game random length, so mass falls roughly geometrically in series length.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eleven live series, all with recovered rules text. Player head-to-heads (KXNBAH2HPRA, KXNBAH2HPTS, KXNBAH2H3PT): Yes if player A records more of the stat than player B 'in the full game'; an exact tie with both players entering resolves 50/50; if either player does not enter, or the game is cancelled or postponed more than two weeks, fair price. Series totals (KXNBASERIESPTS): at least N points over the entire named series; regulation and overtime count; stats final at series end (later corrections ignored); a player who enters no game resolves to fair price. Every-game runs (KXNBAPTSALLGAMES 25+, KXNBA3PTALLGAMES 2+): the threshold must be met in every game of the series; a game not entered resolves the market No; overtime counts. Series leaders (KXNBASERIESPTSLEADER, REBLEADER, ASTLEADER, 3PMLEADER): Yes if the player records the most of the stat over the series; a player entering no game resolves to fair price; ties pay $1/N (rounded down to the cent) to Yes. Summer League (KXNBASUMMERPTS): N+ points in a named Summer League game; active but never entering settles at the last fair price before game start.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official box scores per game (NBA.com / NBA Summer League); series stats final at series conclusion per the rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: Head-to-head ties resolve 50/50 when both enter (PRA, points, threes); Skellam-type tie mass for made threes is about 12-20% at means of 2-5 each (Poisson arithmetic gives 13-21%, overdispersion lowers it), smaller for points and PRA.

Non-entry handling differs by series type: H2H fair price if either player does not enter; series total and leader fair price only if the player enters no game; every-game runs resolve No on any missed game.
Series-level stats are final at series end and later corrections are ignored; overtime counts in series totals and every-game runs; H2H says 'full game' (overtime implied, not stated).
Series length is random (4 to 7 games) and every game of the series counts, so totals rise and every-game runs fall with length.
Leader ties pay $1/N rounded down to the cent; the leader field is all players of both teams.
Summer League ladders are single-game 'N+' points with a pre-game fair-price void for active non-participants; minute plans and participation choices dominate.

game_moneyline_spread.label: NBA game winner and point-spread markets
game_moneyline_spread.target: Team wins outright or covers a stated spread over the full game (OT included per rules text)
game_moneyline_spread.mechanism: Margin = sum over possessions of efficiency differences, shifted by home court, rest and, most importantly, who plays. Sharp closing lines are efficient on average, so model value comes from (1) availability changes between the injury-report vintage priced by Kalshi and the true scenario mixture, (2) regression of luck-contaminated ratings (3P%, close games), (3) variance shape (margin sd grows with spread; OT mass), and (4) Kalshi-specific stale quotes and rung inconsistencies in spread ladders.

Gives the second half of the absence cost; the player_impact input only covers the missing player's rating.
Without it, lineup_adj_rating and off/def ratings mix incompatible samples and over-credit healthy-roster results.

A margin sd off by one point moves a 6-10 point band by about 1.2 percentage points and P(win) by about 1.4 points at a 6-point mean margin (sd 12 versus 13), so sd matters but far less than a 3-4 point rung error.
Series-level markets in this archetype have no mechanism in the draft; the random effect sets the correlation of outcomes between games.
Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.

interactions.hypothesis: Value of a questionable star is asymmetric: a mixture over play/no-play must be priced, and the quote may reflect one branch.
Back-to-back effect operates mainly through star rest; fit the direct effect after controlling for availability.
A defense with lucky opponent 3P% allowed is overrated in raw defensive rating; regress toward shot-quality allowed.
Large spreads change margin variance; at -12 and beyond cover probability depends on late bench minutes.
Teams with seeding locked and stars resting create unusually uncertain rosters.

A questionable star creates a two-point mixture whose mean differs by several points, so the market price may match only one branch; with two questionable players the branches multiply and the cost is non-additive, so the mixture cannot be reduced to an expected rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the model probability as a mixture and compare to using the expected rating; test on nights with two or more questionable starters.

interactions.hypothesis: The back-to-back effect is mostly a star-rest effect; conditional on all stars playing, the direct fatigue effect on margin is small (around a point) and larger for older rosters.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress margin residual on back-to-back with and without controlling for the active-set rating; test an age-by-b2b term.

interactions.hypothesis: Cover probability at a given spread depends on mean/sd, and sd rises with pace and total while the mean is set by ratings, so a fast game with a large favourite covers a wide spread less often than a slow game with the same mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate cover probabilities in a grid of (mean margin, sd) and compare to a constant-sd normal in out-of-sample games.

interactions.hypothesis: Rating correction for hot three-point shooting is proportional to the team's three-point attempt rate: a team with 45% of shots from three has more luck variance to remove than one with 30%.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether the regression coefficient of future margin on past 3P% residual scales with 3PA rate.

interactions.hypothesis: In a series, defensive scheme adjustments after game 2-3 reduce the offence's advantage, so a regular-season matchup edge decays across games; the effect is regime-dependent on whether the coach changes the coverage.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the matchup-edge coefficient by game number within series.

nonlinearities.shape: Probit link from expected margin to win probability
nonlinearities.why: P(win) = Φ(mean/sd) is concave in the favourite's mean margin above about 8 points, so a one-point rating error matters more for near-even games than for heavy favourites.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in number of missing rotation players
nonlinearities.why: The cost of each additional absence grows as depth runs out, so a linear sum of impacts understates multi-injury nights.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in rest days: large first back-to-back penalty, flat beyond 2 days
nonlinearities.why: A game on zero days' rest costs about a point, one day of rest nearly erases it, and extra days add little.

nonlinearities.shape: Local point mass at zero margin
nonlinearities.why: Regulation ties convert into overtime and a margin of a few points, producing a spike in the density just around zero that a continuous normal misses.

mechanism_review.summary: A moneyline or spread market is a statement about the distribution of the final margin D = Score_home - Score_away, which is a sum over roughly 200 possessions of efficiency differences plus home court, rest and who is actually on the floor. The mean of D is the difference of two active-roster ratings, so the first-order question is which players play and how many minutes their replacements absorb; the second is how much of each team's rating is luck (three-point shooting, close-game record) rather than ability; the third is matchup and scheme, which moves efficiency at equal ratings; and the fourth is the variance shape, because the margin sd (about 12) depends on pace and totals and the cover probability depends on the sd as much as on the mean. P(win) = P(D>0) including overtime, and the spread ladder is a set of cut points on one density, so rung probabilities must be monotone. Information arrives in discrete bursts (injury report, starters, reporter tweets), and many edges are timing edges around those bursts, not rating edges.

stages.name: Active set and minutes redistribution
stages.description: Margin starts with who plays: each team's active set is a mixture over star in/out scenarios when statuses are questionable, and an absence moves minutes to replacements of a different quality, so the loss is not the star's rating but the gap between star and the marginal replacement times the minutes absorbed. Two absences are not additive because bench depth is exhausted and rotation changes (a thin guard rotation compresses the replacement quality).
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario mixture with 2-4 branches per team; conditional on branch, margin is approximately normal. Absence cost is convex in the number of missing starters.

stages.name: Baseline team strength with luck regression
stages.description: The base rating is an opponent-adjusted offence and defence estimate whose window and shrinkage decide how much recent form is credited. Rating built from games with different rosters is contaminated, so the weight of each past game should reflect how similar its active set was to tonight's. Three-point shooting on both sides and close-game record are only partly skill, so raw ratings must be pulled toward shot-quality-based expectations.
stages.distribution: Rating estimates carry sd of roughly 1.5-2.5 points of margin early in the season, shrinking with games; luck components regress by a large fraction within 20 games.

stages.name: Matchup, scheme and venue
stages.description: At equal ratings, scheme interactions matter: a drop-coverage defence against a pick-and-roll-heavy offence, a team that lives on threes against a switching defence, and rim protection against rim-attack teams change efficiency. Home court adds roughly two points on average, with larger effects at altitude, and with rest and travel adjustments applying to both teams. In the playoffs the star-versus-defender match-ups gain weight because rotations tighten.
stages.distribution: Additive shifts on the margin mean of about 0-3 points; scheme interactions have small sd across opponents and are weakly identified.

stages.name: Motivation and series state
stages.description: Late-season stakes (clinched seed, tanking, seeding races) change who plays and with what effort, while in a playoff series games are not independent: coaching adjustments, injuries accumulating and the pressure of elimination shift the margin from game to game. For a single playoff game priced here, the series state (elimination, a game after a blowout loss, home/away swing) conditions that game's margin mean.
stages.distribution: Regime change in availability late in the season; series-level correlation between games of a few points of margin.

stages.name: Margin distribution and settlement transform
stages.description: The final margin is approximately normal with sd 11-13 but with lump near zero from overtime (tied regulation adds 5 minutes) and fat tails from garbage-time collapse; sd scales with pace and total, so a high-total game has a wider margin distribution at the same mean. P(win) and spread cover are the same density evaluated at different cut points, and win-margin bands are differences between them, so a single density must be consistent across all these markets.
stages.distribution: Mixture of a normal body, an OT-induced local mass near zero and heavier tails when a team is a heavy favourite; heteroscedastic in pace/total.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Two live series, both with recovered rules text. KXNBAGAME settles Yes if the named team wins the named game (identified by its original schedule date). KXNBASPREAD settles Yes if the named team 'wins by more than X.5 points' in the named game; strikes are half-points (e.g. 37.5), so no push exists and the ladder runs to extreme margins for each team. Both: a game postponed but begun within 48 hours settles on the official final result; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price. NBA games cannot end tied, so the winner market includes overtime; the spread text settles on the 'official final result' but does not say explicitly that overtime points count toward the margin (u1).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game (the rules' wording); NBA.com game summary / box score as the practical source.
variants_and_edge_cases: Scope after reconciliation: only the single-game winner (KXNBAGAME) and spread (KXNBASPREAD) series are filed here; series-state, Cup-group, head-to-head and win-margin tickers belong to other archetypes.

Spread strikes are half-points ('wins by more than 37.5'), so no push; each team carries its own one-sided ladder and P(team A wins by > x) for x < 0 is not offered as such, so the two teams' ladders together trace one margin CDF.
Cup (in-season tournament) games and play-in games count as ordinary games for margin, but the Cup final is a separate game for some other props, so the specific game identity matters.

Scope: every input in this record is pregame-knowable. The game markets trade live, but in-play state (score, clock, fouls, lineup on court) is out of scope here and needs its own state-conditioned model.

game_win_margin.label: NBA winning-margin buckets
game_win_margin.target: Winning team and margin bucket (e.g. 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16+) at settlement including OT per rules
game_win_margin.mechanism: Bucketed margin outcomes are a discretization of the margin distribution: mean from the availability-adjusted spread, shape from empirical residual (sd 11-12, fatter tails for lopsided matchups), plus OT effect that collapses ties to a 1-3 point margin. Bucket edges and inclusivity are rules-driven. Value exists where buckets are priced as independent while they must sum to a coherent distribution.

Lowest bands (1-5) get a sizeable share from OT that a Gaussian misses.

Three-point shooting luck is a large share of single-game margin variance and of the regression of team rating; it is a rating-correction input here, not a band driver by itself.
Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in game_win_margin: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.
Market-free probability that regulation ends tied, from the own-model margin mean and sd with an integer-pmf excess at zero; needed because overtime changes the settled quantity.

interactions.hypothesis: Final-margin pmf has structure from late free throws that shift 1-3 point finishes to 4-6; empirical mass should be used rather than smooth normals.
Bench lineups in garbage time compress margins; the amount depends on coach and bench quality.
OT converts ties into 1-5 point margins; the lowest bucket gets mass beyond smooth models.

A band probability is a CDF difference (mu-b)/sigma, so errors in sigma and in mu multiply: when the mean is near a band's centre, sigma matters more than mu, but for a band two sds away mu matters more.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the sensitivity of band probabilities to sigma and mu on a grid and identify where each error dominates.

interactions.hypothesis: Once the lead exceeds about 15 with under six minutes left the starters leave and the margin drifts rather than grows; the effect of an extra point of lead on the final margin falls from about one to about 0.5 beyond the threshold.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress final margin on margin at 6:00 with a hinge at 15 and compare slope above and below.

interactions.hypothesis: The drift after the pull depends on the second-unit gap: a leading team with the stronger bench keeps its lead, otherwise it shrinks; the sign is conditional on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Group blowouts by the second-unit gap tercile and compare mean change of margin after pull.

interactions.hypothesis: In the regime where regulation ties (3-6% of games) the final margin follows the folded OT density, which is concentrated in 1-8; the lowest bands are a mixture of regulation and OT regimes and the mixture weight falls with spread.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the mixture with mixture weight as a function of own-model spread and compare log loss against a single density.

interactions.hypothesis: In a faster game there are more possessions in the final two minutes, so the late-foul sequences take more time and add margins in 4-8 points; pmf spikes become less pronounced as pace rises.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast the final-margin pmf at 1-8 points in the top versus bottom pace tercile in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Slope falls from 1 to about 0.5 beyond a 15-point lead at 6:00
nonlinearities.why: Coaches pull starters when a lead is large; additional lead points are given back by bench play, so the final margin is a concave function of the late margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Non-smooth with parity spikes and a zero hole
nonlinearities.why: Integer margins show relative deviations from a smooth density by up to 10-20% at margins 1-8, which determine band edges at 5/6 and 10/11. The 10-20% size is recalled, not measured (u2).

nonlinearities.shape: Heteroscedastic: sd grows with favourite size and pace
nonlinearities.why: Wider spreads have larger sd (heavy tail of blowouts), so band probabilities on the favourite side spread out more than a constant-sd model implies.

mechanism_review.summary: A winning-margin band is the probability that the final signed margin falls in a closed integer interval on one side, so the contract is a histogram of one density, not a binary on the mean. The density has four structural features beyond a normal with mean mu and sd sigma: a hole at zero (no ties, so regulation ties move to overtime), a bump at small positive margins from overtime outcomes (final margin after OT is typically 1-8), late-game compression when the trailing team fouls and the leading team keeps the lead at small values, and compression after starters are pulled in blowouts where bench units trim or inflate the margin depending on the second unit's strength. The sum across all bands and both sides must be exactly one, and the middle bands are driven by sigma more than by mu; a band such as 6-10 is the difference of two CDF values, so sigma errors enter directly. The informative inputs are therefore the mean margin from the active-set ratings, the heteroscedastic sd and the empirical shape corrections, in that order.

stages.name: Signed-margin mean and variance
stages.description: The mean of the signed margin comes from the difference of the active-set ratings plus home court, and its sd is about 11-13 and rises with pace and with favourite size. The band probabilities are far more sensitive to sd than win probability is: at mean 6 a one-point change in sd (12 versus 13) moves the 6-10 band by about 1.2 percentage points (16.3% to 15.0%) and P(win) by about 1.4 points, so band probabilities are sensitive to sd but not dramatically more than P(win). The mean uncertainty from questionable players is a mixture that fattens bands on the underdog side.
stages.distribution: Normal body with sd 11-13, heteroscedastic; scenario mixture over star status gives a bimodal signed-margin density before pooling.

stages.name: Final-minutes compression and parity
stages.description: In the last two minutes the trailing team fouls and the leading team shoots free throws, so margins within about 8 points shift toward specific values (a made three moves a 4-point lead to 7, an intentional foul sequence ends at +2 to +6), and a ten-point-plus lead with a minute left is basically fixed. The pmf therefore has spikes and troughs by parity and key numbers (3, 6) that a smooth density does not reproduce. The strength of this effect depends on how often the game is close in the last minutes.
stages.distribution: Non-smooth pmf over margins 1-12 with parity structure; the spikes are about 10-20% relative deviations from the smooth density.

stages.name: Garbage-time margin decay
stages.description: When the lead is large (+15 or more) late in the fourth quarter, coaches pull starters and the bench trades baskets; the final margin is then the margin at the pull time plus a random walk whose drift depends on the relative quality of the two second units and on how early each coach pulls. Leads typically shrink a few points after starters sit, but a deep bench on the leading side can hold or extend the margin. This sets the shape of the 11-15 versus 16+ bands, not the middle bands.
stages.distribution: Margin after the pull: approximately a random walk with sd about 4 points over 6 minutes and drift of -1 to -3 points; strongly dependent on lead size at the time of the pull.

stages.name: Overtime conversion into low bands
stages.description: If the regulation score ties (about 3% from the smooth density and about 6% empirically) a five-minute period is played and the final margin is the OT margin, with a mean absolute value near 5.5 and nearly all outcomes between 1 and 10. This adds roughly 3 percentage points of mass to the 1-5 bands in total that a continuous density would assign elsewhere, and it matters most for bands near zero when the spread is small.
stages.distribution: Tie mass converted into a folded normal with sd about 7 (five minutes of scoring difference); dependence on |spread| through the tie probability.

stages.name: Band construction and coherence
stages.description: The market lists bands for each side, so the model must produce P(A wins by band b) for all bands and both teams and the sum must be one. Because each band is a difference of the CDF at its edges, the cut points near the median of the margin density are sensitive to bias in mu, while the open-ended top band is sensitive to the tail. Rungs priced independently by the market may violate the sum constraint or the unimodality of the density within a side. Coherence is enforced by construction: every band for both sides is integrated from the same own-model integer pmf, so the sum-to-one and unimodality constraints need no input derived from quoted prices (m.ladder_structure is only a benchmark diagnostic of stale quotes).
stages.distribution: Multinomial over 8-10 outcomes with a unimodal-per-side density; sum-to-one constraint couples all bands.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNBAWINMARGIN, now filed under this key after the reconciliation, settles Yes if the named team wins the named game by a margin inside a closed integer band; the sampled market is 'by 6 to 10 points', settled on the 'official final result' (stated in the postponement clause) with a fair-price void if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. The text never mentions overtime, so overtime inclusion is an inference (a regulation tie has no winner otherwise). Only the 6 to 10 band was observed: the other band edges (1-5, 11-15, 16+ in the ledger example), whether the top band is open-ended, and whether bands are listed for both sides are unverified.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game (league box score); overtime inclusion is inferred from 'official final result', not stated in the sampled rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: Per-side bands: the sampled market names the winning team (Brooklyn by 6 to 10), so each game has a set of mutually exclusive bands for each side whose probabilities must sum to one across both sides.
Closed integer bands (6 to 10 inclusive) mean margins of 5 and 11 fall outside; with NBA integer scores no push or gap exists between adjacent bands.

If overtime counts (inferred from "official final result"), every regulation tie converts into a final margin of typically 1-8 points, adding mass to the lowest band beyond what a smooth density gives; if it did not, a tied regulation score would have no winner, so the inference is strong but unstated.
Postponement within 48 hours still settles on the official final result; beyond that the market voids at fair price.

Whether the highest band is open-ended (16+ or 21+) is unseen; if open-ended, its mass depends on the heavy tail of blowouts and the tail input requirements change (nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve and margin decay dominate).

game_total.label: NBA full-game total points
game_total.target: Combined points over a half-point strike (OT included per rules text)
game_total.mechanism: Total = possessions x combined points per possession. Possessions depend on both teams' pace and lineups; efficiency on opponent-adjusted offense/defense, shot-making luck and free-throw volume. Late-game fouling and OT add tail mass; injuries to ball handlers and scorers shift both pace and efficiency. The sharp total is usually efficient, so value is in injury-scenario mixtures, luck regression and rung-level inconsistencies.

interactions.hypothesis: Totals fall more than additive when two slow, strong-defense teams meet because tempo is controlled by the slower team.
Missing a primary ball handler can slow pace while reducing efficiency; missing a rim protector can raise efficiency but not pace.
Offense inflated by recent hot 3P% overstates expected scoring; the correction is larger for teams with high 3PA.
Crew effect is concentrated in high-FTA offenses and in games with big-man foul trouble.
If OT is included, add expected OT points weighted by tie probability; wording must be matched per market.

Total equals possessions times combined points per possession, so a fast game between two efficient offences is multiplicatively larger than the sum of separate pace and efficiency effects; the cross term is about 1.5-2 points when both factors are one sd above average.

interactions.hypothesis: Missing a primary ball handler lowers pace and efficiency (total falls), while missing a rim protector raises opponent efficiency without changing pace (total rises); the sign depends on the missing role.
interactions.how_to_test: Group games by missing player role and compare residual totals; verify opposite signs.

interactions.hypothesis: Crew whistle tendency matters most for teams that live at the line: a high-foul crew adds free-throw points proportional to both teams' free-throw rate, so the crew effect on total is larger when both offences draw many fouls.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact crew foul index with the sum of both teams' FTA rate and test the slope.

interactions.hypothesis: A hot three-point streak is more likely to be luck for a high-3PA team (larger noise per game), so regression is heavier for those teams and the variance load is also larger; direction: shrink recent offence more when volume is high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-game total residual on last-10 3P% residual interacted with 3PA rate.

interactions.hypothesis: Close games produce both late-fouling free-throw points and OT, so the extra points are positively correlated within the same games; the upper tail of the total is generated by close games more than by high-pace blowouts.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition total residuals on final margin buckets and compare tail mass of high rungs in close vs non-close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance increasing in 3PA, sd scales with sqrt(attempts)
nonlinearities.why: The sd of the total rises with the number of threes (9p(1-p) per attempt), so rung probabilities away from the mean are sensitive to shot mix.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at margin within about 8 points in the last 2 minutes
nonlinearities.why: Intentional fouling begins when a game is within a possession or two; adds 4-10 points only in that state, a switch rather than a slope in the margin.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture adding a fixed block to the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: The regulation total plus a 24-point OT block in 6% of games creates a bump to the right of the median that a normal misses.

nonlinearities.shape: Sub-linear in the slower team's pace
nonlinearities.why: If the slow team partially controls tempo, game pace responds less than one-for-one to the faster team's tempo, so the average of paces overstates the effect of the fast side.

mechanism_review.summary: A game total is points = possessions times combined points per possession, so the process has two multiplicative factors and one additive tail. Possessions come from the interaction of two teams' preferred tempos (pace is neither the average nor the slower team's pace, it depends on transition frequency, turnovers and who pushes after makes or misses), reduced by dead-ball time from fouls and free throws. Points per possession depend on each offence against the other's defence for the actual rotation, including who is out (a missing ball handler slows pace and lowers efficiency, a missing rim protector raises efficiency without changing pace), plus free-throw volume driven by foul rates and the officials. Three-point shooting variance is the dominant noise source so the game-level sd of about 17-19 points is heteroscedastic: higher for teams that attempt many threes. Close games add late-game fouling free throws, blowouts shorten starters' minutes, and overtime adds about 24 points in about 6% of games. The settled event is one integer sum against a half-point strike.

stages.name: Possession count from two tempos
stages.description: Game possessions are not the average of the teams' season paces; they depend on offensive transition rate, turnover and steal rates, missed-shot rebound speed and the opponent's own tempo response, plus dead-ball events (fouls, timeouts). A slow, half-court team can slow a fast opponent, but evidence that the slower team fully controls pace is mixed, so the composition rule must be estimated rather than assumed. Pace has a game-to-game sd of about 3 possessions.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal with sd of 3-4 possessions around the composed mean, with weak dependence on the game state (garbage time slightly slower or faster depending on bench).

stages.name: Active-set efficiency of both offences
stages.description: Each offence's points per possession depends on shot quality against the specific defence and on who plays; absences affect pace and efficiency differently by role (a lead ball handler out lowers assist-generated shots and pace, a rim protector out raises the opponent's rim efficiency). The relevant baseline is opponent-adjusted offence and defence separately, not net rating, because a total depends on the sum of both teams' offences rather than their difference.
stages.distribution: Normal with sd about 1.5-2.5 points per 100 possessions around the estimated rating; scenario mixture when key players are questionable.

stages.name: Shot-making noise and its volume dependence
stages.description: Game-level variance is dominated by three-point makes: each three has Bernoulli variance 9p(1-p), so a team taking 45 threes contributes much more variance than one taking 25, and the variance of the total rises with both teams' 3PA. Hot shooting regresses to talent and shot quality, so recent results must be shrunk, and the shrinkage is stronger for defences' opponent 3P%.
stages.distribution: Sum of Bernoulli/binomial shot outcomes: total sd roughly sqrt(var of 2s + var of 3s + var of FT) of about 14, plus possession and rating uncertainty giving 17-19; heteroscedastic in 3PA.

stages.name: Free-throw volume and late-game structure
stages.description: Free throws add points through foul rates (offensive drive rate, defensive contact), the officiating crew's whistle tendency and late-game fouling in close games. When the margin is within about 8 points in the last two minutes, the trailing team fouls and total points rise by 4-10; in blowouts the late phase has no intentional fouls and benches play, which reduces scoring pace for some teams and increases it for others.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed in close games (extra FT tail), compressed in blowouts; crew effect about +/-3 points in total at the extremes.

stages.name: Overtime block added to the total
stages.description: Regulation ends tied with a probability that falls as the own-model expected margin grows (nba.reg_tie_pmf_model), and each overtime period then adds a block of combined points (recalled mean about 20-24, sd about 8) with a small chance of further periods (nba.ot_period_distribution). Because the block is added on top of a near-median regulation total, a strict over near the line gains a few percentage points from OT, more in close, slow games where the tie probability is highest; a total line far from the median barely moves.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation total with weight 1 - P(OT), plus a right-shifted component (one or more 5-minute blocks) with weight P(OT); the OT component is lumpy because periods are discrete.

contract_review.settlement_definition: The sampled full-game total (KXNBATOTAL) settles Yes if the combined points in the named game exceed a half-point strike (floor_strike 274.5 for 'over 274.5 total points'), so no push is possible; the secondary text settles on the official final result for a game that starts within 48 hours of schedule and resolves to a fair price if the game is cancelled or not started within 48 hours. The wording says 'total points are scored in the ... game' without carving out overtime, so overtime is counted by default but is not explicitly stated. KXNBATOTAL is the only live series under this key.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final score of the game (league box score), including overtime unless the full rule text excludes it.
variants_and_edge_cases: Single live variant: the regular-season and playoff full-game combined points total (KXNBATOTAL); no Summer League or series-length total is filed here.

Overtime: the rule text says 'total points are scored in the ... game'; a game with one overtime adds about 24 points, so P(over) near the line rises materially when OT is included; inclusion is plausible but not stated.
Strike spacing: rungs are half-point lines, and the ladder is a survival function of a discrete integer sum, so adjacent rungs differ by P(total = k).
Postponement and cancellation: a cancelled or non-started game resolves to fair price rather than No, which affects only edge accounting.

team_total.label: NBA team total points
team_total.target: One named team's points over a half-point strike (OT included per rules text)
team_total.mechanism: Team points = own possessions x own efficiency against the opponent's defense; dependent on the team's pace and on the game's margin (favorites' points reduced by garbage time, underdogs' points raised by late fouling). Injuries to the team's scorers and to the opponent's defenders move the team total directly; the market's team totals are derived from total and spread, leaving potential inconsistency across the three markets.
