The return market is a CDF of recovery time and cannot be read from a status label.
A season-long one-three market is exposed to the attempt rate of a non-shooter and the number of games, a combination absent from the current input list.
The market is a single decision with an info set that is preseason only; the draft's starter probability input does not specify its sources.
Next-team markets are multinomial and the feasibility screen removes impossible teams before probabilities are assigned.
Play-together markets are about the joint presence of two players, not each one alone.
Gives the signing-then-appearance probability for KXNBACOMPETE.

interactions.hypothesis: Same label implies different play probability by age, injury type and back-to-back; calibrate rather than reading labels.
Reporter lineup tweets precede official confirmation; source reliability should weight updates.
Dead rubbers on the second night of a back-to-back have high rest probability for veterans.

The recovery CDF depends on the injury category and on the team's pattern of reporting; once a player is listed as 're-evaluated in two weeks' the median is later than two weeks, and hazard depends on whether the first date was an initial or an updated timeline.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the ratio of actual to reported timeline by injury category and by report type in historical data.

interactions.hypothesis: KXNBACOMPETE needs a signing and then a regular-season second on court, so P(Yes) sums over signing dates of the signing hazard times the probability the coach uses him in one of the games left; a mid-season injury-replacement signing nearly always plays, while a late buyout-market signing onto a deep contender may sit for weeks, so the second factor is low exactly when the first spikes.
interactions.how_to_test: For unsigned veterans who signed mid-season over 10 seasons, regress days from signing to first regular-season appearance on team depth at his position and signing type (10-day, rest-of-season, buyout).

interactions.hypothesis: The preseason starter signal matters only for contested spots; for an incumbent star the signal is weak but for a battle between two players the last preseason starts are decisive, so the information value is conditional on the competition.
interactions.how_to_test: Test predictive power of preseason starts separately for incumbent and contested positions.

interactions.hypothesis: Team rest decisions are shared, so two stars tend to sit together on back-to-backs; the joint availability has a covariance beyond independence, reducing co-appearance relative to the product for a pair on the same team with a rest-heavy coach.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho from pair data and compare observed co-appearance counts to the product of marginals.

interactions.hypothesis: A reported destination from a reliable source moves probability only if the feasibility screen passes; a rumor to an infeasible team (no cap room, no matching assets) has probability near zero regardless of source credibility.
interactions.how_to_test: Examine historical rumours to teams that failed the feasibility screen versus those that passed.

interactions.hypothesis: A late-playoff return window pays only if the team is still playing when the player is cleared, so the recovery probability is multiplied by team survival game by game; a player with a 70% chance of being ready by the conference finals is worth much less on a team that is an underdog to get there.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate team series survival and recovery jointly and compare with the naive recovery-only probability on historical late-playoff injury returns.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise hazard with bumps at camp, injury waves and the buyout window, value decaying with signing date
nonlinearities.why: A signing is worth less the later it comes because fewer regular-season games remain for the one-second appearance, and the hazard itself is concentrated in a few calendar windows, so a constant monthly signing rate misprices both early and late in the season.

nonlinearities.shape: Weibull with shape above one and a right tail
nonlinearities.why: Return probability is near zero before the minimum timeline, climbs around the median and keeps a long tail from setbacks; a linear interpolation between the stated date and zero misprices.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in the preseason signal score
nonlinearities.why: Starter probability moves slowly for strongly incumbent players and quickly in contested competitions; the response is steepest near an even contest.

nonlinearities.shape: Step by status label
nonlinearities.why: Probability to play is near zero (well under 5%) for Out, roughly 0.05-0.25 for Doubtful, about 0.4-0.6 for Questionable, and above 0.9 for Probable; the step structure is not linear in a numeric status code (approximate values SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

mechanism_review.summary: These markets ask whether a player will be present in a particular role or state, and the four live series are three different processes plus one unseen one. First-game starter (KXNBASTARTERS): a coach's discrete choice among a roster after training camp, constrained by health, a minutes plan and the team's lineup philosophy, settled by who is on the floor at the opening tip; information arrives in preseason lineups, camp reports and a pre-tip confirmation. Return (KXNBARETURN): an injury-recovery time-to-event that only pays if the team still has games inside the dated window, so recovery is multiplied by playoff survival game by game. Compete (KXNBACOMPETE, sampled for an unsigned veteran): a signing must happen first, then the coach must give him at least one second in a regular-season game, so it is a signing hazard times the regular-season games left after the signing. Play-together (KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER, title only): the overlap of two players' availability, positively correlated through shared team rest decisions. Across all of them the common ingredients are the injury status timeline, role decisions and exposure windows, and the sharp tails come from discrete decisions (a signing, a coach's lineup card, an elimination) rather than smooth rates. The rare-make accrual mechanism left this key with KXNBAONE3PT (now in season_stat_markets), and next-team transactions left with KXNBANEXTTEAM/KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF (now in off_court_events).

stages.name: Health state and recovery timeline
stages.description: Every variant begins with whether the player is healthy: a return market is a time-to-event on recovery with a published timeline and uncertainty, a starter market requires him to be healthy for the opener, and a compete market requires him to be fit enough to sign and appear in at least one regular-season game. Reported timelines are lower bounds more often than expected, setbacks occur in a fraction of cases, and restrictions after return reduce minutes. The hazard of recovery depends on the injury type and on the team's disclosure style.
stages.distribution: Time-to-event with Weibull-like shape: slow start, peak near the stated timeline, long right tail from setbacks; about 20-30% of returns slip beyond the first stated date (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Coach role decision and rotation
stages.description: For the starter market the coach chooses five from the roster given health, camp performance, lineup chemistry and the game-one opponent; incumbents start unless displaced by an addition, an injury or a strategic change (small-ball, defence-first). For the compete market a signed veteran still needs the coach to use him for one second in a regular-season game, which is likely but not certain for an end-of-bench signing, and for play-together markets the rotation determines whether two players share minutes. KXNBASTARTERS is itself a single-game contract (verified rules and API: start the team's first 2026-27 regular-season game and be on the floor at the opening tip; announced-but-not-starting resolves No), so the game-level starter mechanism is live inside this archetype once per season, consistent with the catalog label 'starting lineup / player availability'.
stages.distribution: Discrete choice over the roster with strong incumbency (starters last season retain the role about 80% of the time, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); role changes cluster in the off-season.

stages.name: Signing of an unsigned player (compete market)
stages.description: KXNBACOMPETE (sampled for Ben Simmons, an unsigned veteran) requires a regular-season appearance, so the player must first sign with an NBA team. That depends on his health and perceived value, on which teams have a roster spot and minimum-salary room, on the timing (pre-camp signings, mid-season injury-replacement signings, post-deadline buyout market) and on alternatives abroad. After signing, the coach must play him at least one second in a regular-season game. Next-team markets that once used this stage moved to off_court_events.
stages.distribution: Low-rate signing hazard over the season with bumps at training camp, injury waves and the buyout window; conditional on signing, appearance probability is high but not 1.

stages.name: Exposure window: team games available inside the window
stages.description: Return and compete markets need games to happen while the player is available. For KXNBARETURN the sampled window (May 28 to Jun 20) covers the conference finals and Finals, so the number of team games left is a random variable from series survival and length, and P(Yes) = sum over remaining games of P(team still playing that game) x P(recovered and used by then). For KXNBACOMPETE the exposure is the regular-season games left after a signing date. A player cleared one day after elimination resolves No.
stages.distribution: Product of a recovery time-to-event and a decreasing survival curve of team games; mass at zero when the team is eliminated early or the signing never happens.

stages.name: Joint presence and wording filters
stages.description: Play-together and starter markets depend on two or more players being simultaneously present or in specified roles, which makes the events correlated through team rest and injury policy. Wording filters (first regular-season game, on the floor at the tip, regular-season games only) set which observable counts. A single injured teammate or a coach's rest decision applies to both players, so joint presence is more variable than independent presence.
stages.distribution: Joint Bernoulli with positive dependence between rest decisions; regime effects when the stated window is short.

talent_strength.note: The core question is presence and role, not performance level; talent enters only through the coach's choice (who is better) which is covered by nba.starter_probability, and has no separate strength input for these markets.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent identity matters little for season-level or opening-night presence markets; the first-game starter market could depend on opponent size but no evidence supports a measurable effect.

role_personnel.note: Role and roster changes.

availability_news.note: Injury timeline and starter confirmation.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach rotation philosophy.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and travel do not drive these presence markets beyond the minor schedule fatigue effect handled in rest and load management inputs.

game_context_script.note: In-game script changes minutes but not whether a player starts, returns or appears for one second; the relevant game-level context is whether the team still has games in the window, which is carried in stage s4 by nba.series_model.

pace_volume.note: The only volume that matters is exposure: the number of team games inside the KXNBARETURN window (series survival and length) and the regular-season games left after a KXNBACOMPETE signing; no possession or attempt count enters any live contract.

efficiency_conversion.note: No live series settles on converting shots or opportunities: starter, return, compete and play-together outcomes are presence events, and the rare-three accrual that needed a make rate left with KXNBAONE3PT.

distribution_variance.note: Weibull-type recovery times with a setback tail, and positively correlated joint presence for the play-together pair.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Season-level rest and incentive effects work through nba.load_mgmt (rest and return-from-injury policy) and late-season nba.standings_motivation; daily back-to-back context (nba.rest_travel) is audited IRRELEVANT for these season-level and one-time markets and is no longer a stage or coverage input.

officiating_rules.note: Referee behaviour has no bearing on a player's role, return or destination; the only rule-like element is the exposure window (season type filter) handled under settlement.

settlement_contract.note: Rules text for starter (on floor at tip, announced-but-not-starting is No), return (enter a game for the team inside a dated window) and compete (any regular-season second; preseason/playoffs excluded); play-together is title only (u1).

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four live series; three have recovered rules text and KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER is TITLE_ONLY. KXNBASTARTERS: Yes only if the named player starts his team's first 2026-27 regular-season game and is on the floor at the opening tip; an announced starter who does not actually start resolves No; resolution is based solely on who starts that game, regardless of a retirement, signing or trade beforehand. KXNBARETURN: Yes if the named player enters a game for the named team inside a stated window (sampled: after May 28 and before Jun 20, 2026, i.e. late playoff rounds), so the team must still be playing. KXNBACOMPETE: Yes if the named player enters any 2026-27 regular-season NBA game for at least one second; preseason and playoff games do not count (sampled for an unsigned veteran, so a signing is required first). KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER: definition (same game versus shared minutes) is not visible (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official starting lineup and play-by-play (starter, entries), official box scores for appearances; rules name no explicit source.
variants_and_edge_cases: Clock mismatch within the key: first-game starter (one decision at opening night), return (enter a game for the named team inside a dated window), compete (any regular-season appearance across a season, for an unsigned player) and play together (title only) are different processes sharing one label.
Announced versus actual: the starter market resolves No if an announced starter does not take the floor at the tip, so confirmation 30 minutes before tip still leaves a small residual risk.

Return windows in late May and June fall in the conference finals and Finals: if the team is eliminated before the player is healthy, there are no games left and the market resolves No regardless of health.
Compete excludes preseason and playoff games and counts a single second of play; a signing late in the season with few games left sharply reduces exposure.
KXNBAPLAYTOGETHER has no rules text: whether 'together' means the same game or overlapping minutes, and the window, are unseen (u1).

season_futures_team.label: NBA team season futures (title, conference, division, wins, playoffs, seed, round reach)
season_futures_team.target: Team's season win total, seed, playoff/play-in qualification, round reached, conference/division/title
season_futures_team.mechanism: Probabilities come from a simulation: team ratings with uncertainty updated through the season, the remaining schedule with rest and home/away, injury scenarios for key players and the official tiebreaker/play-in structure; the playoffs add bracket path and series models with playoff-tightened rotations. Win-total and seed markets are sensitive to rating uncertainty and boundary effects; title odds are convex in star health. Market prices incorporate narratives; edges come from uncertainty handling, luck regression and rule boundaries.

Provides the quantified prior and its sd, which the existing rating input only asserts.
Converts the generic 'rating with uncertainty' into time-varying numbers for every season-level contract.
Needed for division winner, seed over/under and playoff qualifier contracts where ties decide outcomes at boundaries.

Converts star health into a probability mixture for the series simulation, which is what makes title odds convex. Role lowered to secondary: the 10-season injury history it needs is not available as a clean public dataset (sf-injury-data), so its reliability is unproven.
Required for KXNBAFINALSMVP, KXNBAWFINMVP, KXNBAEFINMVP and KXNBAMVPCHAMP contracts that sit in this archetype.
Without it the two viewership series in this archetype have no input list at all.

KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK is rules-verified here and has no run-length or tie-count input in this archetype; the same mechanism is defined under another id (nba.team_win_streak_hazard) in the unregistered counting-specials record and should be reconciled when the catalog is merged.
The social justice award and other panel-voted series in this archetype had no input; this gives them an explicit nominee and co-winner model and links series MVPs to the team simulation.
KXNBARECORD (worst record, rules-verified) depends on tanking and late-season rest by lottery-bound teams, which pulls their win probabilities below rating-implied values.
Maps seeds 7-10 into playoff qualification and exact 7/8 seeds for KXNBAPLAYOFF, KXNBASEED and KXNBAPIADVANCE; KXNBAPLAYIN and KXNBASEEDOU stop before it.
KXNBAH2HWINS, division races and the extreme-record contracts depend on how head-to-head games make two teams' totals negatively dependent.
Playoff-win ladders (KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS) count wins across series, which depend on series lengths, not only on advancement.
Cup group and knockout games count in the regular-season standings (the final does not) and shift rest and schedule density.

interactions.hypothesis: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability; model the mixture rather than the mean rating.
Seed boundaries depend on tiebreakers and the regress-to-margin rating; teams over-performing point differential are overpriced.
Star-heavy teams gain in the playoffs relative to deep teams; regular-season ratings understate them.
Rest-heavy stretches interact with stars' rest policy; the schedule changes games played by stars.
A trade changes both team strength and uncertainty, with a lag for integration of new players.

Title and conference probability are convex in team strength and in star availability: a healthy-star scenario multiplies title odds several-fold while the injured scenario nearly eliminates it, so the correct estimate is a mixture over star-health states, not the rating at the mean health.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability from a mixture over star-health states with that from average rating; check calibration on historical contenders.

interactions.hypothesis: Seed and division contracts flip at exact ties; teams within one win of a cutoff have probabilities controlled by the tiebreak ledger (head-to-head, division record), which is a discontinuous rule on top of continuous win totals.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the share of simulated seed outcomes decided by tiebreakers and the sensitivity to head-to-head ledger perturbations.

interactions.hypothesis: Early in the season the posterior is dominated by the prior; as games accumulate the weight shifts to results. The optimal weighting depends on roster continuity: teams with many new players update faster because the prior is less reliable.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest end-of-season margin against prior and current margin separately for high- and low-continuity teams.

interactions.hypothesis: Playoff rotation tightening raises star-heavy teams' strength in exactly the games that decide titles, so the bracket path matters differently for deep teams versus top-heavy ones; a bracket in which a deep team faces a star team early changes round probabilities beyond the rating difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate playoff net rating minus regular-season net rating by roster concentration and test its interaction with opponent type.

interactions.hypothesis: A trade changes team strength and uncertainty with a lag of 10-20 games because the integration of a new player lowers early effectiveness; the rating update should widen variance at the time of the trade and then narrow.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team net rating in games 1-10 versus 11-30 after a major trade relative to the player-impact prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: Once a team is out of Play-In contention its incentive flips toward lottery position, and its late-season win probability drops below the rating-implied value; the worst-record contract is decided in this regime, so simulating the last 15-20 games with regular-season ratings overstates the weakest teams' wins.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rating-implied and realised win rates over the last 20 games for teams eliminated from Play-In contention, over 10 seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Playoff qualification is near-certain for seeds 1-6, roughly 55-75% for seeds 7-8 and 20-35% for seeds 9-10 through the Play-In, and zero below; P(KXNBAPLAYOFF) is therefore a piecewise function of the simulated seed distribution with jumps at 6/7 and 10/11, while KXNBAPLAYIN is an indicator of seeds 7-10.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate realised qualification by pre-Play-In seed since the Play-In began and compare with simulated piecewise probabilities.

interactions.hypothesis: Two teams that meet three or four times have negatively dependent win totals, which raises the variance of their difference and lowers the chance of equal wins relative to independent draws; KXNBAH2HWINS and division titles both sit on that difference.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated equal-wins frequency for pairs with 4 versus 2 meetings against historical pairs over 10 seasons.

nonlinearities.shape: steep S-shape: series win probability versus per-game win probability
nonlinearities.why: Per-game probability of 55% gives about 61% series, 60% gives about 71% and 65% gives about 80%, so small rating differences are amplified by the best-of-seven structure.

nonlinearities.shape: logistic around threshold-like contracts: P(60+ wins) as a function of mean wins
nonlinearities.why: With a win-total sd of about 6-7 the probability of reaching 60 moves from about 5% at 52 expected wins to 50% at 60 wins, and the slope is largest near the strike.

nonlinearities.shape: convex/mixture: title odds jump discretely when the star is healthy in the playoffs
nonlinearities.why: Title probability is not linear in expected games missed; it depends on a bimodal health state at playoff time, and losing the top star removes most title chance for a top-heavy team.

mechanism_review.summary: Season-level team contracts are functionals of a simulated season: a latent team strength (a prior from the roster plus in-season updates, with real uncertainty), the realized availability of its stars over the games and into the playoffs, the remaining schedule with home/away and rest, game results as correlated Bernoulli trials giving a Poisson-binomial win total, standings with official tiebreakers, two seed definitions around the Play-In, and then a playoff bracket of best-of-seven series with tightened rotations. Probabilities of rare outcomes (title, 72 wins, a Play-In team in the Conference Finals) are convex in uncertainty: errors in rating sd and star health matter more than error in the mean, and boundary effects at tiebreaks, seed cut points and the 1/N or 50/50 tie rules drive seed, division and record contracts. The MVP-champion conjunction and franchise-set champion contracts add functionals (a vote correlated with team success, sums over fixed franchise lists) on top of the bracket.

stages.name: Latent team strength: prior and in-season update
stages.description: True strength before the season is a roster-based prior (minutes-weighted player impact, aging, continuity, rookies), with an error sd of roughly 3-4 net rating points. Each game updates it with a gain that declines with games played; with ten games played the prior still dominates. Trades and coaching changes shift both mean and variance with a lag for integration.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior with sd about 2.5-3.5 net rating points early in the season shrinking with games; heavy tail for roster shocks (trades, injuries to stars).

stages.name: Availability of stars over the season and into the playoffs
stages.description: Stars miss a random number of games through injury and load management, with a heavy right tail of long absences; the quantity that matters differs by contract: expected games missed for win totals and seeds, probability of being healthy in April-June for round-reach and titles. Availability changes the team rating by a player-specific amount.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most players miss 5-15 games, a few percent miss most of the season; time-to-injury is a survival process with age and workload dependence.

stages.name: Schedule: opponent strength, rest and Cup games in the regular season
stages.description: The remaining schedule determines each game's win probability through opponent strength, home/away and rest asymmetry. Cup group and knockout games before the Cup final count as regular-season games (KXNBAPOSTASREC text) and teams eliminated early receive filler games scheduled later, so part of the schedule is unknown in November. Early in the season schedule effects are small next to rating uncertainty, but they matter for division races, 1 seeds and the final-weeks seed battle.
stages.distribution: Deterministic schedule given; game win probabilities range 15-85%; the rest/travel adjustments are about +/-1 point of margin.

stages.name: Regular-season win totals, extremes and pairwise records
stages.description: The win total is a sum of correlated game outcomes: independent Bernoulli noise (sd about 4.5 wins for an average team) plus common shocks through rating uncertainty and injuries, so the distribution is wider than a binomial. KXNBAMOSTWINS and KXNBAWINRECORD are upper-tail events of the best team (72+ or 74+ wins), KXNBARECORD is the minimum over 30 teams where lottery incentives make weak teams rest veterans late, KXNBAPOSTASREC is a maximum of partial-season percentages, and KXNBAH2HWINS is a difference of two totals linked by their head-to-head games, with the equal-wins mass paid at half.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial with a hierarchical shock (total sd about 6-7 wins); extreme-value behaviour for maxima and minima over 30 teams; integer ties paid 1/N or 50/50.

stages.name: Division titles, seeding, Play-In and playoff qualification
stages.description: Six division winners, conference 1 seeds and seed contracts are ranks of simulated records resolved by the official tiebreak hierarchy (head-to-head, division and conference records). Seeds 7-10 enter the Play-In (KXNBAPLAYIN), whose bracket decides playoff qualification (KXNBAPLAYOFF) and the exact 7 and 8 seeds (KXNBASEED), while KXNBASEEDOU stays on the pre-Play-In seed. Boundary probabilities hinge on one win and on the tiebreak ledger, and division titles carry no seeding reward, so late-season resting follows the conference table.
stages.distribution: Discrete rank outcomes with deterministic tiebreaks; the Play-In adds a three-game mini-bracket with per-game probabilities near 50% that maps seeds 7-10 to 7, 8 or out.

stages.name: Playoff bracket and series conversion
stages.description: Each series is a best-of-seven with home-court structure, playoff-tightened rotations and game-to-game correlation; per-game win probability converts steeply to series probability. The bracket path and star health in each round give conference-finals qualification, conference and league titles, the exact Finals pair, the playoff-win count (sum of wins over series reached, Play-In excluded) and whether a Play-In entrant reaches the Conference Finals; all are strongly convex in team strength.
stages.distribution: Series win probability is an S-shaped function of per-game edge (60% per game gives about 71% series); correlation between games from injuries and adjustments widens outcomes.

stages.name: Derived award and franchise-set functionals
stages.description: Two contract families sit on top of the bracket. The MVP-champion conjunction needs the regular-season MVP vote (a conditional choice among a few candidates whose odds rise with team record) joined to that player's team title probability, including his playoff health. Franchise-set contracts (first-time champion, no title in eight seasons, the three-peat) are sums or single terms of title probabilities over fixed lists, so their errors are the correlated errors of those teams' strength estimates.
stages.distribution: Conditional logit over MVP candidates joined to a title probability (strong positive dependence); sums of correlated team title probabilities for franchise sets.

availability_news.note: Season and playoff-time availability distribution.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes and playoff rotation tightening; only weakly quantified.

environment.note: Venue, altitude and arena effects are small at the season-aggregate level and are absorbed in home/away win probabilities within the schedule; no separate environment variable is warranted for futures.

game_context_script.note: Close-game luck and series dynamics (game-to-game correlation).

pace_volume.note: Possession count has no direct role at the season-futures level; it enters only through net rating, which already includes pace effects, so no separate pace or volume input is needed.

efficiency_conversion.note: Luck versus skill in point differential and records.

distribution_variance.note: Win-total, extreme-record and series distributions with rating uncertainty and head-to-head linkage.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule strength, rest and boundary-stakes.

officiating_rules.note: Format rules: tiebreak hierarchy, Play-In bracket and Cup games counted in the regular season.

settlement_contract.note: Per-series forms: integer win strikes, 1/N and 50/50 tie rules, tiebreak-decided divisions and seeds, pre- versus post-Play-In seeds, Play-In wins excluded, exact Finals pair, franchise lists and the MVP-title conjunction.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Thirty-two team-season series, 31 with rules text. Regular season: win totals (KXNBAWINS: at least N wins), any team to 72+ wins (KXNBAMOSTWINS), breaking the 73-win record (KXNBAWINRECORD, 2025-26 edition: more than 73 wins), more wins than a named rival (KXNBAH2HWINS: equal wins resolve 50/50), worst record (KXNBARECORD: ties by win-loss percentage at 1/N), best winning percentage to the All-Star break (KXNBAPOSTASREC: ties $1/N), six division winners (end-of-regular-season standings, ties by the league's official tiebreak rules, no split), conference 1 seeds at the end of the regular season, seed thresholds on the pre-Play-In seed (KXNBASEEDOU) versus exact seeds with 7 and 8 set by the Play-In (KXNBASEED), Play-In qualification and playoff qualification (Play-In qualification does not count). Postseason: conference-finals qualifiers, conference champions, champion, conference of the champion, exact Finals winner and runner-up (No if either team is eliminated from its role), playoff wins at least N (Play-In wins excluded), any Play-In team reaching the Conference Finals, three-peat, franchise-set champions (ten never-champions; teams without a title in 2018-19 to 2025-26) and the regular-season MVP's team winning the title. Regular-season series exclude preseason, Play-In, playoffs, the All-Star Game and the Cup final; Cup games before the final count. KXNBANEWCHAMP is TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league standings, tiebreak procedure, Play-In and playoff results, and league announcements for the champion and regular-season MVP; the sampled texts name no source agency.
variants_and_edge_cases: Three tie rules coexist: 1/N dead heat (KXNBARECORD worst record, KXNBAPOSTASREC best record at the break), 50/50 (KXNBAH2HWINS on equal wins) and the league tiebreak hierarchy with no split (division winners, 1 seeds, seeds); each needs integer-level win distributions, not means.

Two seed definitions: KXNBASEEDOU uses the seed before the Play-In (a 10 seed that enters as the 8 is still 10), KXNBASEED assigns 7 and 8 from the Play-In; KXNBAPLAYIN is qualification for the Play-In (seeds 7-10) and KXNBAPLAYOFF excludes it.

KXNBAWINS and KXNBAMOSTWINS use greater_or_equal integer strikes (no push); KXNBAWINRECORD needs more than 73 wins; KXNBAMOSTWINS is a maximum over 30 teams, so it is the upper tail of the best team, not of one named team.
KXNBAPOSTASREC compares winning percentage at the All-Star break (Feb 19, 2027) when teams have played different numbers of games; ties split 1/N.
KXNBAMVPCHAMP couples the regular-season MVP vote with the title, and the dependence is strong because voters reward team success; it is not a Finals MVP contract.

Franchise-set contracts (KXNBAFIRSTTIMECHAMP, KXNBANEWCHAMPION) are sums of title probabilities over fixed lists; KXNBANEWCHAMPION lists New York as 2025-26 champion, which also means the Oklahoma City three-peat (KXNBA3PEAT, 2024-25 to 2026-27) can no longer occur.

Several sampled tickers refer to completed seasons (KXNBAWINRECORD 2025-26, KXNBAPLAYOFFWINS and KXNBAPIADVANCE for the 2026 playoffs); the mechanism is the same for the 2026-27 editions but strikes and lists must be read per edition.

Playoff-win ladders exclude Play-In wins; KXNBAPIADVANCE asks whether any Play-In team reaches the Conference Finals; of the eight Play-In entrants only the four that win through (the 7 and 8 seeds, two per conference) can, so it is a union over the bracket paths of those 7 and 8 seeds.

series_and_cup.label: NBA playoff series winner/props and NBA Cup
series_and_cup.target: Series winner, series length / sweep, and NBA Cup winner/stage outcomes
series_and_cup.mechanism: A best-of-seven series is a sequence of correlated games with 2-2-1-1-1 home structure and playoff-tightened rotations; probability of winner and length derive from per-game win probability with state-dependent updating (injuries, adjustments) and correlation. Cup outcomes follow group tiebreakers (point differential), one wild card per conference and single-elimination games hosted by the higher seed through the semifinal, with a neutral final (2026-27: Hinkle Fieldhouse). Both require rule-accurate simulation and availability-aware ratings.

Win-total, seed and round-reach ladders must be coherent across thresholds.
Gives an exact component for KXNBATOP3 and the draft-pick-range series, instead of treating them as team strength outcomes.
Without it a top-N pick contract can be mis-mapped to the wrong team.
Required to separate pre-play-in seed contracts from qualification contracts for the same team.
Directly constructs the target pmf for the home-games series.
Needed for KXNBACUPQUAL and KXNBACUPGROUP contracts, which sit in this archetype.
Supplies the rare-event aggregator needed for the playoff triple-double series.
Seven live draft series (KXNBADRAFTTOP5/10/15/20/30, KXNBATOP3, KXNBATOP5ROTY) depend on this layer; it replaces the unaudited nba.draft_board with a market-free definition.
Replaces the weak, market-referenced nba.score_resid in stage s4 with a raw margin pmf for the Cup point-differential tiebreak.
KXNBAMATCHUP (rules-verified) resolves on the named Cup Finals pair qualifying; this archetype had no input for the joint bracket-reach probability of two teams.
Series-games, exact-score, Game 7 and games-spread contracts are direct functionals of the length distribution.

Gives the per-game probability of a 40-point final margin that KXNBAFINBLOWOUT compounds over the Finals games.
The only input that prices KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK; series simulations and final-margin distributions cannot see a 30-point deficit that was erased.
Prices the round-count and team-total contracts (sweeps, upsets, Game 7s, exact losses, 16-0) whose payoffs depend on the joint distribution across series.

interactions.hypothesis: An injury to a key player during a series creates positive correlation across later games; independent-game models overstate the stronger team's sweep probability.
Playoff ratings should weight top-8 rotation; deep-bench teams lose their depth advantage.
Cup group tiebreakers on point differential create incentives to run up margins in some games and rest stars in others.

A star injury during a series makes later-game outcomes positively correlated, so independent-game models overstate sweep probability and the chance of an undefeated run; a healthy and an injured regime have different per-game probabilities and the lengths differ accordingly.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the distribution of series length conditional on a star injury during the series with an independent-game model.

interactions.hypothesis: Group tiebreakers on point differential give incentives to run up scores in some games and rest stars in others; the value of margin is non-linear because it matters only if the team ends tied on record, and the probability of a tie depends on the state of the group.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the group with and without margin-based tiebreaks and compare qualification probabilities; check late-game garbage-time scoring when the margin matters.

interactions.hypothesis: Total home games is a convex function of advancement because deep runs add rounds each with up to four home games, while early exits produce few; the distribution is right-skewed and its mean is dominated by the probability of reaching the third and fourth rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated home-games pmf by seed with historical outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: The pair probability is the product of two bracket-reach probabilities only after the groups are settled; before that, each team's path depends on which wildcard slots open, and a margin-driven tiebreak in one group can move a team into the other half of the bracket, changing which pairs are even possible.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate group stages with and without point-differential tiebreaks and compare pair probabilities; check against historical Cup brackets for pairs excluded by bracket halves.

interactions.hypothesis: Clinch-at-home depends on the venue sequence: under 2-2-1-1-1 a higher-seed winner clinches at home only in games 5 or 7, a lower-seed winner only in games 4 or 6, so the probability is a path functional; a larger home-court edge makes home teams win more of their games, which lengthens series between even teams (more 2-2 and 3-3 states) and shifts clinches toward the higher seed's games 5 and 7.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated series-length and clinch-location frequencies with a venue-free model on 20 seasons of playoff series, split by seed gap.

interactions.hypothesis: If teams facing elimination play above their rating and teams up 3-0 relax, series lengthen and 2+ game comebacks become more frequent than independent games imply; the effect exists only in specific series states, so it shifts the tails of the sequence distribution, not the winner.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed frequencies of 6-7 game series and 0-2/1-3 comebacks over 25 seasons with an independent-games model and with the state-dependent model.

interactions.hypothesis: A 40-point Finals margin is likelier in uneven matchups, which also end in fewer games, so the per-game tail and the number of games are negatively linked; treating them as independent overstates the blowout probability for lopsided Finals and understates it for even ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate Finals with per-game margins drawn from the same strength gap that sets series length and compare the union probability with the independent product on historical Finals.

interactions.hypothesis: Second-round upset and sweep counts depend on which pairings survive round one: chalk first rounds produce even 1-4/2-3 matchups (few sweeps, few upsets by definition), while first-round upsets create mismatched or seed-inverted pairings, so round-two counts switch regime with round-one results.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition historical second-round sweep and upset counts on the number of first-round upsets and compare with unconditional rates.

nonlinearities.shape: multiplicative in two bracket-reach probabilities, with a zero floor for pairs in the same bracket half
nonlinearities.why: A specific pair needs both teams to win their halves; the pair probability is the product of two small numbers and is exactly zero for teams that the bracket places in the same half, so it is far more sensitive to bracket structure than either team's title odds.

nonlinearities.shape: product structure: undefeated-playoffs probability is a product of four sweep probabilities
nonlinearities.why: Each sweep needs about 60-80% for the favorite, so the product is a few percent; small errors in per-game probability multiply across 16 games.

nonlinearities.shape: inverted-U of P(7 games) in the per-game edge
nonlinearities.why: P(series reaches Game 7) is maximal (about 31%) when teams are even and falls steeply as the per-game edge grows, so Game 7 counts depend on how many even pairings the bracket produces, not on average strength.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts are functionals of a playoff (or Cup) bracket simulated game by game. Per-game win probability comes from availability-adjusted strength, playoff-tightened rotations and the venue under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern, with dependence between games of a series through injuries, adjustments and elimination-game effects. The ordered game sequence yields winners, lengths, exact scores, games spreads, comebacks from series deficits, road-win counts and clinch venues; concurrent series in a round yield counts of sweeps, upsets and Game 7s; and each team's run yields its losses, home games hosted and the rare 16-0 path. Two contracts need within-game score paths (a 30-point comeback, a 40-point margin). The Cup adds group tables with point-differential tiebreaks and a single-elimination knockout.

stages.name: Per-game win probability inside a playoff series
stages.description: Each game's win probability comes from playoff-strength ratings adjusted for who is available, rotation tightening that lifts star-heavy teams, and home court under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern (higher seed at home in games 1, 2, 5 and 7). Within a series the probability drifts with injuries, matchup adjustments and the series state: a team facing elimination tends to perform above its rating and a team that has just lost at home adjusts, so games are not independent draws.
stages.distribution: Per-game probabilities typically 30-80%, alternating with venue; mild positive serial dependence plus regime switches when a star is injured mid-series.

stages.name: Ordered game sequence: length, score, spread, comebacks, road wins, clinch venue
stages.description: The ordered win/loss sequence of a best-of-seven determines the series winner, the number of games, the exact score, whether a games spread is covered, whether a team came back from 0-2, 1-3 or 0-3, how many road wins occurred, whether no road team ever won, and in which arena the clinching game was played. These are not functions of the winner alone: road-win and clinch-venue contracts depend on venue-specific probabilities, and comeback contracts on the dependence between consecutive games.
stages.distribution: Discrete distribution over the 70 possible win/loss sequences; length on {4,5,6,7} with mass moving to 6-7 for even matchups; road wins on {0..7}; comeback paths have low single-digit probabilities.

stages.name: Round counts and whole-run totals across the bracket
stages.description: Playoff-wide contracts aggregate over concurrent series and over a team's run: the number of Game 7s, sweeps or upsets in a round depends on the seed gaps of the pairings that actually occur (set by earlier rounds and the Play-In); a team's exact playoff losses, its home games actually hosted and the 16-0 title run are sums or products over the rounds it reaches. Common shocks such as officiating emphasis or a league-wide injury wave make concurrent series dependent.
stages.distribution: Counts over four to eight concurrent series (Poisson-binomial with dependence); team losses and home games are lumpy sums over rounds; the 16-0 path is a product of four sweep probabilities, well under 1%.

stages.name: Within-game score extremes compounded over a series
stages.description: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK pays if any game in the series is won by a team that trailed by 30 or more, and KXNBAFINBLOWOUT if any Finals game ends with a 40-point margin. Both need the score path or final margin distribution of playoff games, conditional on the strength gap and pace, compounded over a random number of games. Even matchups produce longer series (more chances) but fewer huge leads; uneven ones produce blowouts but end sooner, so the series length and the per-game tail interact. These two series are deliberately kept with the series contracts but staged separately, fed by play-by-play score paths (required_data 3), because the compounding over series length is what couples them to the bracket.
stages.distribution: Per-game P(margin >= 40) and P(win after trailing by 30+) are well below 1% for even playoff teams; union over 4-7 games with dependence through matchup and pace.

stages.name: Cup group stage and knockout
stages.description: Cup group winners and qualifiers are determined by group record and tiebreakers (including point differential), and the knockout stage is single-elimination. The Finals-matchup contract resolves when both finalists are known, so it is the joint probability of two bracket paths, group-to-win sums title chances of teams that played each other in the group, and the champion contract is three knockout wins after qualification. Incentives in the last group games depend on the standings state, and margin matters for tiebreaks. Filing decision (resolver, 8 Nov 2026): the Cup contracts stay in this archetype as this separate stage with their own inputs and data set (Cup schedule and group tables) rather than a new archetype, because they share the team-strength and single-elimination machinery but none of the best-of-seven inputs. 2026-27 format: group winners and one wild card per conference make conference-split quarterfinals hosted by the higher seed, semifinals at the higher seed's arena, final at Hinkle Fieldhouse.
stages.distribution: Small group tables with discrete outcomes; margin enters via the tiebreak; knockout rounds are single games with win probability near rating-implied values.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Twenty-four playoff-series and Cup series, 23 with rules text. Single series: winner (KXNBASERIES), total games over X.5 (KXNBASERIESGAMES), exact score (KXNBASERIESSCORE, KXNBAFINALSEXACT), games spread (named team wins by more than X.5 games), comeback after trailing by 2+ games (KXNBASERIESCOMEBACK: 0-2, 3-0 or 3-1 deficits count), any team winning a game after trailing by 30+ points (KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK), exact number of road wins (a road win is a visiting-team win), no road win in the series (KXNBASERIESROADWIN), the champion clinching at home (wins the title in a home game) and a 40+ point margin in any Finals game (KXNBAFINBLOWOUT). Playoff-wide: any 3-0 series comeback (lose the first three, win four straight), at least N series going to Game 7, at least N sweeps or upsets in a round (an upset is a higher numerical seed beating a lower one), a team's exact playoff losses, a team going 16-0 and winning the title, and at least N home playoff games actually hosted in the home stadium (Play-In games excluded). Cup: champion, Finals qualifiers, group winners, any team of a group winning the Cup, and the Finals matchup, which resolves on qualification. No text addresses overtime, suspended games or relocated venues; KXNBAPLAYOFFHOMEGAMES is TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official playoff results, game-by-game scores and venues, play-by-play score paths (for 30-point deficits), the post-Play-In seeding, and the Cup standings and bracket; the sampled texts name no source agency.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction differs: series games 'over 6.5', games spread 'more than 2.5 games', road wins and playoff losses 'exactly N' (KXNBAPOLOSE is titled 'exactly 7 losses' but carries strike_type greater_or_equal), Game 7 and sweep/upset counts 'at least N'.

Path events (2+ game comeback, 3-0 comeback, first road win, clinch at home) are functions of the ordered game sequence and venue pattern, so the series model must be simulated game by game with dependence, not collapsed to winner and length.

In-game extremes (30-point comeback win, 40-point margin) union a per-game tail over the series' games; the number of games is itself random and correlated with how even the teams are, which works in opposite directions for the two events.
Home playoff games count only games actually hosted in the home stadium; Play-In games do not count, and a game moved to a neutral site would not count.

Cup: the Finals matchup resolves when both finalists qualify, group-to-win sums title probabilities over a group, group winners and qualifiers depend on group tiebreakers including point differential, and the Cup final itself is not a regular-season game.

Upsets use numerical seeds after the Play-In, so a 7 or 8 seed that came through the Play-In beating a 2 seed is an upset; equal seeds cannot meet before the Finals, where seed numbers from different conferences make the definition ambiguous.

season_stat_markets.label: NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials
season_stat_markets.target: Season stat leader, player streaks, team records and special season outcomes
season_stat_markets.mechanism: Players' season stat races and streaks depend on per-game rates, role stability, games played and thresholds, with injuries and rest as the main source of variance. Team record markets depend on game-level simulation. Streak markets (consecutive games meeting a threshold) depend on per-game hit probability and a persistence structure with absence risk. Rules define qualifying games and ties.

inputs.why: Current totals and per-game trajectory.
Minutes projection for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.
Role stability for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.
Availability risk for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.
Rest patterns for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.
Minimum-game rules for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.

Team context and remaining schedule.
Role shifts when teammates miss time.
Team record markets for NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials.
Futures prices drift on news and with limited liquidity; the path shows staleness and information arrival.
Tiebreaker, play-in, cutoff and settlement-source wording defines the outcome.
Realized frequency by rung across seasons is the only calibration source for rare season-level events.
Provides the leader-gap state in correct units, rather than raw season totals.

Context only: needed solely for a contract that applies a minimum-games or minutes rule; KXNBASTATAVG waives qualification, and the live KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE has none. Turns the static eligibility rule into the cliff probability that moves leader markets.

Hypothetical: no player consecutive-game threshold series exists in the ledger (only team win streaks), so this is not a required input until such a contract is listed. Gives the actual structure of consecutive-game contracts, where the product of per-game probabilities is the wrong approximation.
Needed for record and winning-streak contracts of any team vs the league.

The live streak contracts mapped to this form are team win streaks (KXNBAWINSTREAK threshold of 20 wins, KXNBALASTTOLOSE last undefeated team) whose value is a run-length extreme over 30 teams; this input supplies the run-length and tie mechanism that the player-threshold streak input does not.
KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE (54+ in any game, OT counted) and the first-to-50 race both need the per-game exceedance tail of a scorer's points; moved here with the series from the counting-specials record.
KXNBASTATAVG resolves on the rounded published average with no minimum and zero for zero games; this state-and-rounding input converts the rate posterior into the settlement probability.
KXNBAWINSTREAK asks whether any team reaches 20 straight regular-season wins (Cup games counted); the per-window run-length chain gives each team's hazard directly.
KXNBALASTTOLOSE is decided by the calendar day of each unbeaten team's first loss with same-day ties 1/N; no other input in this archetype models first-loss dates.
KXNBAONE3PT asks whether a low-volume shooter makes at least one three all season; season attempts (rate x minutes x games) and a position-level make prior decide it.
KXNBAFIRST50PTS (rules-verified) is a calendar race across players with 1/N same-day ties; neither the ceiling tail nor the rate posterior alone prices it.
KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE and KXNBAGAMESPECIALS (both rules-verified) are league-wide unions of tail events; no other input gives per-game tail probabilities summed over the schedule.
KXNBASTATLEADER (rules-verified, total plus/minus) is decided by team margin times minutes, which the per-game stat-rate inputs do not represent.

KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE and KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE count overtime; a 325-point game nearly always needs one or more overtimes, so the multi-OT probability from the ratings-implied regulation margin is part of the tail.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability of leading is a mixture over games played; the gap in totals matters less than who is likely to stay healthy.
Streak probability is the product of per-game thresholds; a small shortfall in minutes probability compounds over the streak.
Threshold rules create managed-absence incentives that change expected games played.

The probability of leading is a mixture over the number of games the candidate plays; a small current gap matters less than the chance that the leading player misses time, so leader probability falls faster than a gap-based normal calculation implies.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute leader probability from a model with random games played vs fixed games and compare calibration on historical season leaders.

interactions.hypothesis: Applies only if a contract uses a minimum-games rule (none is sampled; KXNBASTATAVG waives it): then players near the threshold are managed to qualify, so expected games played is not independent of the rule and the leader probability steps at the threshold. Under KXNBASTATAVG the interaction collapses to a smooth average plus a mass at zero games.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rest rates in the final 15 games by distance to the eligibility threshold.

interactions.hypothesis: A 20-game team streak (KXNBAWINSTREAK) or the league-longest streak needs roughly six weeks of near-certain wins, which in practice requires the team's stars to be healthy for the whole window; a single absence lowers per-game win probability for several games and usually ends the run, so the streak probability depends on the joint health of the top players over a window, not on the season-average rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute historical run-length distributions split by whether the top two players by minutes missed any game in the window, and compare streak hazards from the simulation with and without star-absence draws.

interactions.hypothesis: For the longest-streak and last-undefeated contracts, a head-to-head meeting between two teams on runs (or two unbeaten teams) ends one of the runs with certainty, so their run lengths and first-loss days are negatively linked; simulating teams independently overstates the chance that two teams share the maximum streak (1/N payout) or are both still unbeaten past a given day.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the league-longest streak, its tied count and first-loss days with and without zero-sum head-to-head games, and compare with the last 15 seasons of real streak ties and last-unbeaten dates.

interactions.hypothesis: A teammate's long-term injury switches the player's role regime for the rest of the season, changing the posterior mean and variance at once; to-date averages from the earlier regime are misleading.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rate models with a regime indicator for key-teammate absence and compare predictive error with and without it.

interactions.hypothesis: A candidate's chance of being first to 50 falls with the number and early-season schedule of rival candidates, not only with his own tail: the same per-game exceedance gives a much lower race probability when three other scorers play more games in October and November, and same-day hits split the payout.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test simulated first-to-50 winners and dates against past seasons; compare race probabilities with naive per-player season probabilities normalised to sum to one.

interactions.hypothesis: Total plus/minus is team net margin per minute times minutes played, so a strong team's starter accumulates margin quickly while a missed month cuts his total proportionally; the leader race is therefore a product of team strength and durability, and teammates are positively correlated through the team term.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress season plus/minus totals on team net rating times minutes and on the player's on/off differential; check the share of variance explained by the product term.

interactions.hypothesis: A 325-point game is out of reach in regulation for almost all matchups and becomes possible mainly through one or more overtimes, each adding roughly 22-26 combined points; the season probability therefore scales with the multi-overtime probability of high-pace, evenly matched games rather than with average totals.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical 300+ games by number of OT periods and compare the simulated share of 325+ outcomes with and without overtime.

nonlinearities.shape: cliff at the games threshold, conditional on a qualification-based contract (absent under KXNBASTATAVG)
nonlinearities.why: The payoff for a leader depends on meeting a minimum number of games, so the probability of leading jumps when a player's expected games cross the threshold; the response is a step smoothed by availability uncertainty.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in run length (geometric) with minutes-dependent hazard
nonlinearities.why: The probability of N consecutive hits decays roughly as p^N, with p itself dependent on minutes; small errors in p are amplified exponentially in N.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating: weight on observed average rises as n/(n+n_prior)
nonlinearities.why: The influence of to-date results on the posterior mean follows a hyperbolic shrinkage curve, so early-season changes in average move the estimate little and late-season changes move it a lot.

nonlinearities.shape: union compounding: 1 - prod over about 1,230 games of (1 - p_g)
nonlinearities.why: Tiny per-game probabilities compound over the season, so a factor-of-two error in tail shape changes the season probability almost proportionally while it is small and saturates near one when the tail is fat; the response to tail parameters is far from linear.

nonlinearities.shape: linear in minutes, maximum over correlated candidates
nonlinearities.why: Each player's total grows linearly with minutes and team margin, but the leader probability is a maximum across correlated teammates and rivals, so it is steep in the gap between the top two projected totals.

mechanism_review.summary: Season stat markets are long-horizon functionals of game-level production, decided by three layers: (1) how many games each candidate plays (injury, load management), which under the sampled rules scales totals and the number of chances smoothly rather than through a qualification cliff; (2) the per-game rate or per-game tail (minutes, usage, role, team margin), shrunk toward a preseason projection; and (3) the aggregation form: a rounded average, a leader maximum over correlated totals (plus/minus is mostly team margin times minutes), a first-passage race across players by calendar day, a union over the whole schedule of rare single-game events (54 points, 325 combined points with overtime, 15 stocks), team run lengths (any 20-game streak) or a survival race (last undefeated). Settlement details such as 1/N calendar-day ties, OT inclusion and rounding change the functional.

stages.name: Games played and qualification
stages.description: The number of games a candidate plays is a random variable with heavy mass near the full schedule and a left tail from injuries and load management. In the sampled contracts it acts smoothly: the average has no minimum and zero games gives zero, totals such as plus/minus and the chance of a 54-point or first-to-50 game scale with games played, and a low-volume shooter's chance of one made three grows with his games. Rest decisions concentrate in the second half for older stars.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most rotation players play 65-78 of 82 games with a long left tail; hazard rising with age and prior absences; no cliff under the sampled rules.

stages.name: Per-game rate trajectory
stages.description: A player's true per-game rate is a function of minutes, role, usage and age, which evolves through the season with teammates' availability and coaching decisions. Observed averages to date are noisy estimates of the true rate; shrinkage toward a preseason projection prevents overreaction to early results.
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior for the true rate with sd shrinking with games played; role shocks (injuries to teammates) produce jumps.

stages.name: Aggregation into averages and leader races
stages.description: A season average has sampling variance falling with games played, and resolves on the rounded published figure, so the effective strike sits half a rounding unit below the stated one. A leader contract is the maximum over candidates whose totals are correlated: for total plus/minus, teammates share the same team margin and differ mainly in minutes, so the leader is set by team strength times durability rather than individual rate.
stages.distribution: Average: Gaussian-like posterior with a step at the rounding boundary; plus/minus leader: maximum over correlated totals with strong within-team dependence; ties 1/N.

stages.name: Streak and run-length processes
stages.description: The live streak contracts are team-level. Any-team-reaches-20 is a union over teams and over 20-game windows of products of game win probabilities, dominated by the strongest healthy teams and by stretches of weak opponents; the last undefeated team is a survival race by calendar day, decided within the first two weeks, with same-day losses tied. Run lengths across 30 teams and the tied count come from the same game-level simulation; the player threshold-streak input is retained only as a hypothesis with no live series.
stages.distribution: Run-length extremes over teams (right tail driven by rating uncertainty and star health); first-loss dates nearly geometric per team with heterogeneous win probabilities.

stages.name: Season simulation backbone for team run-length contracts
stages.description: The three team contracts here (any 20-game streak, the longest streak with 1/N ties, the last undefeated team) are read off one simulated regular season: game win probabilities from team strength with common rating shocks, head-to-head games that make one team's win another's loss, and Cup games before the final included in the sequence. Run lengths, the number of teams tied at the maximum and first-loss dates all come from the same paths, so they must be drawn jointly rather than from separate marginal models.
stages.distribution: Thirty correlated game-outcome sequences; extreme-value behaviour of the maximal run length with integer ties; first-loss day is discrete with same-day ties.

stages.name: League-wide extreme single-game events and first-passage races
stages.description: Several contracts are unions over the remaining schedule of rare single-game events: a named star's 54-point game, the first 50-point game by anyone, a 325-point combined game and a 15-stocks player game. Each per-game probability lives in the tail (hot shooting plus heavy minutes, overtime periods, unusual pace), and the season probability compounds across hundreds or thousands of games; the first-to-50 race also depends on the calendar order of candidates' games.
stages.distribution: Per-game generalised-Pareto exceedances with overtime as a discrete mixture; season probabilities are 1 - prod(1 - p_g), highly sensitive to tail shape; race outcomes are first-passage times with same-day ties.

stages.name: Season-long first event for low-volume players
stages.description: The one-made-three contract targets players who rarely shoot threes, often centers; the outcome is whether the season's attempts produce one make. Attempts per game are near zero and may be a coaching choice, so the probability is governed by games played times attempt rate (zero-inflated) and a position-level make prior, with role changes (a new coach encouraging stretch bigs) able to switch the rate regime.
stages.distribution: Zero-inflated Poisson attempts over the season; P(at least one make) = 1 - E[(1 - p3)^A] with A random; a point mass at zero for players who never attempt.

talent_strength.note: Player rate posterior, team strength for streaks and survival, and team-margin-driven plus/minus.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-long averages and records wash out single-opponent effects: the schedule's opponent mix enters through schedule strength in the simulation rather than through matchup-specific variables, so no matchup input is needed at this horizon.

role_personnel.note: Role and minutes trajectory, redistribution when teammates miss time.

availability_news.note: Games-played distribution, which scales totals, averages' denominators and the number of chances for single-game events.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes that alter a star's role, minutes cap or rest policy are not quantified by any input in this archetype's list; the effect on a season stat leader could be large mid-season.

environment.note: Venue and altitude effects average out over 82 games and do not matter for season totals or streaks beyond what pace and team ratings capture.

game_context_script.note: Overtime is counted for the 54-point and 325-point contracts and is usually required for the latter; game script otherwise averages out over the season.

pace_volume.note: Per-game volume trajectory, three-point attempts for low-volume shooters, and game pace for extreme totals.

efficiency_conversion.note: Regression of early hot streaks in shooting-dependent stats toward talent.

distribution_variance.note: Variance of averages, team run-length and first-loss distributions, single-game exceedance tails and league-wide unions.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest incentives near eligibility thresholds and schedule density.

officiating_rules.note: Scorer-credit practices for steals and blocks (relevant to the 15-stocks contract) and the source agencies' rounding and correction policy for averages are not versioned in any input; referee crews themselves are irrelevant at season horizon.

settlement_contract.note: Rounded published average with no minimum, 1/N ties by calendar day or total, OT counted for single-game thresholds, regular season only with Cup games before the final.
