contract_review.settlement_definition: Twelve 2026-27 regular-season series are filed here, ten with sampled rules. Player forms: per-game average at or above a strike (KXNBASTATAVG: no qualification minimum, zero games played means an average of zero, rounded figure from the Source Agencies), at least one made three in the season (KXNBAONE3PT), a single game at or above a points threshold including overtime (KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE), the first player to a 50-point game (KXNBAFIRST50PTS: same-day firsts split $1/N), and league leader in total plus/minus (KXNBASTATLEADER: traded players' totals combined, ties $1/N). League-wide forms: any game with 325+ combined points including overtime (KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE), any player with 15+ steals plus blocks in a game (KXNBAGAMESPECIALS), any team with a 20+ game win streak (KXNBAWINSTREAK), the team with the longest win streak with ties paid $1/N (KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK) and the last undefeated team by calendar day of first loss with same-day ties $1/N (KXNBALASTTOLOSE). All count only regular-season games: preseason, Play-In, playoffs, the All-Star Game and the Cup final are excluded and Cup games before the final count. KXNBAHIGHESTSCORING and KXNBAPLAYERSPECIALS are TITLE_ONLY.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league statistics via the 'Source Agencies' named in the full rules (not named in the sample); plus/minus and average figures as published, with the rounding procedure for averages unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: No qualification cliff where rules are sampled: KXNBASTATAVG waives league minimums and sets a zero average for zero games, and KXNBASTATLEADER (total plus/minus, a counting total) has no minimum; a games-played cliff applies only to a leader contract with a minimum rule, none of which is sampled.

Ties: KXNBAFIRST50PTS (same calendar day of tip-off), KXNBALASTTOLOSE (same day of first loss) and KXNBASTATLEADER split $1/N; the average contract has no tie but resolves on the rounded published figure, so the effective strike is strike minus half a rounding unit.

Overtime is explicitly counted for KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE and KXNBAGAMEHIGHSCORE, and a 325-point game almost always needs overtime, so the number of OT periods is part of the event; KXNBAGAMESPECIALS' secondary text notes that quarter-specific markets in that series exclude overtime.
Regular-season only, with Cup games before the final counted (stated for every sampled series); streaks span Cup knockout games but not the Cup final, and the Play-In is excluded.

Streak contracts with live series are team win streaks (KXNBAWINSTREAK, any team reaching 20) and the last undefeated team; no player consecutive-game series exists, so the player threshold-streak input is context only.

awards_draft.label: NBA awards, All-NBA selections and draft
awards_draft.target: Award winner, All-NBA selections and draft position/outcomes
awards_draft.mechanism: Awards and selections are results of voting or formula: production and advanced metrics, team success, games played (the 65-game rule with its Extraordinary Circumstances appeal for MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA and All-Defensive) and narrative interact; All-NBA ballots are positionless; All-Star starters and reserves are positionless with a nationality minimum; the Hustle Award is a tracked-stat formula. Draft outcomes depend on lottery order, consensus rankings and trade/workout news. Mostly slow-moving until late-season/draft-week information arrives.

inputs.why: Production and advanced metrics.
Ballot structure and media consensus.
Team-seed effect on voting for NBA awards, All-NBA selections and draft.
Advanced impact measures for NBA awards, All-NBA selections and draft.
Risk of missing eligibility for NBA awards, All-NBA selections and draft.
Lottery odds and consensus ranking.
Late narrative and trade news.
Minutes and role for counting stats.
Futures prices drift on news and with limited liquidity; the path shows staleness and information arrival.
Tiebreaker, play-in, cutoff and settlement-source wording defines the outcome.
Sportsbook futures prices give a de-vigged consensus for comparison.
Realized frequency by rung across seasons is the only calibration source for rare season-level events.
MVP, All-NBA, DPOY and Clutch markets can flip from near-certain to impossible on one game, so the ledger is the first gate for every candidate price.
The candidate field and the named statistic differ per series, so a single production metric misranks Sixth Man, Clutch and MIP contenders.
Coach of the Year, Executive of the Year and MIP prices should key off surprise rather than wins; the existing catalog has no baseline for it.
Rung markets on 1st/2nd/3rd team are cumulative on the same ranking and need an enforced consistent ladder, which the market's independent quotes may violate.
Pick-slot and team-to-draft markets settle on ownership as much as on prospect choice, and traded protections create incentives that move standings.
Draft slot markets on picks 1-10 are priced as separate coins; the Plackett-Luce structure enforces that one prospect fills one slot.
Monthly series are decided in a fixed short window where a schedule difference of three games matters.
Carries the dominant 50% fan component and slot arithmetic that the media-ballot stage omits, which is the mechanism behind the live starters and All-Stars series.
Reserves are decided by a different electorate than starters and by a different rule, and the roster markets need both.
Gives the narrative and voter-fatigue effects an observable form for MVP, DPOY, ROY and similar awards.
Captures the All-Star voting calendar, captains and event participation that fix when fan-vote returns and roster announcements arrive; context for the starter and reserve inputs.
Series and Cup MVP markets need P(team wins the series or title) as the first factor.
Series length and winner per round feed the series-MVP first factor and the number of games a candidate accumulates.
Second factor of every series MVP market: P(player chosen | his team wins), driven by series scoring share and best-player status.
Nominee/panel awards (Social Justice Champion, Teammate, Sportsmanship, series MVPs) and the $1/N co-winner payout need a nominee-set and co-winner model.
KXNBALOTTERYODDS, KXNBATOPPICK and KXNBATOP3 settle on the lottery draw, which is the published odds table applied to the final pre-lottery ranks.
KXNBAHALLOFFAME needs P(inductee) through a two-stage committee election that no ballot, draft or All-Star input describes.
Prices all draft range, matchup, count and comparison markets from one coherent order.
Turns MVP/All-NBA eligibility from a hard ledger into ledger plus a dated appeal branch, which moved 2025-26 award prices.
The 16/8 minimum with Commissioner additions is a selection stage the vote composite cannot produce.
KXNBAHUSTLE is settled by a tracked-stat formula; without this index the series has no driver.
Cup MVP depends on which team survives the group tiebreaks and the knockout games (higher seed hosts through the semifinal; neutral final).
65-game rule (20+ minutes in 63) gates MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA and All-Defensive; ROY, Sixth Man, All-Rookie and the draft are exempt.

interactions.hypothesis: Voters reward production attached to team success, so model vote share with an interaction between individual metrics and team win percentage.
Eligibility is a hard gate: a player on the games-played bubble has a bimodal outcome.
Narrative shifts in the final weeks can overcome small metric gaps; use ladder trackers as a signal with caution.
Pre-draft trades and workout news create large consensus changes in the final days.

Voters treat team success as a gate: production wins only when the team is a top-two seed, and below that seed the same production sees a sharp discount, especially for MVP and DPOY; the effect is much smaller for ROY and MIP.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit vote share on production gap with a seed-bucket dummy and compare slopes by award across 2000-2025 results; test seed-bucket x gap coefficient.

interactions.hypothesis: At zero slack a single missed game removes a candidate completely, so the probability is a step in games remaining rather than a smooth penalty; players with high slack are insulated.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised winner rate across slack buckets 0, 1-3, 4-8, 9+ on historical candidates; look for a discontinuity at slack 0.

interactions.hypothesis: Similar candidates split ballot ranks: two centres with equal metrics both fall relative to a lone candidate with the same metrics, and a surplus of strong forwards lowers P(third team) for a marginal one.
interactions.how_to_test: Add the count of candidates with a similar profile within 1 sd as a feature, or simulate ballots to see whether pairwise vote-share correlation is negative. Treat this as a modelling choice (a ballot-split simulation) and validate it on past points distributions rather than assuming the dependence.

interactions.hypothesis: Coach of the Year rewards positive surprise but saturates once a team is already a top seed, because a title favourite cannot overperform much; a mid-seed team with a large surprise beats a top seed with a small one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress COY winner on surprise and seed with a saturating term; compare predictions of winners for teams above 60 wins.

interactions.hypothesis: Slot probabilities for prospects depend on who holds the pick: a team with a veteran roster, a rebuilding team and a team trading the pick pick differently, so P(prospect at slot k) is conditional on the holder.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit selection model with owner-type features on past drafts; measure rank-error of consensus by pick holder.

interactions.hypothesis: A series MVP needs both his team to win and the panel to pick him, so a star on a modest favourite can be worth less than the second option on a heavy favourite; the product, not either factor, ranks candidates, and both update after every game.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare log loss of P(win) x P(chosen | win) against a model using only individual series production on past Finals and conference-finals MVPs.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at the threshold (65 qualifying games)
nonlinearities.why: The rule is a hard threshold, so effect on P(win) is zero until the player is within a few games of the line and then collapses; linear injury-risk adjustment would misprice players near the line.

nonlinearities.shape: Step in seed (top-2 vs rest), saturating above
nonlinearities.why: Winners cluster in top seeds, so probability changes little between seed 1 and 2 but falls sharply beyond seed 4; response is closer to a gate than a slope.

nonlinearities.shape: Softmax in the gap to the next candidate
nonlinearities.why: Vote share is concentrated; a candidate's win probability depends on the margin over the runner-up on voter-visible stats rather than the absolute level.

nonlinearities.shape: Entropy collapse near draft night
nonlinearities.why: Selection probability concentrates quickly as boards converge and insiders report, so the dispersion measure should be time-weighted rather than static.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts resolve through human processes whose inputs arrive at different clocks. Awards are a ranked-ballot election: a panel of media voters ranks five candidates for MVP (points 10-7-5-3-1) and three for most other awards (5-3-1) after the season, so the winner is the candidate with the greatest points, which depends on (a) who is eligible after the games/minutes minimum, (b) the candidates' perceived production relative to the field, (c) team success which voters treat as a prerequisite, and (d) vote splitting among near-equal candidates and voter fatigue for repeat winners. Selection markets (All-NBA, All-Star, All-Defensive, All-Rookie) are nested cut lines on the same points ranking. Monthly awards depend on the games actually played in a calendar window. Draft markets are a different chain: lottery draw and pick ownership (protections, swaps) decide which team holds slot N, then team preference, workouts and trade activity decide who is selected. Outcomes are lumpy (one winner), early prices drift on narrative, and the most informative single observable is eligibility, which can flip an outcome from near-certain to impossible. All-Star selection is a separate process: a 50% fan, 25% player and 25% media weighted-rank composite picks the top five per conference without regard to position (2026 rules), subject to a 16 US / 8 international minimum, and conference coaches then pick reserves (stage s6). Series MVPs (Finals, conference finals, Cup) are a third process: a small media panel picks a player almost always from the winning side right after the deciding game, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(chosen | team wins). Committee and peer-vote honours (Hall of Fame, Social Justice Champion, Teammate and Sportsmanship awards) are nominee elections with their own panels and calendars.

stages.name: Eligibility and games-played gate
stages.description: A candidate must clear league thresholds before production matters. Verified for 2025-26 and unchanged as of Nov 2026: the 65-game rule governs MVP, DPOY, Most Improved, All-NBA and All-Defensive, counting games with 20+ minutes in at least 63 and 15-20 minutes in up to two more; ROY, Sixth Man and All-Rookie are exempt, and monthly awards, Coach/Executive of the Year, All-Star and the draft are outside it. The ledger moves with each injury, rest night and minute total, but it is not the last word: an Extraordinary Circumstances challenge decided by the NBA and NBPA granted Doncic and Cunningham eligibility in April 2026 and an arbitrator denied Edwards, so eligibility = ledger survival plus a discretionary appeal branch. Clutch-award coverage is not confirmed (u3).
stages.distribution: Bimodal near the line: mass near 0 or 1 for most players, with a narrow band of players with zero slack whose probability is a binomial-style survival over remaining games and injury hazard.

stages.name: Perceived production versus the field
stages.description: Voters rank on points, rebounds, assists, efficiency summaries and advanced numbers, but also on role-specific awards: defensive reputation and block/steal counts for DPOY, improvement delta versus the previous season for MIP, rookie rank for ROY. The relevant quantity is the gap to the next-best candidate on the stats voters actually look at, not the candidate's absolute level, and the stats used by voters are not identical to RAPM-type impact models.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail in the leader's margin; the winner's vote share is typically concentrated (first-place votes dominated by one or two names) so P(win) behaves like a softmax over a small candidate set.

stages.name: Team success and narrative conditioning
stages.description: Historical winners overwhelmingly come from top seeds, and the penalty for a lower seed is steep for MVP/DPOY while smaller for ROY; coach and executive awards are driven by wins relative to preseason expectation, not wins alone. Late-season stories (a surge, a record chase, a voter-fatigue narrative about a repeat winner) can reverse a small metric gap, and voters' ballots are submitted before the playoffs.
stages.distribution: Step-like in team seed and approximately logistic in the gap between win total and preseason expectation; narrative shocks are rare and large.

stages.name: Ballot aggregation and cut lines
stages.description: Final standings are the sum of points across about 100 ballots, with ties broken by rule or shared payout; All-NBA and similar teams are cut lines on the same ranking (positionless since 2023-24), so P(1st team) is nested inside P(any team). Vote splitting between two similar candidates (two centers, two rookies) reduces both below what each would earn alone.
stages.distribution: Discrete, bounded sum of ranks; winner and cut-line events are strongly negatively correlated across candidates; nested sets must satisfy monotone sums.

stages.name: Draft order and selection
stages.description: Lottery order is a draw from published odds that depend on final standings (and tie-break coin flips); KXNBALOTTERY, KXNBATOPPICK and KXNBALOTTERYODDS settle directly on that draw, while pick ownership (protections, swaps) decides who holds each slot. Given owner and slot, selection depends on consensus board rank and its dispersion, team need, workout and medical information, and draft-night trades. Slot, team, range (top-5..top-30, first 33), matchup (A before B), count (freshmen in the top 10) and comparison (ACC vs Big 12 in round 1) markets are all functionals of one joint draft order, so they must be read off the same simulation with prospect attributes attached; KXNBATOP5ROTY additionally needs the ROY ballot model conditioned on draft slot.
stages.distribution: Lottery is a known discrete probability table; selection among the top few prospects is a categorical mixture whose entropy falls sharply in the final 48 hours.

stages.name: All-Star selection: positionless vote composite, coach reserves and nationality minimum
stages.description: Verified for 2026: starters are the top five per conference on a 50/25/25 fan/player/media composite chosen without regard to position (fan vote breaks composite ties), reserves are seven per conference voted by head coaches without regard to position and not for their own players, and injured selectees are replaced by the Commissioner. The USA-vs-World format then imposes a 16 US / 8 international minimum filled by Commissioner additions, so a fringe candidate's chance depends on conference rank and on the depth of his nationality group. The 2027 format has not been announced; the stage applies the 2026 rules until it is.
stages.distribution: Weighted-rank composite with a random-walk fan component that shrinks as the voting window closes; discrete slot allocation (5 starters and 7 reserves per conference) with correlated displacement within a conference and within a nationality group (positionless since 2026).

stages.name: Series and tournament MVP conditional on the winning side
stages.description: Finals MVP, the two conference-finals MVPs (awarded since 2022) and the Cup MVP are voted by a small media panel immediately after the deciding game, and the winner almost always comes from the team that won (the only losing-team Finals MVP was in 1969). The probability therefore factors into the chance the team wins the series or the Cup knockout (bracket path, home court, series length, single Cup knockout games hosted by the higher seed through the semifinal, with only the final neutral) and the chance the panel picks this player given a win, which follows his share of the winning team's series scoring and pre-series best-player status; a dominant star takes most of the conditional mass, a balanced roster splits it. Prices move game by game as both factors update. The Cup All-Tournament Team (KXNBACUP1STTEAM) is the same panel's five-player selection, drawn mostly from the knockout-round teams.
stages.distribution: Product of a series-win Bernoulli and a categorical over two to four candidates on the winning roster, highly concentrated on the top scorer; small co-MVP mass for the $1/N clause.

stages.name: Committee, nominee and peer-vote honours including the Hall of Fame
stages.description: The Hall of Fame (KXNBAHALLOFFAME) inducts a class through a screening committee that names finalists, usually at All-Star weekend, and an honors committee whose supermajority vote is announced in early April, with direct-elect committees for veterans, contributors and international candidates bypassing the finalist stage; coaches such as the sampled candidate follow the coach path. The Social Justice Champion is chosen by a league committee from team nominees and finalists, and the Teammate and Sportsmanship awards by player votes among finalists. These outcomes depend on nominee status, career markers and committee composition, not on game production in the market window, and the finalist announcement is the main information jump.
stages.distribution: Two-stage Bernoulli (finalist, then elected) for the Hall of Fame with no fixed class size; categorical over five or so finalists for the nominee awards, with a small co-winner probability.

stages.name: Formula-decided Hustle Award
stages.description: KXNBAHUSTLE is settled by the league's statistical formula, not a ballot: qualifying players are ranked per minute in nine tracked hustle categories and the top aggregate wins. The outcome therefore depends on season-long tracked rates, the minutes floor that filters out small samples, and the unpublished category weights, which must be inferred from past winners. Low-usage bigs and defensive guards dominate; production and team record are irrelevant except through minutes.
stages.distribution: Winner is an argmax over a few dozen qualifiers; rates per minute are approximately normal after 1,000 minutes, so the probability concentrates on 3-5 players with heavy weight uncertainty.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Each award, selection or draft market settles Yes only if the named player, coach, executive, team or pick slot is the one officially announced for the stated season or draft. Award texts say Yes if the person 'wins' the award in the 2026-27 season; most add a co-winner clause paying Yes $1/N rounded down (Clutch, Cup MVP, monthly awards, Coach and Executive of the Year, MIP, Hustle, conference-finals MVPs and the 2026-27 Finals MVP (KXNBAFINMVP; the older KXNBAFINALSMVP 2025 text has no tie clause), Social Justice, Sportsmanship, Teammate), while MVP, DPOY, ROY, Sixth Man, All-NBA/All-Defensive/All-Rookie team and Cup All-Tournament texts have no tie clause. Selection markets settle on being 'selected' to the team (All-Star regardless of whether he plays). Award finalists (KXNBAAWARDFIN) settle on Source Agency reports, and all resolve No if finalists are not reported before the winner. Draft-slot markets settle on the player selected at slot N; team-to-draft (KXNBADRAFTTEAM) settles on the team making the selection at the draft, ignoring later trades, and No if the player is undrafted; range, matchup, count and comparison markets (top-5..top-30, first 33 picks, A before B, at least 9 freshmen in the top 10, ACC count equal to Big 12 count in round 1) settle on the realised draft order. Lottery markets settle on the lottery result (pick awarded, regardless of later trades), and KXNBALOTTERYODDS on the pre-lottery odds of the team awarded pick 1. The Hall of Fame settles on announced inclusion in the class. After the reconciliation the key holds 65 series (60 with rules text; KXNBATOP3, KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBADRAFTTRADE, KXNBADRAFTCONF, KXNBADRAFTINT are TITLE_ONLY).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: League official announcements: voting-result releases for awards and All-NBA, All-Star starters announcement, draft lottery broadcast and the draft transaction record.
variants_and_edge_cases: Co-winner or tie: Clutch, Cup MVP, monthly awards, Coach and Executive of the Year, MIP, Hustle, series MVPs and the community/peer awards pay $1/N rounded down; MVP, DPOY, ROY, Sixth Man, All-NBA/Defensive/Rookie and Cup All-Tournament texts have no tie clause; Hall of Fame inductees settle independently.

Eligibility gates (65-game and 20-minute rule) are enforced by the league and, if they govern the market, can disqualify an MVP-calibre candidate after the market has priced him; the sampled text does not say which awards they govern or whether Kalshi follows the league on eligibility.

Draft-slot markets (KXNBADRAFT1..10, KXNBADRAFTPICK) settle on who is picked at slot N whichever team holds it; KXNBADRAFTTEAM settles on the selecting team at the draft (undrafted = No); lottery markets (KXNBALOTTERY, KXNBATOPPICK) settle on the lottery award regardless of later trades.

Group markets (All-NBA teams, All-Star starters, award finalists, lottery picks) are nested or cumulative sets of the same latent ranking, so rung probabilities must be monotone and sum to the set size.

Draft aggregates (top-5..top-30 ranges, first-33 over/under, A-before-B matchups, freshman counts, ACC vs Big 12 equality) are functionals of one joint draft order and need prospect attributes; KXNBATOP5ROTY couples the ROY ballot to the draft slot of the winner.
Five series remain TITLE_ONLY (KXNBATOP3, KXNBAASSTARTERS, KXNBADRAFTTRADE, KXNBADRAFTCONF, KXNBADRAFTINT); their construction is inferred from titles (u1).
Finalist markets resolve No for all if finalists are not reported before the winner is announced; All-Star markets settle on selection even if the player does not play.

off_court_events.label: NBA off-court events: transactions, coaching, business, All-Star, schedule
off_court_events.target: A dated off-court event (trade, signing, coach change, announcement, All-Star participant) occurs by a stated date or condition
off_court_events.mechanism: Sparse-event markets determined by rule feasibility (cap/apron, roster counts, deadlines), organizational incentives and reporter signals, with resolution by official announcements or credible reports. Priors come from base rates of similar events by team and timing; the main edge is the correct interpretation of reporter reliability and the settlement wording.

interactions.hypothesis: A reported trade is only likely to complete if matching rules and deadlines allow; rumor probability should be conditioned on feasibility.
Coach changes cluster after underperformance vs expectation and at schedule breaks.
The official-announcement wording decides the effective event time; leaks before the announcement do not settle the market.

A top-tier report that an agreement is signed multiplies with the remaining approval pipeline probability; a reliable report at the agreed stage still leaves the approval and timing risk, so the market should not jump to one.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare outcomes of deals reported at 'agreed' by reliable sources against the share that cleared approval within 90 days.

interactions.hypothesis: Trade probability collapses after the deadline and spikes in the days before it, so the hazard is convex in days to deadline; feasibility constraints bind most tightly in the last week when salary-matching is tested.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the daily hazard around the deadline with and without a feasibility flag; test hazard ratio at days -3 to 0.

interactions.hypothesis: A franchise star is traded mostly when his team turns seller: the KXNBATRADE hazard stays near its floor while the team is near or above expectation and rises steeply once the team falls clearly below it before the deadline, more so after a front-office change; rumours about a star on a contender convert rarely whatever their volume.
interactions.how_to_test: Hazard model of in-season trades of players with All-Star-level usage on 15 seasons, with a hinge in the team's gap to preseason expectation and a front-office-tenure interaction.

interactions.hypothesis: The same news item resolves differently under different wordings: an agreement in principle satisfies an announcement market but not a Board-award or league-processing market, so one report moves the series in opposite directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Code each historical report against each wording in the series set and measure the divergence in outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: A retirement announcement clusters after the season ends and before free agency, so the player's age hazard is conditional on being in that period; before the season's end the hazard is lower regardless of age.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate retirement announcement timing by month for players aged 36+ and test the seasonal hazard ratio.

interactions.hypothesis: Pick trades agreed on draft night count only if officially processed before the window end; deals with salaried players are processed only after the July moratorium, so the agreed-trade hazard is truncated by a hard date for one deal type and not the other.
interactions.how_to_test: Split 15 drafts' top-10 pick trades by whether salaried players were included and compare processing-date shares before and after the moratorium.

interactions.hypothesis: Before leaks the pairing probability comes from the selection model's TV-appeal features; once a tier-one reporter leaks the Christmas or opening slate, probability jumps to near certainty regardless of features, so the model applies only in the pre-leak regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare leaked versus final Christmas slates over 10 seasons and the timing of leaks relative to release.

interactions.hypothesis: Realignment probability is near zero unless the expansion vote passes; once two Western cities are awarded, one Western incumbent must move East to make 16/16, so KXNBAJOINCONF jumps from a residual to a high conditional probability exactly at the final expansion vote.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realignment announcements against expansion decisions in past leagues (NBA 2004 Charlotte, NHL 2021 Seattle) and check the conditional jump at vote dates.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked and convex around deadlines
nonlinearities.why: The probability mass of trades concentrates in the final days before a deadline and then goes to zero, so linear time decay misprices markets near the deadline.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function by stage
nonlinearities.why: Probability to complete jumps at each stage (exploration about 0.2, definitive agreement about 0.9) rather than rising smoothly with time, and timing risk is lognormal.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating in report stage
nonlinearities.why: Reports at the agreed stage from tier-one sources approach 1, while talks-stage reports sit near 0.1-0.3, so credence is not linear in the intensity of the language.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic threshold in the record-vs-expectation gap (seller status)
nonlinearities.why: Seller status, and with it the trade hazard of a team's veterans, is nearly flat for modest underperformance and switches on past a gap threshold in the weeks before the deadline, so a linear effect of record understates deadline trades of stars on collapsing teams.

mechanism_review.summary: Off-court events are sparse, one-off outcomes generated by organisations, so the mechanism is a process of stage-gated progress against a deadline rather than a rate per opportunity. An event happens when (1) it is feasible under league rules and finances (salary cap and apron constraints for trades, Board of Governors approval for relocation, expansion and realignment), (2) a decision-maker with incentives chooses to pursue it (a front office's competitive position, a player's career horizon and market), (3) counterparties agree and the process clears its approval stages, each with typical durations, and (4) a qualifying public act occurs inside the window and at the stage the contract wording requires (announcement, signed definitive agreement, completed approval). Information arrives through reporters whose reliability varies by outlet and by stage, so the key variable is not the rumor but the stage reached and the historical time from that stage to the qualifying act. Hazards are not uniform: they spike around calendar landmarks (draft, free agency, trade deadline, Board meetings). Two families do not fit the pipeline: schedule-content markets (Christmas and opening opponents) are a selection by the league for national TV, and personal-act markets (apology, retirement, overseas signing) are individual decisions.

stages.name: Feasibility under league rules and finances
stages.description: Whether an event can happen at all is governed by hard constraints: trade salary matching tied to payroll tiers (the apron levels), roster size, moratorium dates, the league approval requirement for relocation and expansion, the expansion process and the CBA rules for contract extensions. An infeasible event has probability near zero regardless of rumors, and a feasible event has a conditional probability given the actors' incentives; the two are multiplied. For player-transaction markets feasibility is the cap arithmetic: which teams have space or matching salary for the player (nba.player_move_destination_model) and what contract value the maximum and minimum tiers allow (nba.next_contract_value_model), which bounds both the destination set and a contract-size strike.
stages.distribution: Binary feasibility gate times a continuous incentive term; feasibility is deterministic given payroll and roster data and is often the cleanest source of low probabilities.

stages.name: Actor incentive and hazard rate
stages.description: Given feasibility, the decision-maker's incentive sets the base hazard for the live player-transaction and career markets: a team well below its preseason expectation or with a new front office becomes a seller, which raises the trade hazard for its veterans (KXNBATRADE); a veteran near the end of his contract or career weighs retirement (KXNBARETIRE) against a last contract, which drives KXNBANEXTTEAM, KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF and KXNBATEAMANNOUNCE. The base hazard comes from reference classes (star trades by team gap to expectation, retirements by age and contract status) and is then updated by organisation- and player-specific facts.
stages.distribution: Low-rate hazard process, over-dispersed across organisations; discrete events with heavy clustering around specific calendar points.

stages.name: Deal stage progression and approval pipeline
stages.description: Trades, expansions, relocations, realignment and rule changes move through ordered stages (exploration, agreement, governance vote or league processing), each with a stage-specific completion probability and delay, and the contract requires a specific stage. Player trades must be officially processed (trade-call approval) before the date; top-10 pick trades depend on draft-night bargaining over the pick value curve and on whether the deal is processed before the window end or after the July moratorium. Expansion awards, relocation approval and conference realignment are Board of Governors decisions scheduled around board meetings and linked to each other (expansion forces realignment). Rule adoption follows the Competition Committee then Board vote pipeline.
stages.distribution: Sequential Bernoulli transitions with log-normal durations between stages; the final-stage timing is clustered around meeting dates.

stages.name: Information flow and reporter reliability
stages.description: The market learns about the stage through reporters and official channels with different lead times and error rates; a report that a deal is 'agreed' from a top-tier reporter has a very high completion rate while 'in talks' reports often fail. The edge is in assigning the right probability to a report given its stage and source, and in timing relative to the official announcement.
stages.distribution: Report-to-event conversion probabilities vary from about 0.1 for 'talks' to over 0.95 for 'agreed' from a tier-one source; lead times of minutes to months.

stages.name: Wording and qualifying-act mapping
stages.description: The final stage is semantic: each contract's wording defines which observable counts (league processing, Source Agency confirmation, Board award, formal adoption, public statement, official registration). Events can occur in an unrecognised form (a leak, an agreement in principle, a conditional announcement) and fail the wording, or occur on the edge of the window in Eastern Time. The mapping from real-world events to the contract's qualifying act is a model component in itself.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given wording but uncertain because real-world events are ambiguous; mass concentrated at the boundary of the window.

stages.name: Schedule construction for marquee dates
stages.description: KXNBAXMASOPPONENT and KXNBAFIRSTOPPONENT settle on the announced schedule, which the league builds to satisfy national-TV partners: the Christmas slate (about five games) and opening-night/opening-week games are chosen for star power, market size, rivalries, a championship rematch and ring-ceremony home openers, subject to arena availability and travel constraints. The outcome is a selection from a small set of feasible pairings, largely decided before the release and often leaked days ahead.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice over feasible opponent pairings; strong persistence of marquee teams year to year; near-deterministic once leaks from tier-one reporters appear.

stages.name: Personal statements and overseas moves
stages.description: KXNBAAPOLOGY, KXNBARETIRE and KXNBATOJOINCBA are individual decisions rather than organisational pipelines. An apology after an on-court incident depends on league discipline (fine or suspension), public backlash and the player's history of public contrition, and must be public and topic-specific. A CBA signing depends on the player's NBA market (unsigned, minimum-contract offers only), health, CBA foreign-player slots and registration windows, and requires an official announcement or registration. Retirement depends on age, contract and health and must be effective before the next season.
stages.distribution: Low-rate hazards concentrated in short windows (days after an incident; the CBA signing period before its season; after a season ends for retirement); heavy dependence on individual signals.

talent_strength.note: No performance measure produces a transaction, announcement or schedule pairing directly; team and player quality enter only as incentives (trades, retirement) and as TV appeal inside the schedule selection model.

opponent_matchup.note: Christmas and first-opponent markets are pairings of two named teams chosen by the league; no on-court matchup is involved.

role_personnel.note: Decision-makers (owner, GM, coach, player) and their tenure or career stage.

availability_news.note: Reporter signals and injury-driven decisions.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach tactics do not produce any live off-court event; no coach-firing or coach-hiring series is filed here, and front-office state enters only through nba.org_stability as context for trades.

environment.note: Venue and weather do not drive league approvals, transactions or announcements; arena availability enters only as a constraint inside the schedule selection model and relocation is a governance decision, not an environmental effect.

game_context_script.note: These markets have no game script; the relevant timeline is the calendar and deal stage, which sit under situational and settlement categories.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities to scale; the equivalent is the number of live negotiations or candidate trades, folded into base rates in nba.offfield_base_rate.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of reports to events and of agreements to approvals.

distribution_variance.note: Rare-event base rates and clustered timing.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Calendar landmarks and team incentives.

officiating_rules.note: CBA and league governance rules as the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: All 16 series have rules text; stage required (processing, Source Agency confirmation, Board award, adoption, public statement, registration), window, multi-outcome rules and carve-outs coded per series.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Sixteen live series, all with recovered rules text; each resolves Yes only if a narrowly defined, officially confirmed act occurs inside a stated window. Families: (a) player transactions: KXNBATRADE (trade 'officially processed and approved by the Governing League' before the date; a later failed physical or rescission still resolves Yes), KXNBAPICKTRADE (any top-10 pick, or its draft rights before the drafted player signs, traded and officially processed before the window end), KXNBANEXTTEAM / KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF (mutually exclusive destinations with a 'Retires / No Team' outcome; staying under contract resolves the current team; a free-agent spell then signing anywhere, including the previous team, resolves that team), KXNBATEAMANNOUNCE (a Source Agency confirms the player is joining a named NBA team), KXNBANEXTCONTRACT (total reported value >= strike, counting options, incentives, void years and deferred money at nominal value; highest value if a range), KXNBATOJOINCBA (official CBA team announcement or CBA registration before 12:00 AM ET of the deadline); (b) personal acts: KXNBARETIRE (announcement effective immediately or before the next season), KXNBAAPOLOGY (public, topic-specific apology; conditional, sarcastic or private statements excluded); (c) league governance: KXNBACITYEXPAND (Board of Governors franchise award naming the city; preferred-bidder selection or conditional awards do not count), KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE (firm decision naming a confirmed inaugural season), KXNBARULE (formal adoption of the defined 'one free throw' rule), KXNBARELOCATION (relocation or official relocation announcement; announcing while still playing at the current arena next season still counts), KXNBAJOINCONF (public announcement or formal agreement to join a conference counts even if effective later); (d) schedule content: KXNBAXMASOPPONENT and KXNBAFIRSTOPPONENT (the announced schedule, from a Source Agency, pairs the two named teams on Dec 25 / in the team's first regular-season game).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official league processing/transaction records (trades), Board of Governors and league announcements (expansion, rules, Europe), team announcements (relocation, conference), CBA club/league registration, and Kalshi 'Source Agencies' (unnamed in the sampled texts) for schedules, contracts and joining announcements.
variants_and_edge_cases: Qualifying stage differs by series: official league processing (KXNBATRADE, KXNBAPICKTRADE), Source Agency confirmation (KXNBATEAMANNOUNCE, KXNBANEXTCONTRACT, schedule markets), official club/league registration (KXNBATOJOINCBA), Board of Governors award (KXNBACITYEXPAND), formal adoption (KXNBARULE), announcement (KXNBARETIRE, KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE, KXNBARELOCATION, KXNBAJOINCONF), public statement (KXNBAAPOLOGY).

Draft-night timing: KXNBAPICKTRADE needs official processing before the window end (Jun 25 in the sample); many draft-night deals involving salaried players are agreed then processed after the July moratorium, so agreed trades can fail the window.

Multi-outcome construction: KXNBANEXTTEAM / KXNBANEXTTEAMCONF are mutually exclusive with a 'Retires / No Team' outcome; remaining under contract resolves the current team; an extension while under contract does not trigger early resolution; re-signing after any free-agent spell resolves the previous team.

Contract size (KXNBANEXTCONTRACT) counts maximum nominal value with options, incentives and void years, extensions add remaining money, and the highest figure of a reported range is used, so reported headline values, not guaranteed money, settle it.

Relocation (KXNBARELOCATION) resolves to the announced city even if the team still plays at its current arena next season; conference realignment (KXNBAJOINCONF) resolves on announcement even if effective later.

Schedule markets settle on the announced pairing on Dec 25 (Christmas Eve excluded) or the team's first regular-season game; later schedule changes after announcement are not addressed by the text (u1).
Windows: most texts say 'after issuance and before' a date; Eastern Time is stated only for some (KXNBAEUROPEANNOUNCE, KXNBACITYEXPAND, KXNBATOJOINCBA).

summer_league_games.label: NBA Summer League game and season markets
summer_league_games.target: Summer League winner, spread, total and tournament outcomes
summer_league_games.mechanism: Summer League rosters are fluid with rookies, two-way and fringe players, minute plans and unusual pace, with little team-level history. Strength comes from who is playing (draft picks, returning rotation players), coach minutes plans, and league-specific scoring baselines. Variance is high and lines are less efficient, but information is hard to obtain and often arrives game-day.

inputs.why: Rosters, minutes plans and rookie usage.
Prior-season performance for returning rotation players.
Scratches and availability for NBA Summer League game and season markets.
League-specific pace baseline.
Residual sd in Summer League is large and different from the regular season.
Back-to-back and schedule density in Las Vegas.
Roster announcements and DNP plans.
Coach's minutes plan for NBA Summer League game and season markets.
Futures prices drift on news and with limited liquidity; the path shows staleness and information arrival.
Tiebreaker, play-in, cutoff and settlement-source wording defines the outcome.
Sportsbook futures prices give a de-vigged consensus for comparison.
Replaces the unavailable NBA impact rating with a measurable prior for the players who actually play.

Gives the structural distribution for the single largest Summer League uncertainty, whether the best player plays. Role lowered to secondary: the announcement half has no structured historical archive.
Captures effort/rotation incentives that vary within the Summer League week and have no analog in the regular season.
Provides correct variance and totals scale for spread and total contracts in a league with little history.
KXNBASUMMERMVP is the only rules-verified series in this archetype and had no input; the award depends on games played, production share and team advancement.
Prices KXNBASUMMER1HSPREAD, KXNBASUMMER1HTOTAL and KXNBASUMMER1HWINNER, which settle on first-half points only and whose margin is driven by the prospects who play first-half minutes.
Gives the qualification and knockout path that KXNBASUMMER settles on; the archetype otherwise had no input for the bracket or its margin-based tiebreak.

interactions.hypothesis: A team's strength depends on who plays minutes, not on franchise rating.
Summer League variance and totals are wider than regular-season; use league-specific residuals.
Rest announcements for key rookies shift game and player markets late.

Team strength is the minutes-weighted sum of player ratings, so the same rating matters more for a player with 28 expected minutes than one with 10; a top pick who is shut down removes both his rating and the minutes, producing a step in team strength rather than a gradual change.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team margin with and without the top-drafted player across past Summer Leagues, controlling for opponent.

interactions.hypothesis: Summer League totals are both higher-variance and higher-pace than regular-season; the variance of totals scales with possessions and with defensive looseness, so the sd of total and sd of margin move together with the format baseline.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate total and margin sd by event and format from past Summer League results and test heteroskedasticity versus pace.

interactions.hypothesis: A late announcement that a key rookie rests switches the team to a different regime (bench-heavy rotation, evaluation lineups); the market reaction depends on timing, and the same news before and after the order time has different value.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the move in team margin conditional on announcement timestamps relative to the prior price time.

interactions.hypothesis: Importance and schedule density jointly determine who rests: on the second game of a back-to-back with no seeding stakes, minutes shift to bench and prospects, whereas the same schedule in a must-win game keeps starters; the effect of rest depends on stakes.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress minutes of top prospects on back-to-back x importance indicator across past events.

interactions.hypothesis: A candidate's MVP chance is roughly P(keeps playing) times P(chosen | plays through), so a top pick with the best per-game production can be a poor MVP bet if his team plans a two-game appearance, while a second-year player on a contending roster gains; the shutdown hazard multiplies the whole award probability.
interactions.how_to_test: On past events compare MVP winners' games played with the field's top scorers per game; fit the award logit with and without expected games played.

interactions.hypothesis: When a team's top prospect is announced out, the first-half margin loses most of its roster-strength signal while the full-game margin changes less, because the second half was going to fringe players anyway; first-half contracts react more to participation news than game contracts.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare first-half and full-game margin residuals in games where a top-10 pick sat versus played, over five Summer League events.

nonlinearities.shape: bimodal/step: top prospects play full or not at all
nonlinearities.why: The impact of a top pick on team strength is not proportional to expected minutes because the distribution is bimodal; mean-minutes models understate the variance of team strength and the effect of announcements.

nonlinearities.shape: heavy-tailed star effect: team strength is dominated by one or two high-talent players
nonlinearities.why: Summer League rosters contain few players above NBA-rotation level and their share of usage is large, so team strength is convex in the top player's rating.

nonlinearities.shape: heteroskedastic: margin sd larger in blowout-prone mismatches and in loose-defense formats
nonlinearities.why: Summer League games have higher variance than regular-season games and variance grows with talent gaps, so the format baseline's margin sd must be heteroskedastic in the talent gap; normal approximations with a fixed sd misprice tails.

mechanism_review.summary: Summer League outcomes are produced by rosters and decisions rather than by franchise strength: who actually plays (rookies, two-way and G League players, returning bench players), how long each plays under coach evaluation plans, how good those players are on a common scale given thin or non-NBA data, and a game environment (format, pace, defensive intensity) that differs from the regular season. The outcome distribution has large variance because rotations are fluid, defense and execution are loose, and teams sometimes prioritize evaluation over winning; incentives change with the tournament state. Information is scarce and arrives game-day through announcements rather than structured injury reports, which makes timing as important as level for any model.

stages.name: Roster and participation decisions
stages.description: The first stage is who is on the floor: drafted rookies, two-way players, returning bench players on contracts, G League invitees. A top pick may play one game then be shut down, and veterans sit once their evaluation is done. Announcements arrive game-day through informal channels and are the main information.
stages.distribution: Discrete participation states with team-policy-driven probabilities; high-impact players have a bimodal minutes distribution (full or zero).

stages.name: Coach minutes plans and rotations
stages.description: Coaches use Summer League to evaluate players, so minutes are allocated to give looks to all players rather than to maximize winning; rookies often have caps and second-round or two-way players receive extended minutes. Rotation patterns are less stable than in the regular season and are set by program philosophy.
stages.distribution: Plan-driven minute vectors with random deviations; minutes variance within player is high and cross-team variation is structural.

stages.name: Team strength from translated talent
stages.description: A team's Summer League strength is the minutes-weighted sum of players' strengths on a common scale. With limited NBA data for most participants, ratings must be translated from college, G League and international performance and drafted position, with large uncertainty and no cohesion effect from shared practice.
stages.distribution: Sum of independent uncertain player ratings; strength uncertainty large (assumed prior sd of team rating of 5-8 points per 100 possessions, unsourced) and heavy-tailed because of star presence.

stages.name: Game environment: format, pace and variance
stages.description: The format (period length, overtime rules, foul limits) and talent mix produce a different scoring environment: more possessions per minute, weaker half-court defense and larger point-total variance. League-specific baselines are required, and event-level differences exist between sites.
stages.distribution: Margin and total distributions with larger sd than the regular season (margin sd assumed at about 14-16 per 40-48 minutes, an unsourced prior to be estimated); tie and overtime probabilities depend on format.

stages.name: Incentive state and schedule
stages.description: The tournament structure gives some games importance (seeding for the final) while others are for evaluation only, and schedule density in a short event affects rest decisions. The effect is on minutes and effort and varies across the week.
stages.distribution: State-dependent: effort and bench depth shift discretely between meaningful and meaningless games.

stages.name: Award selection for the event MVP
stages.description: The MVP contract is not a game outcome: the field of candidates is the handful of high-usage players who keep playing through the event, and the winner is usually on a team that reaches the final rounds. Shutdowns of top picks after a few games remove candidates abruptly, and voters weigh per-game scoring, draft status and team record; the choice is made from realised production, so each game day reshapes the field.
stages.distribution: Conditional choice over roughly 5-15 credible candidates with a long tail; probability mass concentrates fast after the first two game days and collapses for players who are shut down.

stages.name: Game and first-half margin and total distributions
stages.description: Game winner, spread and total and their first-half versions are read off one joint distribution of Summer League team points. The mean margin comes from translated roster strength weighted by who actually plays; the variance is far larger than in the NBA because of loose defense and fluid rotations. First halves are where drafted rookies and invited starters log most of their minutes, so the half margin tracks roster quality more closely, while second halves are handed to end-of-bench players and the margin regresses. The 1H winner adds an explicit tie outcome at integer margin zero.
stages.distribution: Approximately normal team-point totals with Summer-League-specific sd; margin pmf on integers with tie mass near 3-5% for halves; full-game margin wider and fat-tailed when one roster rests its prospects.

stages.name: Championship seeding and knockout path
stages.description: The champion contract is a path through the Las Vegas event: group-stage games produce a standings table in which ties are broken by tiebreakers including point differential, the top teams enter a single-elimination bracket and the rest play consolation games. Rosters thin as teams shut down prospects after qualification fails or after a few games, so a team's strength in the knockout is not its group-stage strength. Probability is the qualification probability times the knockout wins needed (two, semifinal and final, if the recent four-team knockout is kept; the 2026 format is unverified, see sl-format-facts), each close to a coin flip.
stages.distribution: Qualification is a discrete function of a four-game record plus margin tiebreak; title probability is a product of single-game win probabilities, heavily compressed toward 1/N by Summer League variance.

talent_strength.note: Translated player strength for those without NBA ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: With rosters assembled days before and few repeated opponents, matchup-specific scheme effects are not identifiable from Summer League history and add little beyond team strength and pace.

role_personnel.note: Minutes plans and who plays; the dominant signal.

availability_news.note: Game-day announcements and shutdown probabilities; no official report.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach evaluation philosophy and minutes policy.

environment.note: Arena conditions and the number of events (Las Vegas, California Classic, Utah) may matter through crowd and altitude (Salt Lake), but no input captures event-site effects and their size is unknown.

game_context_script.note: Importance state and format-specific scoring environment.

pace_volume.note: League-specific pace and possessions per game.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency regression for unfamiliar players is not addressed; the noise in efficiency of low-minutes rookies is large but no input models shrinkage to a talent prior beyond the translation prior.

distribution_variance.note: League-specific margin and total variance, plus the first-half share and tie mass for 1H contracts; the line-residual nba.score_resid is benchmark-only.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule density and tournament incentives.

officiating_rules.note: Format and rules differences (period lengths, overtime, foul limits) captured as league baselines; officials' tendencies unmeasured.

settlement_contract.note: All eight series have rules: 1H winner tie strike and two-week postponement; game, spread and total texts silent on overtime; champion via bracket; MVP award with no co-winner rule.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Eight Summer League series, all with sampled rules. Game level: KXNBASUMMERGAME (named team wins the game), KXNBASUMMERSPREAD (named team wins by more than X.5), KXNBASUMMERTOTAL (combined points above X.5), KXNBASUMMER1HSPREAD and KXNBASUMMER1HTOTAL (same forms on first-half points) and KXNBASUMMER1HWINNER (team scoring more points in the first half of regulation; equal points make all team strikes No and the Tie strike Yes; postponed games stay open until the rescheduled game ends within two weeks). Event level: KXNBASUMMER (named team wins the 2026 Summer League championship) and KXNBASUMMERMVP (named player wins the Summer League MVP award). Only the 1H winner text speaks to ties and postponement; the game, spread and total texts say nothing about overtime, ties, cancellation or the result source, and the MVP text names no voting body or co-winner rule.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official Summer League box scores and period scores (NBA.com) for game and first-half series, the tournament bracket for the champion and the league announcement for the MVP; the sampled texts name no source agency.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: the game, spread and total texts are silent; Summer League overtime formats differ from regulation NBA overtime, so whether and how OT points enter KXNBASUMMERTOTAL and KXNBASUMMERSPREAD is unverified, while first-half contracts are unaffected.
First-half winner has a Tie strike (team strikes resolve No on equal points); first-half spread and total use half-point strikes, so no push.

Multiple events exist (Las Vegas, California Classic, Salt Lake City) with different participating teams and formats; the sampled game contracts are dated Jul 19, 2026, during the Las Vegas event, which also hosts the championship.
Champion (KXNBASUMMER) depends on seeding rules (record, point-differential tiebreak) as well as team strength, and teams that miss the knockout play consolation games with weaker incentives.

MVP (KXNBASUMMERMVP): the award is decided around the championship game and usually goes to a high-usage player on a team that reaches the final rounds; a player shut down early cannot win, and the text gives no rule for co-MVPs.

player_escalator_payout.label: NBA scalar-payout escalator markets (points/threes)
player_escalator_payout.target: Expected payout of a single-game player stat under a convex payout schedule (e.g. points in 2-point bands, 0-10+ threes)
player_escalator_payout.mechanism: Scalar payouts require the full count distribution, not a single threshold probability; a convex schedule makes the upper tail dominate value. The distribution is a mixture over minutes scenarios with overdispersed attempts and make rates. Settlement tables are in rules_primary and differ by series. Value arises where the market schedule over- or under-weights extreme counts relative to a calibrated tail model.

inputs.why: Full count distribution including tail mass.
Scenario mixture drives the right tail.
Attempt volume for the threes escalator.
Shot share for the points escalator.
Shrink make rates for NBA scalar-payout escalator markets (points/threes).
Minutes loss in blowouts truncates tails.
FT points add to points bands.
Own/teammate status for NBA scalar-payout escalator markets (points/threes).
Possessions for NBA scalar-payout escalator markets (points/threes).
Futures prices drift on news and with limited liquidity; the path shows staleness and information arrival.
Tiebreaker, play-in, cutoff and settlement-source wording defines the outcome.
Win-total, seed and round-reach ladders must be coherent across thresholds.
A strong team's blowout wins cap minutes; a weak team's lead role raises usage.
A convex schedule shifts value into the upper tail, and the exact shape of g decides which probabilities matter.
The convex payout puts weight on heavy-minute games, so the probability of that regime is a primary driver.
Directly sets the upper-tail probability for 5+ threes or 35+ points under a convex payout.
A points escalator in 2-point bands is a lattice problem; parity affects band masses.

The escalator pays on the realised count, so an in-game exit truncates minutes and the lower bands, and the non-appearance branch may void or pay zero depending on the unseen rule; the hazard gives P(zero or truncated minutes) separately from injury status.
A missing creator or scorer raises a player's attempts and heavy-minutes probability, shifting the whole tail of a cubic payout.
Escalator points need a clean attempt volume by shot type; usage is an imperfect proxy.
Replaces the spread-based nba.garbage in player_escalator_payout: blowout truncation of the relevant players' minutes from own ratings and the coach's pull curve, with no closing line used.

interactions.hypothesis: The tail beyond 5 threes or 35 points depends on rare high-minutes high-variance outcomes; mixture modeling matters.
Tail probability is convex in both attempts and make rate; over-shrinking or under-shrinking changes expected payout materially.
The payout table must be parsed per series; convexity changes which part of the distribution drives the expected payout.

The top bands are reached when a heavy-minutes game coincides with hot shooting, and since both are rare, their joint probability determines the tail; the product of marginal tail probabilities underestimates it when close games also increase attempts.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate joint tail frequencies of (minutes >= 38, makes in top decile) and compare to the product.

interactions.hypothesis: The count of made threes is attempts times make rate, so the tail is convex in both; over-shrinking the make rate shrinks the tail multiplicatively while a high-attempt shooter's tail is more sensitive to the rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute tail probability sensitivity to shrinkage constant k for low versus high attempt shooters.

interactions.hypothesis: Under a convex payout, expected value is more than the payout at the mean (Jensen), so overdispersion raises value and an underestimate of variance understates it; the effect is larger the steeper the schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute E[g(K)] with the fitted pmf and with the same mean but lower variance, report the difference.

interactions.hypothesis: In a blowout the starter's minutes drop and the count falls to low bands; since the payout is convex, losing the upper tail costs more than the shift of the mean, and the effect appears beyond a expected margin threshold of about 10 points.
interactions.how_to_test: Stratify games by expected margin and compute realised mean payout versus the prediction using the mean only.

interactions.hypothesis: Free-throw trips add odd points that move outcomes between 2-point bands; for a player with high FTA the parity of the composite matters more than for a pure jump shooter, so the band mass is conditional on FT mix.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted band masses with and without parity modelling for high-FTA players.

nonlinearities.shape: Cubic payoff capped at 50 points or 10 threes
nonlinearities.why: A cubic schedule gives disproportionate weight to the right tail (a 7-three game pays $0.343 versus $0.027 for 3), so a small change in tail probability moves expected payout far more than a change in the mean, and the cap removes value beyond 50 points or 10 threes.

nonlinearities.shape: Overdispersion widens both tails
nonlinearities.why: Beta-binomial clustering raises the probability of 5+ makes beyond a binomial, an effect that grows with attempts.

nonlinearities.shape: Mixture with a heavy-minutes bump
nonlinearities.why: Counts in a 40-minute game are not a stretched version of a 32-minute game but a separate regime with higher attempts and fatigue effects, so the response to minutes is piecewise.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave shrinkage in the sample size
nonlinearities.why: Weight on a player's recent make rate grows slowly with attempts (about 0.3 at 100 attempts), so the tail is sensitive to small-sample extremes.

mechanism_review.summary: A scalar-payout contract pays a function g(K) of a single-game count K, so its value is the expectation of g over the whole distribution of K, and a convex g puts most of the expected value in the upper tail where data are scarce. The distribution is built from stages: whether and how long the player plays (a mixture of normal, truncated, extended and overtime games), how many attempts occur (for threes, attempts depend on role and spacing; for points, on usage and free-throw trips), and what fraction convert (a binomial with extra within-game dispersion because shooting is clustered, not independent). Then points are a composite 2 x FG2 + 3 x FG3 + FT, so a 2-point band is a statement about the sum with parity effects from free throws. The tail beyond the 90th percentile is generated by rare combinations: high minutes plus high attempts plus hot shooting, so the payout depends on the joint upper tail rather than on any single factor, and on shrinkage choices for make rates which change the tail non-linearly.

stages.name: Payout schedule operator
stages.description: The contract defines g(K) in its rules text: band edges, payout per band, a top band that may be open-ended, rounding and the treatment of non-appearance. The value of the contract is sum over K of P(K) g(K), so the schedule is a part of the model: a convex schedule up-weights the 95th-99th percentile outcomes, a capped schedule cuts the extreme tail and a floor schedule pays something for low counts. The two live schedules are cubic and capped: points pay (y/50)^3 with y = min(50, 2 x floor(s/2)), threes pay (min(10,s)/10)^3.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the text; the information content is in how g weights the pmf (convexity, cap, void rule).

stages.name: Playing time and extreme-minutes tail
stages.description: Minutes set the number of attempts, and the right tail of minutes (38 to 44 minutes in close games or overtime) generates the largest counts. The probability of heavy minutes depends on closeness of the expected game, bench quality, foul trouble and the coach's habit with stars; overtime adds five minutes with a probability near six percent. A truncated blowout night produces the low band and can be bounded by the payout floor.
stages.distribution: Right-tailed mixture with a heavy-minute component of 10-20% for stars and a point mass near the low band for blowouts.

stages.name: Attempt volume
stages.description: Attempts are the count of opportunities: three-point attempts depend on role (catch-and-shoot share), opponent concession of threes and team pace; field-goal attempts for the points escalator depend on usage and free-throw trips. Attempt counts are overdispersed with game-to-game sd roughly 30-40% of the mean, and they covary with minutes and with team scoring environment.
stages.distribution: Negative-binomial-like counts; attempts per minute vary by game script and by opposing scheme; correlation with minutes about 0.6-0.7.

stages.name: Make rate with within-game clustering
stages.description: Make probability per attempt is a skill parameter shrunk toward the player's long-run rate, but within a game makes cluster beyond a binomial because of shot quality sequences and defensive attention, so the count of makes is a beta-binomial with an intra-game correlation of about 0.02-0.05. Overdispersion widens both tails and increases the weight of high counts that a convex schedule rewards; shrinkage of the rate to the mean lowers the tail.
stages.distribution: Beta-binomial with rho about 0.03: variance increases about 15-30% beyond binomial for 10-attempt games (approximate, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED).

stages.name: Composite points parity and the joint tail
stages.description: For the points schedule the count is 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FTM, a composite whose parity and band mass depend on free throws and threes; the pmf over 2-point bands is not the same as that over single points. The expected payout is the sum over the composite pmf, and the upper tail needs the joint of minutes, attempts, make rate and free-throw trips, which is a copula problem rather than a product of marginals.
stages.distribution: Composite integer distribution with parity structure; upper tail from the joint of volume and luck.

talent_strength.note: Shooting skill (shrunk) and team strength as it affects the script.

opponent_matchup.note: Opponent concession of three-point attempts and defence profile.

role_personnel.note: Role determines volume and the chance of heavy minutes.

availability_news.note: Own and teammate status; also drives void rules.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme influences attempt allocation, but the information is in usage and three-point volume; a distinct coaching input would duplicate those and no specific scheme variable for scalar payouts is warranted.

environment.note: Altitude and venue have no credible direct effect on a single player's count beyond pace and rest, which are already in the volume and minutes drivers.

game_context_script.note: Blowouts and closeness set the minutes mixture.

pace_volume.note: Possession and attempt counts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Make rates and clustering.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, back-to-back and late-season incentives alter the chance of heavy minutes for stars, but no input in this archetype quantifies the schedule-driven change in the heavy-minutes tail.
