contract_review.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation both live escalator series are filed under this key, KXNBAESCALATORPTS and KXNBAESCALATOR3PT, each with sampled rules text. Both are scalar markets whose Yes payout is a cubic function of a single-game count: points use floor(10000 x (y / 50)^3) / 10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s / 2))) and threes use floor(10000 x (y / 10)^3) / 10000 with y = min(10, s); No pays 1 minus the Yes payout and a zero count pays Yes $0.00. The economic quantity is therefore E[g(K)] with g cubic and capped at 50 points or 10 threes, not a threshold probability. The treatment of a player who is inactive, never takes the court or exits early is not visible in the sampled text (the points rules_primary is truncated at 600 characters) and is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; a zero count paying Yes $0.00 suggests a non-appearance pays the lowest band, but that is an inference.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official box score points or made threes for the named player and game; the payout table and formula come from the contract text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Two live variants with different resolution: points settle on 2-point bands (y = 2 x floor(s/2), so 24 and 25 points pay the same, 50 or more points pay $1.00) and threes settle on single made threes with a payout of $1.00 at 10 or more.

Cubic payout: g = (y/cap)^3 puts most of the expected value in the upper tail (a 5-three game pays $0.125, a 7-three game $0.343), so the contract is far more sensitive to tail probability than to the mean.
Cap: the formulas cap y at 50 points and 10 threes, so extreme tails beyond the cap carry no extra payout and only P(K >= cap) matters there.

Non-appearance: the sampled text does not say how an inactive or never-on-court player is paid (a fair-price void as in the threshold ladders, or a zero count paying the lowest band, an opposite treatment); the points rules_primary is truncated at 600 characters.
Parity: 2-point points bands mean an odd free throw moves mass between adjacent bands only through the floor, so free-throw and three-point parity shifts the pmf over bands.

team_and_player_counting_specials.label: NBA playoff single-game scoring milestone (any player 50+ points in any playoff game; union over the playoff games)
contract_types: Any player scores 50+ points in a playoff game
team_and_player_counting_specials.target: Whether at least one player scores 50 or more points in at least one game of the playoffs (a union event over a random number of games and players).
team_and_player_counting_specials.mechanism: A player reaches 50+ points in at least one playoff game: the probability is a union over a random number of playoff games of a single-game upper-tail event, driven by the team's playoff path (games available), the star's availability and playoff minutes and usage, and the scoring tail against playoff defenses; cumulative points across games do not count.

inputs.why: Per-stat count distributions with overdispersion.
Minutes distribution is the common driver.
Usage drives scoring and assist components.
Possessions scale every component.
Opponent allowance by position.
Three-point attempts for make-one-three thresholds.
Shooting luck regresses: a hot start in 3P% or FG% inflates season-average thresholds and should be shrunk toward talent.
Availability and minutes restrictions.
Rotation patterns shape minutes.
Prices KXNBAPLAYERHIGHSCORE directly; the existing milestone-rate input addresses a different event.
Single-game ceiling and season averages for scorers depend on the minutes lost in lopsided games; the curve gives that loss without the price.

The team-simulation series in this archetype (six division winners, KXNBAWINSTREAK, KXNBALASTTOLOSE, KXNBAMATCHUP) start from a preseason strength prior; without it early-season probabilities are driven by a handful of games.
Team strength sets qualification and advancement, and therefore how many playoff games the player gets.
The settlement functional of KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS; without it per-game tails and the games count are never combined.
The named star must be healthy in each round he would play; his health also drives his team's advancement.
Series lengths per round give the number of games, the volume over which the 50-point tail compounds.
Advancement through the bracket sets how many rounds, and so how many games, the player gets.
Players on teams finishing 7-10 reach the playoffs only through the Play-In, whose games probably do not count for this contract.
Star minutes inflation in the playoffs widens the scoring tail that a 50-point game needs.
Player-specific exceedance rates relative to his mean give a second estimate of the far tail that the ceiling model extrapolates.
50-point games almost always come with 38+ minutes; this gives the weight of that regime in playoff games.
A series-long primary defender compresses the star's tail for four to seven correlated games.
Overtime adds about five minutes and a small extra chance of 50; market-free probability of a regulation tie.

interactions.hypothesis: Usage matters only with minutes; the product drives all components together.
Higher pace raises all components but correlates rebounds and assists with scoring, widening the joint tail.
Blowout probability cuts milestone completion for stars more than for role players.

The contract compounds a small per-game tail over a random number of games; for p near 1% the value is roughly p times expected games, so a contender's star with 18 expected games is worth several times an equal scorer on a first-round team.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised playoff 45+ and 50+ game incidence by player against per-game tail times games played, bucketed by team depth of run.

interactions.hypothesis: Advancement is conditional on the star's health and his games are conditional on advancement, so the joint probability of 'healthy and still playing in round three' exceeds the product of marginals for teams that depend on him and falls below it for deep teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate runs with and without coupling team strength to the star's health state and compare games-played distributions with historical star playoff games.

interactions.hypothesis: Playoff minutes inflation applies only in competitive games; in a lopsided series the star sits fourth quarters, so the heavy-minutes regime needed for 50 depends on the series strength gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress star playoff minutes on game margin and series seed gap over 15 seasons; compare 40+ minute frequency in close versus lopsided series.

interactions.hypothesis: When a co-star is out, usage jumps by several points and the 50-point tail thickens sharply; with both creators healthy the tail is thin, so the effect is a regime switch rather than a linear shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 40+ point game rates for stars in games with and without the second-highest-usage teammate over 5 seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: An elite primary defender assigned for a whole series lowers the scale of the tail for every game of that series, so the per-game tails are positively correlated within a series and the union is smaller than independent games imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare stars' playoff points tails by primary-defender quality bucket and test within-series correlation of residuals.

nonlinearities.shape: power-law (generalised Pareto) decay of exceedance in N
nonlinearities.why: Moving the strike from 45 to 50 cuts per-game probability by a factor of roughly two to four depending on the tail index, so small errors in the shape parameter move the price more than errors in mean points.

nonlinearities.shape: convex effect of usage on P(50+)
nonlinearities.why: A few points of extra usage add little to the mean but shift the far tail strongly because 50 points needs both volume and hot shooting; the response accelerates at high usage.

mechanism_review.summary: A single-game 50-point playoff performance needs three things at once: the player's team must be in the playoffs and keep playing (the number of games is set by qualification, Play-In and series advancement), the player must be on the floor for a full playoff workload, and one of those games must land deep in his scoring tail. Per-game P(50+) is a generalised-Pareto tail of points given minutes, usage, three-point volume and free-throw trips, pulled down in the playoffs by slower pace, tighter officiating and opponents who scheme a whole series against the star, and pushed up by longer star minutes and teammate absences that concentrate usage. The contract value is 1 - E[prod over games (1 - p_g)], with the games count and the star's health positively linked.

stages.name: Team playoff games available to the player
stages.description: The opportunity set is the number of playoff games the player's team plays: zero if it misses the playoffs or loses in the Play-In, four to seven per series, up to 28 for a finalist. It comes from the regular-season standings simulation, the Play-In bracket for seeds 7-10, and series-by-series advancement and length; deeper runs add the most games for the strongest teams, which also employ the most likely 50-point scorers.
stages.distribution: Lumpy on {0, 4..28}: point mass at zero for non-qualifiers, then sums of series lengths over rounds reached; right-skewed for contenders.

stages.name: Star availability through the playoff run
stages.description: The player has to be healthy for the games his team plays. A survival-type hazard of an availability-ending injury runs from the end of the regular season through each round, and a star playing through an injury carries a minutes restriction that removes him from the 50-point tail even when active. His health also moves his team's advancement, so games played and availability are positively dependent.
stages.distribution: Per-round probability of being healthy, decreasing over the run; bimodal per-game state (full workload versus out or restricted).

stages.name: Playoff minutes and usage regime
stages.description: Playoff rotations tighten to eight or nine players and stars gain two to four minutes, with 44+ minute nights in overtime or elimination games. Usage concentrates further when a co-star is out. Blowouts still truncate minutes, so lopsided series cut the tail. The relevant quantity is the probability of a heavy-minutes, high-usage game, not the average minutes.
stages.distribution: Minutes mixture with a heavy-minutes component (40+) whose weight rises in close and elimination games; usage shifts as a step when a teammate is absent.

stages.name: Single-game scoring tail against playoff defense
stages.description: Given a full workload, P(points >= 50) is the far tail of the per-game distribution: a generalised-Pareto exceedance over a high threshold fit on the player's history, raised by three-point volume and free-throw trips and lowered by the series opponent's primary defender, slower playoff pace and fewer fouls called. Single-game shooting is mostly luck, so the tail index must be shrunk to a league value; overtime adds a small extra chance.
stages.distribution: Heavy right tail: GPD above about 35 points with a shrunk shape parameter; per-game P(50+) typically 0.1-2% for the top scorers, near zero for others.

stages.name: Union over the run and settlement
stages.description: The contract pays if the maximum single-game score over the player's playoff games reaches N. With per-game probability p_g and a random number of games, P(YES) = 1 - E[prod (1 - p_g)], where the expectation runs jointly over team advancement, the player's health and a shared latent form factor that makes his per-game tails correlated within a run. No void applies, and Play-In and overtime treatment follow the open contract questions.
stages.distribution: Concave in the number of games; for small p roughly p x E[games played]; dependence through form and matchup makes the union smaller than the independent formula.

contract_review.settlement_definition: The only live series is KXNBAPLAYOFFPTS (NBA Playoffs Player Points): YES if the named player records at least N points (sample: Paolo Banchero, 50) in any single playoff game of the 2026 Pro Basketball Playoffs; points are not summed across games. It is a union over the player's playoff games, so a player whose team misses the playoffs, or who is eliminated or injured before reaching N, simply runs out of chances. The text states no fair-price void for an inactive or traded player, does not say whether Play-In games are playoff games or whether overtime points count, and names no source agency.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official playoff box scores (points per player per game); the sampled text names no source agency.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike: the sample uses 50 points (title '50+ points in a single game'); other players or editions may carry other N, and the per-game tail probability falls steeply with N.
Play-In: the text says 'any playoff game'; other NBA series exclude the Play-In explicitly, so a 50-point Play-In game probably does not count, but this is not stated here.
Overtime: not mentioned; official box-score points include overtime, which adds about five minutes for stars in roughly 6% of playoff games.
No void: unlike single-game player props, there is no fair-price settlement for an inactive player; an injured star loses games and the contract settles No if he never reaches N.
The sampled contract concerns the completed 2026 playoffs (status finalized); the mechanism applies unchanged to later editions, with the player list and strikes read per edition.

all_star_weekend_events.label: NBA All-Star Weekend events
all_star_weekend_events.target: Winner of an All-Star Weekend contest or exhibition game
all_star_weekend_events.mechanism: Each All-Star Weekend series settles on the winner of a one-off event: rosters and fields come from votes, drafts and invitations, and a withdrawn named player resolves No; performance is timed rack shooting, judged dunks, team shooting relays, or low-defence exhibition games that are either timed 12-minute round-robin games (point-differential tiebreak) or races to 40/25; the format turns performance into a champion and the MVP is chosen by a panel, almost always (by convention, not rule) from the champion's players. Inputs are scoped per series because the processes are disjoint.

inputs.why: Format parameters decide scoring scale, ties and the number of rounds, so they define what a win means in each series.
Simulated winner distribution over rounds, advancement and shoot-offs is the direct model of the 3-point contest.
Contest make rate is a catch-and-shoot skill without a defender; this input converts game stats to that setting.
The dunk series settles on panel scores, so judge behaviour and ties are the mechanism.
Dunk tier choice and make rate under attempt caps drive expected judged score.
Only pregame talent measure for contestants who rarely appear in season statistics.
Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters in an exhibition environment.
Exhibition margin variance and late effort set how much talent gap converts to a win.
Who plays and how many minutes in each game of the format changes the effective roster.
Contest fields change before the event, shifting every entrant's winning probability.
Selection, captains and participation determine who is on each roster and which events they enter.
Reserve selection and injury replacement set roster membership that feeds roster strength.
Player impact ratings feed the roster strength composite for both All-Star Game series (2026 round robin and 2025 four-team event).
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals and replacement players across all three events.
Announcements on field, captains, format and participation arrive as news before official lists.
All-Star Game only: three-point volume shapes roster offence in a high-3PA exhibition; not used for the contest.
Open-shot make probability by shot type is the best game-data proxy for rack shooting.
Hot-hand dispersion of makes inside a minute-long round sets contest score variance.
Free-throw skill is a low-noise proxy for shooting form in a defender-free setting.
Arena sightlines, backdrop and rim feel shift contest conversion for all entrants.
Format changes announced by the league alter scoring rules for the Game and contests.
Announcement timing of rosters, fields and format sets the as-of date for every input.
Rules fix withdrawal-to-No, the 70 s round, dunk rounds, the 12-minute round robin and 40/25 targets; two series have primary text only.
Official winner announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.
Location splits, deep-ball rate, rack placement and release tempo convert a shooter to the 70-second contest's scoring.
Round-robin and bracket simulation turns pairwise team gaps into champion probabilities, including the point-differential tiebreak.
Rising Stars and the 2025 game are races to 40/25, which a margin-per-minute model cannot represent.
Rising Stars teams of first/second-year and G League players need their own shrunk, cross-league strength rating.
Shooting Stars is a team shooting contest whose format is unverified; this input carries team skill and the format flag.
MVP is champion probability times the panel's choice among winning-team players.
Home-market or farewell narratives shift the MVP panel's choice among champion-team players.
Shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line that wins MVP.
Carries the 25% in-game fan vote that decides KXNBAALLSTARMVP alongside the media panel.

interactions.hypothesis: Small per-ball edges compound into only a modest winner probability because the max over about eight noisy round scores caps favourites.
Difficulty beats polish only when the panel's top-score compression is low; with lenient panels a clean easy dunk ties a hard one.
A real roster gap converts to wins less in a short high-variance game, so the same gap gives a lower win probability at 12-minute length than at 48.
Entrant injury status shifts both his own winning chance and the rest of the field through the replacement draw.
With nationality-built teams one side can be systematically stronger, and the point-differential tiebreak rewards a team that blows out the weakest team, not just wins.
MVP probability is roughly champion probability times within-team choice, so a star on a weak team is capped by his team's path.

Win probability is a max-of-noisy-scores function of per-ball make rates, so a shooter's gain from a few points of make probability is bigger when the field is thin at the top and shrinks as more strong shooters enter.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the field with and without the best entrant and compare the change in each remaining entrant's P(win); check against historical favourite hit rates by field strength spread.

interactions.hypothesis: Judged score saturates near the scale maximum, so extra difficulty adds little once a clean dunk already earns near-perfect marks, while a miss subtracts a lot; this reverses the naive hard-dunk advantage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dunk score on difficulty tier and make flag with a ceiling-aware ordinal model and compare the marginal effect of tier among clean dunks versus the miss penalty.

interactions.hypothesis: Win probability is the roster gap divided by margin SD, and the SD depends on format length and late effort, so the same gap gives a smaller edge in a shorter or more effort-compressed format.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute z = gap / SD for each past exhibition and test the win rate by z bucket and format length.

interactions.hypothesis: A withdrawal changes the winner probability differently depending on the number of finalists and rounds: with fewer rounds a replacement has a larger chance to win through variance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare historical outcomes for replacement entrants against the pre-event field ranking, split by number of rounds.

interactions.hypothesis: A star with a minor injury often plays a sharply reduced role or none, so impact on team strength is a threshold at the status level, not a gradual one.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate minutes by injury status tier in past exhibitions and test the roster composite with a status-tier discount versus a linear one.

interactions.hypothesis: In the 2026 round robin a team only needs margin when all three finish 1-1, so the value of a roster edge switches from win probability to expected point differential in that branch; a deep team that runs up the score on the weakest opponent gains disproportionately.
interactions.how_to_test: In the simulation compare champion probability under win-only versus margin-aware ranking, and check past round-robin exhibitions for margin-chasing in decided games.

interactions.hypothesis: A per-possession scoring edge converts concavely into win probability in a race to 25 because there are few possessions; the same Rising Stars roster edge yields a larger edge in the 40-point semifinal than in the 25-point final.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate fixed per-possession edges at targets 25 and 40 and compare with realised win rates of favoured sides in past target-score exhibitions.

interactions.hypothesis: MVP probability is the product of the player's team reaching and winning the championship and his conditional selection share, so a dominant individual scorer on an underdog team stays priced low while a moderate scorer on a heavy favourite rises.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test past All-Star MVPs: fraction from the winning team and the conditional-logit fit of selection share given team win.

interactions.hypothesis: The gain from placing the all-money rack at a shooter's best location depends on the ball values and whether deep bonus balls exist in that year's format; a large location split is worth more when money balls carry double value and less when deep balls dominate the maximum.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate expected round score with optimal versus average rack placement under each historical format vector and compare with announced placements and realised scores.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in P(win) near the top of the field, flat for low skill
nonlinearities.why: The winner is the maximum of several noisy scores, so top shooters gain disproportionally from higher make rates while low-skill entrants have almost no chance regardless of small skill changes.

nonlinearities.shape: Ceiling at the maximum score with heavy tie mass
nonlinearities.why: Scores are bounded and compressed at the top, so differences in dunk quality translate into almost no score difference above a threshold and the winner is then decided by ties and dunk-offs.

nonlinearities.shape: Regime-dependent: late variance compression in timed games only
nonlinearities.why: In timed 12-minute games defensive effort rises near the end, lowering final-minute margin variance; in target-score races there is no clock and the end is a first-passage threshold, so the same compression term must be zero there.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at the target with overshoot
nonlinearities.why: The game ends the moment a team reaches 25 or 40, so the probability of winning jumps discretely with a made three near the target and possession order matters more than average efficiency.

nonlinearities.shape: Multiplicative cap on Yes probability
nonlinearities.why: Because withdrawal resolves No, a named entrant's Yes probability is capped by P(participates), which falls sharply with an injury status change rather than linearly.

mechanism_review.summary: Seven series settle on the winner of a one-off All-Star Weekend event: two individual skills contests (3PT, dunk), a team shooting contest (Shooting Stars), three team exhibition tournaments (2026 All-Star round robin, 2025 four-team All-Star, Rising Stars bracket) and an award (All-Star MVP). The outcome is generated in layers: the league, voters and honorary coaches form fields and rosters; withdrawal resolves a named player's market to No; entrants produce performance (timed rack shooting, judged dunks, low-defence scoring in timed 12-minute games or untimed races to 40/25); the format converts performances to a champion through rounds, tiebreaks such as point differential, and finals; the MVP is then chosen by a panel, by convention (not by rule) almost always from the champion's players. Winners are maxima over noisy scores or short high-variance games, so favourites are capped and format parameters matter as much as skill. Regular-season counting-stat machinery is mostly irrelevant; each series uses its own scoped inputs (contract.series_input_scope).

stages.name: Field and roster formation
stages.description: Fields and rosters are produced by invitation (contests), fan/player/media votes and coach reserve picks (All-Star Game), nationality-based team assignment (2026 USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), honorary-coach drafts (Rising Stars, 2025 ASG teams), franchise teams (Shooting Stars) and commissioner injury replacements. Withdrawals and doubling up change the set until the day before. For 3PT, dunk and MVP a withdrawn named player resolves No, so participation probability multiplies every Yes price.
stages.distribution: Discrete set membership; withdrawal is a Bernoulli per entrant with correlated risk when an entrant also plays the Game.

stages.name: Contest skill: location-specific rack shooting, tempo and dunk repertoire
stages.description: In the 3PT contest each shooter has 70 seconds (rules) for racks at several locations with no defender; skill is per-location make probability, deep-range accuracy for bonus balls, choice of the all-money-ball rack location and release tempo, since unreleased balls score zero. In the dunk contest the analogue is the repertoire of difficulty tiers and conversion within attempts. Season box scores predict these only through open catch-and-shoot and location splits plus prior contest record.
stages.distribution: Per-ball Bernoulli with positive within-round correlation (beta-binomial); dunk make is Bernoulli by tier with a miss penalty, so scores are a bimodal mixture.

stages.name: Contest format aggregation: rounds, advancement, final reset and shoot-offs
stages.description: Round scores become a winner through the format: in the 3PT contest the top three of round one advance and the final-round score alone decides (rules), so round-one scores do not carry; in the dunk contest the top two of four advance and the two final dunks decide. Ties go to shoot-offs or dunk-offs that the rules do not describe. The maximum over noisy scores means the best shooter wins well under half the time.
stages.distribution: Discrete scores with ties; the winner is an extreme-value statistic over finalists, so upset probability is high and shoot-offs are not rare.

stages.name: Judging of dunks
stages.description: Judges score each dunk on a bounded scale, so a dunk's value is a function of difficulty, execution, creativity and crowd response, and scores compress near the top. The panel's composition (former players, celebrities), the sequence of contestants and the use of props all shift scores, and per the rules round-one combined scores only select the two finalists, after which the two final-round dunks alone decide the champion; dunk-offs on ties are not in the rules.
stages.distribution: Ordinal bounded scores with heavy ceiling mass; ties common; panel effects shared across all contestants.

stages.name: Exhibition team strength: All-Star and Rising Stars rosters, minutes and effort
stages.description: Each exhibition team's scoring edge comes from the offence, shooting and creation of players who actually play capped minutes under low defensive effort. All-Star teams are star rosters split by nationality (2026) or by draft (2025); Rising Stars teams are first/second-year players plus a G League team with noisy, cross-league ratings. Effort and variance depend on the regime: timed 12-minute games versus untimed races to a target, which must be estimated separately.
stages.distribution: Timed games: roughly normal margin with large SD per 12 minutes and late compression; target games: first-passage race with discrete 2/3-point jumps.

stages.name: Tournament path: 2026 round robin and target-score brackets
stages.description: Champion probability for KXNBAALLSTARGAME follows the quoted path: Game 1 USA Stars vs World, Game 2 USA Stripes vs the winner, Game 3 USA Stripes vs the loser, then a championship between the top two; a 1-1-1 tie goes to point differential, so blowout margins matter. KXNBARISINGSTARS and the 2025 KXNBAALLSTAR chain two races (semifinals to 40, final to 25), and in 2025 the Rising Stars winner entered the ASG bracket.
stages.distribution: Sequential multi-game path; champion distribution is a mixture over round-robin outcomes, with margin-sum tiebreak creating dependence between games.

stages.name: Shooting Stars team contest
stages.description: Franchise-named teams of shooters (recent editions mixed current players with retired or other-league shooters) score made shots from a sequence of locations against a clock; the higher team score wins. Kalshi's rules give only the team name and event date. The 2026 league format (verified) is four trios of two current players and one legend, seven spots in fixed order, a 70-second clock and two rounds with the top two advancing; the per-spot point values and the tie rule are not verified and still have to be read from the league's rules document.
stages.distribution: Sum over team members of correlated timed make processes; discrete scores with a winner over few teams and possible ties; format-dependent.

stages.name: All-Star MVP selection
stages.description: After the tournament a selection panel names the All-Star MVP, historically almost always a player from the winning team with the standout scoring line or a strong narrative such as a home-market star. P(MVP) is therefore the champion probability times the conditional choice among that team's players, driven by usage and minutes in short games; a withdrawn named player resolves No. 2026 check: the media panel votes right after the championship game and the fan vote counts 25% (Edwards won 10 of 14 panel votes); the award covered the whole three-game tournament, not the final alone, so popularity enters through the in-game fan vote (nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share), a separate ballot from the January starter vote.
stages.distribution: Categorical over roughly 8-12 players per champion team, highly concentrated on one or two players once the champion is known; heavy uncertainty pregame.

stages.name: Settlement
stages.description: Each series settles on the officially announced winner. Rules text confirms withdrawal-to-No for the player series, the 2026 round-robin structure with a 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak and championship game, and the Rising Stars 40/25 targets, but is silent on the next tiebreaker, overtime in tied 12-minute games, shoot-offs, dunk-offs, MVP co-winners and any format for Shooting Stars or the 2025 game.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official result; ambiguity mass sits in rare branches (later tiebreakers, ties, cancellation, renamed teams).

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seven series, one winner each. Player series (KXNBA3PTCONTEST, KXNBASLAMDUNK, KXNBAALLSTARMVP) settle Yes if the named player wins the stated year's event; a player who drops out, withdraws or does not participate resolves No (not void). Team series settle Yes if the named team wins: KXNBAALLSTARGAME = champion of the 2026 three-team mini-tournament of four 12-minute games: three round-robin games (Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1) and Game 4, a championship between the top two; point differential is the first tiebreaker only when all three teams finish 1-1; KXNBARISINGSTARS = winner of a four-team bracket with semifinals to 40 points and a final to 25; KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) and KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS have only a one-line primary rule, so their format, ties and non-participation handling are unstated. The 3PT contest has two rounds of 70-second shooting with three finalists; the dunk contest has four players, two judged dunks per round, two finalists, and only the finalists' two final-round dunks (combined) decide. No rule names a source of truth or treats shoot-offs, dunk-offs, tied championship games or MVP co-winners.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled rule; assumed to be the NBA's official announcement of each event's winner and of the All-Star MVP (NBA.com results/press release). Kalshi's own determination governs if it differs.
variants_and_edge_cases: Withdrawal: 3PT, dunk and MVP rules say a non-participating named player resolves No; the four team series contain no such clause, so a renamed or merged team is unhandled.
KXNBAALLSTARGAME 2026: point differential is the first tiebreaker only for a 1-1/1-1/1-1 round robin; the next tiebreaker and overtime in a tied 12-minute game are not in the text.

KXNBAALLSTAR 2025 versus KXNBAALLSTARGAME 2026: same contract type, different formats (2025 four drafted teams with target-score games from memory; 2026 timed round robin quoted), so history cannot be pooled without the format vector.
KXNBARISINGSTARS: semifinals end at 40, final at 25 (race formats, no clock); the event was 'originally scheduled' for a date, so postponement keeps the market alive; cancellation is unstated.
3PT contest: the final-round score decides; round-1 ties for third place and final-round ties (shoot-off) are not described in the rules.
Dunk contest: judging scale, number of judges, attempt limits and dunk-off on ties are not in the rules; only round structure is.
KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS: rules_secondary is empty, so team size, scoring, rounds and ties are all unverified.
MVP: no statement of whether the award covers the championship game or the whole tournament, how it is chosen, or co-MVP treatment.
Celebrity Game is no longer claimed: no live Kalshi series exists for it in the evidence pack.

series_cumulative_points.label: NBA playoff series cumulative team points (total and spread)
series_cumulative_points.target: Combined points or cumulative point differential of two teams summed over all games of a playoff series vs a strike
series_cumulative_points.mechanism: Both contracts sum per-game quantities over a best-of-seven series that stops when one team reaches four wins. The total is approximately series length times a playoff-adjusted per-game total, so its distribution has one mode per possible length (4-7 games) and rungs between modes largely price length. The differential sums game margins; margins also decide who wins each game, so the stopping rule couples them: lopsided series end quickly and accumulate a large differential in few games, while even series run long with margins that partly cancel. A shared matchup regime correlates games, mid-series injuries switch paths, close-out games and blowout truncation shape the decisive margin, and whether overtime counts is not stated in the rules.

interactions.hypothesis: Series total is length times per-game total, so sensitivity of a rung to the per-game total is highest near a length mode and lower, though not zero, between modes.
The stopping rule couples per-game margins and series length, so expected cumulative differential grows concavely with the rating gap.
A mid-series star absence switches the path regime, moving margins, win probability and series length together.
Playoff pace and whistle shifts apply to every game and add to the shared series factor, so they move the whole total distribution rather than averaging out.

Within the simulator the series total is about simulated length times per-game total (length drawn jointly, not from the separate DP pmf), so a 5-point shift in per-game total moves a 4-game sum by 20 and a 7-game sum by 35; a rung at a mode centre is highly sensitive to per-game total while a rung in a trough is less sensitive, by an amount that depends on the within-mode sd (about 40-65 points).
interactions.how_to_test: On historical series compare the realised total minus N times pre-series per-game expectation across N; compute the rung-probability derivative with respect to per-game total by rung position.

interactions.hypothesis: Margins decide game wins, so large positive margins for one side shorten the series; the cumulative differential and length are negatively dependent, and treating them as independent overstates the differential in lopsided matchups and understates its spread in even ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress cumulative differential on series length and pre-series rating gap in 2004+ series; compare simulator output with and without coupling of margin and winner.

interactions.hypothesis: Losing a star mid-series shifts every remaining game's margin by several points and the win probability with it; this can lengthen a series the injured team was winning or shorten one it was losing, moving total and differential at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare series in which a top-two player missed games after game 1 with matched series without, on realised length and differential relative to pre-series projection.

interactions.hypothesis: The decisive game's margin regime depends on series state: a team trailing 0-3 may concede late and lose big, while game-7 margins compress; because the decisive game always counts, this changes differential tails asymmetrically.
interactions.how_to_test: Margin mean and sd in close-out games by series state (3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3) versus non-close-out games, controlling for rating gap and venue.

interactions.hypothesis: Fewer possessions and fewer free throws per possession multiply into lower per-game points, and since both apply to every game they add to the series-level factor, shifting the whole total mixture down rather than averaging out across games.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose playoff total residuals into possessions and FTA per possession shifts by round; check whether the series random effect shrinks once both are included.

interactions.hypothesis: Large leads shrink once starters sit, so each game's contribution to a dominant team's differential saturates; combined with fewer games in lopsided series, the cumulative differential grows much slower than the rating gap at the top end.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot per-game realised margin against pre-game expected margin in playoff games and fit a saturating curve; compare simulated differential with linear versus saturated margins.

interactions.hypothesis: Once banked points approach the strike, the rung reduces to whether one more or two more games are played, so probability switches from a smooth tail to a length bet; when the banked sum already exceeds the strike the total is certain, a hard threshold in the remaining requirement K - B.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate rung probabilities after games 1-5 of historical series with and without conditioning on banked points; compare calibration for rungs whose remaining requirement K-B lies within one game total of zero.

nonlinearities.shape: soft staircase in the strike of the simulated P(total >= K): steep near length-mode centres, shallower but non-flat between modes
nonlinearities.why: Each extra game adds roughly a full game of points, so P(total >= K) falls in steps near 4x, 5x, 6x and 7x the per-game total; with single-game sd about 18-20, a positive shared factor and mean uncertainty multiplied by N, within-mode sd is roughly 40-65 points against a mode spacing of about 220, so troughs keep a sizeable fraction of peak density. The step sharpness depends on the fitted shared-factor size (u4).

nonlinearities.shape: concave expected differential in the per-game rating gap
nonlinearities.why: A larger rating gap increases each game's margin but shortens the series, so fewer margins are summed; expected cumulative differential rises sub-linearly and its variance falls as the gap grows.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete jump of one extra period of combined points
nonlinearities.why: An overtime game adds a five-minute period of points to one game's total, so rung probabilities near a mode edge jump with the market-free regulation-tie probability (P(OT)) if overtime is counted in cumulative points.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at K - banked total <= 0 (probability 1), steep within one game total of that point
nonlinearities.why: The total contract cannot go back once the running sum has crossed the strike, and just below it a single additional game decides, so response to the banked sum is a kink then a step in series length, not linear.

mechanism_review.summary: The outcome is a random sum over a random number of games. Per game, possessions (slower in the playoffs and matchup-specific) times points per possession (opponent-adjusted, lineup-dependent, partly shooting luck, plus a playoff whistle that cuts free throws) give each team's points; their sum is the game total and their difference the margin. The margin decides the game winner, and the series stops at four wins under a 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern, so the number of summed games is endogenous. For the total, length dominates: each game adds roughly a full game's combined points, so the distribution is a mixture with one mode per length and strikes between modes mainly price length. For the differential, the stopping rule couples margin size with length: a dominant team piles up margin but over fewer games, while a balanced series lasts longer with cancelling margins; the decisive game is always included and blowout truncation and close-out effort shape it. A shared matchup factor makes games correlated, in-series adjustments drift totals by game number, mid-series injuries switch the regime, and overtime adds a discrete jump if it counts.

stages.name: Series-start strength and availability paths
stages.description: Before game 1 each team's strength is the rating of the players who will actually play over the next two weeks, not the regular-season average. Rotations shorten and stars play more minutes; an injury report vintage fixes the next game's scenario, and a per-game health hazard spreads probability over availability paths for later games, where a star loss mid-series is the largest regime change for both margins and length.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over availability paths; each path has a nearly deterministic rating shift, so the mixture is lumpy rather than normal.

stages.name: Per-game possessions and efficiency in the playoff matchup
stages.description: Each game's points per team come from matchup pace (both tempo preferences, slowed by a round-specific playoff shift) times points per possession against this defence, including free throws under a playoff whistle that allows more contact. Venue alternates under 2-2-1-1-1, rest varies from one to three days, and coaches adjust coverages after each game, so totals tend to drift by game number.
stages.distribution: Game total roughly normal with sd near 18-20 points; per-team points slightly right-skewed by three-point variance and overtime.

stages.name: Per-game margin, win and truncation
stages.description: The margin of each game decides its winner and is what the spread contract sums. Its sd scales with pace and total; big leads shrink after starters are pulled, overtime games end within a few points, and close-out and elimination games have their own effort and blowout profile, with a bounce-back tendency for the team that lost the previous game.
stages.distribution: Margin roughly normal around the rating gap plus home edge, with compressed far tails from garbage time and a point mass of small margins from OT games.

stages.name: Stopping rule and series length
stages.description: Game winners accumulate until one side has four wins, so the count of summed games is 4 to 7 and depends on per-game win probabilities, home pattern and dependence between games. Length is the main volume of the total contract and sets how many margins enter the differential; the higher seed's extra home games in games 5 and 7 matter only in long paths. The length pmf is an output of the joint simulator (nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator), with nba.series_length_distribution kept as a cross-check.
stages.distribution: Discrete on {4,5,6,7}; game-to-game correlation and adjustments make sweeps and seven-game series both differ from an independent binomial.

stages.name: Aggregation into series total and cumulative differential
stages.description: The simulator sums game totals and margins along each path. Because a shared matchup factor persists across games, the sum's sd exceeds sqrt(N) times the single-game sd. The total becomes a mixture with modes near N times the per-game total; the differential is coupled to length through the stopping rule, so lopsided paths are short with large sums and even paths are long with cancelling margins.
stages.distribution: Total: mixture over N in {4..7} with modes about one per-game total (~215-225 points) apart and within-mode sd of roughly 40-65 points, so troughs between modes stay well above zero density; differential: sign follows the series winner, so it is bimodal (a lump on each side of 0) for near-even matchups and unimodal only for lopsided ones, with length-dependent variance.

stages.name: Settlement against the rung
stages.description: The running sums are compared to the strike at the series end: at-least K for the total, more-than S for the named team's differential. The total can be decided before the series ends once the sum crosses K. Rules state cumulative points throughout the series but not overtime treatment, incomplete-series handling or the source of truth, so those branches carry contract risk. Mid-series, the banked points of completed games (nba.series_banked_points_state) shift each strike and can decide the total before the series ends.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official scores; ambiguity is concentrated in OT inclusion near rungs and in rare incomplete-series branches.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Total: YES if the two teams 'collectively score at least' the strike (sampled strike 900) over the series; the sampled strike is an integer, so at-least K is exact with no tie. Spread: YES if the named team scores 'more than' the strike (sampled strike 9.5, floor_strike 9.5, strike_type greater_or_equal) more points than the opponent, summed as 'cumulative points scored throughout the series'; with integer game scores a half-point strike cannot tie, but only the 9.5 strike was observed so this is not verified for other strikes. Both sum every game actually played until the series ends. Rules do not state whether overtime points count (assumed included in official final scores), what happens if a game or the series is not completed, or the source of truth; these are open.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; assumed official NBA final box scores (NBA.com) summed over all series games, OT inclusion unconfirmed.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: neither series' rules mention overtime; official game scores include OT, but explicit inclusion is unverified and matters for rungs near a mode.
Early determination: a total of at-least K is decided as soon as the running sum crosses K, before the series ends; whether Kalshi settles early or waits for the series end is not stated.
Orientation: the spread is written for one named team; whether mirror markets for the other team or negative strikes exist is not visible from one sample.
Only Finals series were sampled (NYK vs SAS 2026); earlier-round series may use different strikes, team naming or wording.
Incomplete series (cancelled or forfeited game, suspended play) has no stated treatment.
